stories.title: UP announces polls for 10 Rajya Sabha seats:Voting on October 16; 11 teacher MLC seats to vote on October 23
stories.summary: Elections have been announced for 10 Rajya Sabha seats and 11 teacher MLC seats in Uttar Pradesh. Voting for the Rajya Sabha seats will be held on 16 October, while voting for the MLC seats will take place on 23 October. Of the 10 Rajya Sabha seats, eight are held by the BJP, while the Samajwadi Party and the Bahujan Samaj Party hold one seat each. The BJP members include former DGP Brijlal, Seema Dwivedi, Neeraj Shekhar, Geeta Shakya, Hardeep Singh Puri, Arun Singh and BL Verma. Dr. Dinesh Sharma's term was also due to continue until 25 November, but he resigned from the post after being appointed Lieutenant Governor of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. Therefore, an election will also be held for that one seat. In addition, the terms of Samajwadi Party national general secretary Ram Gopal Yadav and Bahujan Samaj Party's Ramji Gautam are also ending around the same time. Who could lose out and who could get a chance in BJP for the Rajya Sabha election? 1. Dr Dinesh Sharma: Dr. Dinesh Sharma was appointed Lieutenant Governor of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands on 5th September. Therefore, the BJP will have to choose a new face in his place. 2. Hardeep Singh Puri: The Modi Cabinet could be expanded anytime in September or October. If Puri remains a minister, he could return to the Rajya Sabha from UP for a third consecutive term. If he is dropped from the Cabinet, the party could send a new face instead. 3. Arun Singh: Arun Singh was sent to the Rajya Sabha in 2020 when he was the BJP’s national general secretary. He is the brother-in-law of Defence Minister Rajnath Singh. If Rajnath Singh backs him, Arun Singh could get another term; otherwise, the party may choose a new face. 4. BL Verma: Union Minister of State BL Verma is expected to be sent to the Rajya Sabha again. After the death of former Chief Minister Kalyan Singh, the BJP has been promoting Verma as its new Lodh community face. He is also considered close to the BJP’s central leadership, Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah. 5. Brijlal: Former UP DGP and Rajya Sabha MP Brijlal was sent to the Upper House under the SC quota. He is now 71. Some party leaders believe the BJP could replace him with a new Dalit face. 6. Geeta Shakya: Rajya Sabha MP Geeta Shakya is also a BJP state general secretary. The party had given her the Rajya Sabha seat to strengthen its outreach among the Shakya community. She has the support of several senior leaders, including organisational general secretary Dharampal Singh and Deputy CM Keshav Prasad Maurya. Political observers therefore believe she could get another term. 7. Seema Dwivedi: Seema Dwivedi has been active in Jaunpur recently but is also reportedly at odds with Badlapur BJP MLA Ramesh Mishra and other leaders. One section of the party wants her to get another Rajya Sabha term, while another believes her nomination did not benefit the BJP in Jaunpur or eastern UP. This section favours an OBC or Brahmin woman instead. 8. Neeraj Shekhar: Former PM Chandrashekhar’s son Neeraj Shekhar joined the BJP after leaving the Samajwadi Party in 2019. The BJP sent him to the Rajya Sabha in 2020. He contested the 2024 Lok Sabha election from Ballia but lost. The decision on whether he will return to the Rajya Sabha will depend on the BJP leadership. Now, about the SP and BSP… SP: Only one SP Rajya Sabha seat is falling vacant, while the party’s current strength could give it two seats. This would mean a net gain of one seat. SP national general secretary Ram Gopal Yadav is among the party’s key decision-makers, so the report says he is likely to get the Rajya Sabha ticket. BSP: Ramjilal Gautam is considered close to BSP chief Mayawati. The report says Gautam’s role was linked to Mayawati’s decision to expel her nephew Akash Anand’s father-in-law from the party. If the BSP and BJP reach an understanding in the Rajya Sabha election, Gautam could get another term. If not, the BSP could be left without any MP or MLA in the country, according to the report. Understand the Rajya Sabha seat calculation Rajya Sabha seats are allocated based on the strength of MLAs. A party or alliance with more MLAs can elect more candidates. In UP, the formula given for the required votes for one Rajya Sabha seat is: Total MLAs ÷ (Vacant seats + 1) + 1 With 397 MLAs and 10 Rajya Sabha seats falling vacant: 397 ÷ 11 + 1 = 37.09 So, a candidate would need 38 votes to secure a seat, based on this calculation. stories.title: Bride found dead on bed, groom hanging on wedding night:She was in bridal attire; couple married at temple day before
stories.summary: The bride and groom died on their wedding night in Siddharthnagar. The wife's body was lying on the room floor in her red wedding outfit, while the husband's body was found hanging from the wife's sari. Police suspect that the couple had an argument over something during the night. The husband then allegedly killed his wife before taking his own life. When the daughter-in-law had not woken up by 7 a.m. on Wednesday, her mother-in-law went to wake her. The couple did not respond when she called out from outside. When she knocked, the door opened. Their bodies were lying inside. The sight made the mother-in-law scream. Hearing her cries, family members arrived and took the groom's body down from the noose. On 21 September, Deshraj and Anita got married at a temple. The wedding feast was held yesterday. People danced to a DJ's music until 11 p.m. The bride and groom then went to sleep. The entire incident falls under the jurisdiction of Kotwali police station. Wedding was scheduled for May 2027, but the girl suddenly came home Deshraj Chauhan was from Janiyajot village, while Anita was from Karjaha village. Their homes are about 15 km apart. Their families had fixed their marriage three months ago, with the wedding scheduled for May 2027. They got engaged in July. Deshraj then went to Delhi, where he worked at a pani puri stall. The two remained in touch over the phone. About 15 days ago, Deshraj returned home from Delhi. Around the same time, Anita also went to his house. Their families then decided to get them married. Couple went to sleep at 11 pm; bodies found at 7 am On 21st September, the couple got married at Tekdhar Baba Temple in Bansi at around 2 pm. Their families blessed them, after which Deshraj brought Anita home. A wedding feast for relatives and neighbours continued until 11 pm. The family then went to sleep, and Deshraj and Anita went to their room. Deshraj’s father, Mukesh, said his sister Meenakshi went to wake Anita at around 7 am on Tuesday. A short while later, she heard her screaming. When the family rushed in, they found Deshraj and Anita dead. The family said they do not know what happened during the night. Groom’s family lives in a two-storey house Deshraj’s parents are Mukesh Chauhan and Mamta. Mukesh sells vegetables in Delhi but has been staying at home for the past few days. Deshraj had a younger brother, Arun, and a younger sister, Kucchi. The family lives in a two-storey house. Anita’s father, Panchram, is a farmer. CO Shivendu Singh said; “The bodies of the husband and wife were found after their wedding. It would be premature to say anything at this stage. The matter is being investigated. The bodies have been sent for post-mortem. The exact circumstances will become clear after the report.”

stories.title: 3,013-page chargesheet in 9 cases against Mahfooz Alam:₹1,600 crore found across 68 accounts in 12 Kanpur banks; 60 witnesses named
stories.summary: Chakeri and Jajmau police in Kanpur have filed chargesheets in all cases against Mahfooz Alam alias Pappu Chhuri in connection with illegal transactions worth crores. A chargesheet running to more than 3,000 pages has been filed in the 9 cases against Pappu Chhuri. Police have accused him of illegal transactions worth more than ₹750 crore. Pappu Chhuri's son Faiz and other associates have also been named as accused in the chargesheet. Investigation reveals illegal transactions worth ₹773 crore Police had received information about illegal transactions worth around ₹1,600 crore through 68 accounts in 12 banks linked to Mahfooz Alam, alias Pappu Chhuri, of Jajmau Colony. The names of Pappu Chhuri, his son Faiz, and several others had emerged in the case. After they were sent to jail, people who had fallen victim to the fraud began coming forward. Based on their complaints, 5 cases were registered at Chakeri police station and four at Jajmau police station. When the investigation began, illegal transactions worth ₹773 crore were uncovered against Mahfooz. Police have filed a 3,013-page charge sheet in all nine cases. Mahfooz is accused of luring his acquaintances, relatives and poor people into schemes by deceiving them, opening accounts in their names and getting fake firms registered for GST. He brought money into the accounts in the names of these fake firms and operated the accounts himself, carrying out illegal transactions worth crores of rupees. The details of bogus firms opened in the name of tanneries, scrap businesses and slaughterhouses, mule accounts opened with banks, transaction details, statements from bank employees, physical verification reports of the firms, tenancy agreements and electronic evidence have been used as the basis for the charge sheet. More than 60 people have been made witnesses in these cases. Mahfooz arrested on 12 June, son on 30 June Police arrested Mahfooz Alam in Chakeri on 12 June and sent him to jail, while his son Faiz was arrested from the PWD Colony in Aliganj, Lucknow, on 30 June and sent to jail. After the case involving illegal transactions worth crores of rupees came to light, Police Commissioner Raghubir Lal referred it to the Enforcement Directorate (ED). The ED has also started its investigation into the case. The charge sheet and other details have also been sent to the ED. Accounts found in these banks Fourteen accounts were found in HDFC, five in RBL, five in IndusInd Bank, six in Kotak Mahindra, four in Union Bank, three in Axis, four in Bandhan, two in ICICI Bank, seven in City Union Bank, two in BoB, and one in Bank of India. Mahfooz operated them.

stories.title: ‘Witness appeared in court 28 times, yet no justice’:Apple manager’s wife says evidence was ignored; will approach HC, seek CM’s help
stories.summary: Vivek Tiwari's family is dissatisfied with the court's verdict in the high-profile Lucknow Apple manager murder case. His wife, Kalpana Tiwari, said she had gone to court for every hearing for 8-years in the hope of getting justice, but the verdict did not go in their favour. She said Sana Khan, the eyewitness to the incident, appeared in court 28 times and recorded her testimony in around 70 pages. Despite this, the court did not accept the key statements and evidence presented by the family. Kalpana Tiwari said the family would now approach the High Court's Lucknow Bench. She would also appeal to Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath over the entire case. Kalpana said: This is why we did not go to court on 21 September Kalpana Tiwari said she had made it clear on 17 September itself that the family was not satisfied with the conviction verdict. No family member went to court when the sentence was pronounced on 21 September. She said they would now take legal recourse to seek a review of the verdict and file a petition in the High Court. Former DGC said eyewitness testimony was crucial Former DGC (Criminal) Manoj Tripathi, who had represented the case, told Dainik Bhaskar that eight witnesses appeared in court. They included the investigating officer, members of the forensic team, and members of the team that recreated the scene of the incident. According to him, Sana Khan was the case's main eyewitness and appeared in court 28 times. Manoj Tripathi claimed that Sana had stated in her testimony that, in front of her, the constable shot Vivek and she kept screaming for help. According to him, the evidence presented by the defence and the prosecution was debated during the judicial process, but the family believes that crucial evidence was not given sufficient importance. Family's testimony and forensic report also cited The former DGC said that Vivek's wife, Kalpana Tiwari, and other family members had also testified in court. In addition, the statements of officials linked to the forensic and magistrate's inquiries were recorded. He said an appeal against the verdict would now be filed in the High Court. Case reached sentencing after 2,914 days In the Vivek Tiwari murder case, which took place on 29 September 2018, the sentence was pronounced on 21 September. A total of 2,914 days, or around 7 years, 11 months and 23 days, passed between the incident and the verdict. On 17 September, the court convicted Prashant Chaudhary of culpable homicide not amounting to murder, while acquitting Sandeep Kumar. On 21 September, Prashant was sentenced to 10 years' rigorous imprisonment. Read what happened on the night of the incident... Late on 29 September 2018, Vivek Tiwari was returning by car with a female colleague. In the Makdoompur area of Gomtinagar Extension, police personnel riding motorcycles attempted to stop his car. According to the police, the car did not stop, and a collision appeared imminent, following which Prashant Chaudhary opened fire. Vivek was taken to the hospital after being shot, where he died.

stories.title: Mother-daughter killed by hammer blows to head in Etah:Eyes gouged out; husband, father-in-law accused, both absconding
stories.summary: A double murder took place in Etah, where a mother and daughter were allegedly killed by smashing their heads with a hammer. Their faces and eyes were also mutilated. The victims’ husband and father-in-law have been accused in the case and have been absconding since the incident. The incident triggered a police response, with SSP Dr. Ila Maran reaching the spot. Dog squad, forensic, field unit and SOG teams were called in to investigate. Police have sent both bodies for post-mortem and are conducting raids to trace the accused. The victims have been identified as Kamla Devi, 65, and her daughter Priyanka, 35. The incident took place around 12:30 am on Monday in the Awagarh police station area. Now understand the full case Rukumpal (43), son of Siyaram, lives in Yadav Nagar and is originally from Thathi Gadanpur in Firozabad. He is the fourth of six brothers and has been living with his family in Yadav Nagar, Awagarh, for the past five years. Rukumpal works in farming. His family includes his wife Priyanka and their four children: Himanshu (22), Kalpana (18), Rahul (13) and Sapna (10). Daughter recounts the incident Priyanka’s daughter Kalpana said her parents had an argument on Monday morning. Her father then went to the city for some work. When he returned at night, the couple argued again. Later, Priyanka and her mother slept on a cot near the house gate, while the four children slept inside a room. Around midnight, the children suddenly heard a commotion. Kalpana said that when they came outside, they saw their father and grandfather assaulting their mother and grandmother. Another man from the village was also with them. She said her father was carrying a hammer, while her grandfather had another iron weapon. The children were frightened after seeing this. Son ran to police station and reported the incident Kalpana said her younger sister fainted after seeing their mother and grandmother being attacked. While she tried to help her sister, everyone involved fled the house. When the siblings reached the spot, they found their mother and grandmother dead. After seeing this, her younger brother Rahul ran nearly 3 km to the police station and told the police what had happened. Police then reached their house. Kalpana said her mother was her grandmother’s only daughter, which is why they had been living with her. Their grandfather had died several years ago. Her elder brother works outside the area. Brother said Rukumpal suspected his wife’s character Rukumpal’s elder brother Prempal reached Etah from Firozabad after learning about the incident. He said his brother had been having frequent disputes with his wife for a long time. He had reportedly suspected her character, which was allegedly the reason for their repeated arguments. Prempal said their father lived with the family and had come to stay with Rukumpal just two days before the incident. ASP Shwetabh Pandey said; “A mother and daughter were murdered in an outer area of the Awagarh police station limits. A dispute between the husband and wife has come to light. The children have told us about the entire incident. The accused are being traced.”

stories.title: Gorakhpur Municipal Commissioner unhappy over tax collection:Says ‘No house should be left untaxed’; action if target not met
stories.summary: Gorakhpur Municipal Commissioner Ajay Jain expressed displeasure over the low property tax collection during a review of property tax recovery by the Gorakhpur Municipal Corporation. Information presented at the review meeting held on Monday showed that, against the 40% target set by the government for September, collection stood at only 34% in Zone 2, 21% in Zone 3 and 38% in Zone 4. The Municipal Commissioner directed the concerned zonal officers to increase collection in line with the target. Municipal Commissioner Ajay Jain said clearly that action would be taken if the target was not achieved. No building should be left out of tax assessment The Municipal Commissioner directed all zonal officers and tax superintendents to ensure that no building in their areas remained outside the property tax net. Buildings that have not yet been assessed for tax are to be identified and action taken against them. Instructions were also issued to ensure that pending objections related to property tax are resolved at the competent level within one week. Camps to be organised in wards for OTS The one-time settlement scheme (OTS) implemented by the government was also reviewed. The Municipal Commissioner directed all zonal officers and tax superintendents to co-ordinate with councillors and organise camps in their respective areas. They were instructed to encourage as many people as possible to submit applications under the OTS through the camps and recover the outstanding tax. He also directed officials to pay special attention to major defaulters. Along with serving major defaulters notices related to the OTS, officials were instructed to contact them personally and take action to ensure payment of the outstanding property tax. Departmental action if targets are not met The Municipal Commissioner also directed revenue inspectors and recovery officials to collect revenue in line with their assigned targets. He made it clear that departmental action would be taken against the employees concerned if the recovery was not satisfactory compared with the targets. Show-cause notice issued to tax inspector During the meeting, the Municipal Commissioner sought information from Santosh Kumar Singh, Tax Inspector Grade 2 of Zone 4, regarding OTS. Dissatisfied with his response, the Municipal Commissioner directed that a show-cause notice be issued.

stories.title: Varanasi Police to crack down on cybercrime network:CP seeks reports from police stations in 15 days; 277 members of 58 gangs arrested
stories.summary: Police in Varanasi will now take stricter action against cyber criminals arrested during investigations and operations. The cybercrime team will also change its approach to dismantle their networks. Arresting cyber criminals will not be considered the end of a case once they are sent to jail. In the second phase, police will target their associates and other members of their networks. In the third phase, action will be taken against their properties and other sources of income. Police will identify the entire network, including those opening mule accounts, selling fake SIM cards, running fake call centres and withdrawing fraud proceeds from ATMs. Action will also be taken under the Gangsters Act. Police Commissioner Mohit Agarwal has directed officers to adopt this approach towards identified cyber criminals in the district. The cyber team presented a blueprint, after which the CP issued further directions based on some suggestions. The CP has also instructed cybercrime officers in all three zones to review pending cases every 15 days and submit progress reports. They have been directed to monitor identified local criminals and trace their phone numbers. 58 gangs busted, 277 cyber fraudsters arrested The Cyber Crime team presented its report card, highlighting the Commissionerate Police's achievements over the past year. It said that during this period, the Cyber Crime Police busted 58 cybercrime gangs, arrested 277 cybercriminals and sent them to jail. In five major digital arrest cases, 36 criminals were arrested, and ₹1.20 crore, cars, and electronic devices were recovered from them. In a major crackdown on illegal call centres, 15 call centres were busted, and 175 people were arrested. The gangs were involved in investment fraud, cheating foreign nationals and defrauding people on the pretext of offering jobs. Acting swiftly on cyber complaints, 16,982 NCRP complaints were resolved. ₹25 crore put on hold, ₹4.5 crore returned The cyber team said ₹25 crore in fraud proceeds was put on hold as part of financial action. After the process was completed, ₹4.5 crore was returned to the victims. A total of 10,176 mobile numbers and 8,262 IMEI numbers used in cybercrime were blocked. The Gangster Act was invoked against 21 hardened criminals. A total of 550 people trapped in fraudsters' network were rescued and safely handed over to their families, while 17 four-wheelers were recovered. The CP said that under the awareness campaign, more than 25,000 people had been told about ways to protect themselves from cyber fraud at schools, colleges and crossroads. DCP Crime Neetu, DCP Rajesh Kumar Pandey, ADCP Crime Nripendra, along with cyber in-charges and cyber nodal officers from all zones, were present at the cybercrime meeting.

stories.title: UP transfers 34 IAS officers, 14 DMs changed:Mangla Prasad, who demolished Mukhtar’s stronghold, sidelined; Mahendra Singh Tanwar made Kanpur DM
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh government transferred 34 IAS officers late Monday night, including district magistrates of 14 districts such as Moradabad, Kushinagar and Kanpur Nagar. Five of the transferred IAS officers have been given another district posting, while nine district magistrates have been shifted to government departments or other assignments. New DMs appointed ahead of Assembly elections The government has appointed new district magistrates in the affected districts. The reshuffle is being linked to preparations for the upcoming Assembly elections, with the newly appointed DMs expected to oversee the election process in their respective districts. Rajendra Pensia moved after four-and-a-half months in Moradabad Dr Rajendra Pensia, who served as Moradabad district magistrate for around four and a half months, has been appointed Special Secretary in the Prisons Administration and Reform Department. Mangla Prasad Singh moved to Cooperative Sugar Mills Federation IAS officer Mangla Prasad Singh, who was serving as Ballia district magistrate, has been appointed Managing Director of the Uttar Pradesh Cooperative Sugar Mills Federation. Singh had earlier been associated with the demolition of properties linked to gangster Mukhtar Ansari. See the list of districts whose DMs were transferred earlier... Now see the list of transfers of 20 more IAS officers... These District Magistrates Have Been Removed CM Yogi was unhappy with their working style According to sources, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath and senior government officials were not satisfied with the working style of these district magistrates. It was believed that leaving these officers in charge during the Assembly elections could harm the party and the government. This is why district magistrates have been transferred on a large scale. Now, learn about the IAS officer in the news... Rajendra Painsia removed after four and a half months District Magistrate Rajendra Painsia, who came into the spotlight over the Sambhal mosque case, was considered close to the government. Painsia served as Sambhal's District Magistrate for around 23 months. He was transferred to the post of Moradabad District Magistrate on 5 May. However, he was removed from Moradabad after just four months and 15 days. He has also been appointed Special Secretary in the Prisons Department, which is considered a sidelined department in the government. These five IAS officers have been given district postings again These nine officers have received field postings Jasjit Kaur appointed MD of UP Electronics Corporation Jasjit Kaur has been removed as Bijnor district magistrate and appointed managing director of the Uttar Pradesh Electronics Corporation. While she was serving as Bijnor DM, the Lucknow Bench of the Allahabad High Court had issued a bailable warrant against her. The matter was related to her failure to decide on a caste-related application despite a court order. Jasjit Kaur is a 2012-batch IAS officer of the Uttar Pradesh cadre. She has previously served as the district magistrate of Shamli and Sultanpur. She has also served as additional commissioner in Meerut. After five years, Bhatia's departure from YEIDA Shailendra Bhatia, ACEO of the Yamuna Expressway Industrial Development Authority (YEIDA), has left YEIDA after nearly five years. Bhatia was posted to YEIDA as a PCS officer. He served as OSD at YEIDA from June 2024 to December 2025, after which he was given the responsibility of ACEO. He has now been appointed chief executive officer (CEO) of the Uttar Pradesh Expressways Industrial Development Authority (UPEIDA). He will be responsible for implementing around six new expressway projects. Tenders worth more than ₹50,000 crore related to these projects will also be under his supervision. Saharanpur ADM becomes Mirzapur CDO Gyanendra Singh becomes Ballia's new DM; had been in the news for fuel conservation campaign Gyanendra Singh has been removed as the District Magistrate of Pilibhit and appointed the new District Magistrate of Ballia. Singh came into the spotlight while serving as Pilibhit's DM for his campaign to conserve fuel. Appeals were being made to save fuel amid tensions between Iran, Israel and the United States. He also took the initiative during this period. He first had the escort vehicle assigned to his security removed. He also directed officials living in the Officers' Colony to walk to the Collectorate. This step was taken after Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath appealed to people to conserve fuel.

stories.title: Atiq’s son says complainant visited him several times:‘We have family ties; how could I demand extortion from jail?’
stories.summary: Ali Ahmed, the second son of gangster-turned-politician Atiq Ahmed, denied all allegations against him in a case registered against five people at Kareli police station in 2023. He claimed the FIR was registered under administrative pressure based on a fabricated story. Ali was produced before a Prayagraj court on Monday, September 21, to record his statement in the case. During the hearing, ADJ Court 16 Judge Shailendra Mani Tripathi questioned him about the FIR, police allegations and chargesheet. The questioning continued for around an hour. Ali says he was in Naini Central Jail when incident took place Responding to the allegations, Ali said he had nothing to do with the incident and was lodged in the high-security barrack of Naini Central Jail at the time. He claimed that Afzal, who filed the FIR, has family ties with his family and had also visited him several times in jail. ‘I neither assaulted anyone nor threatened anyone’ Ali said he had no knowledge of the land mentioned in the case and denied assaulting or threatening anyone. He stated, “I have no knowledge of any such land. I neither assaulted anyone nor issued any threats. Demanding extortion money from jail is out of the question.” Ali further claimed that the case was filed at a time when several cases were being registered against his family as part of a conspiracy. He also said he did not know the two people who were made witnesses in the case at the time. See 2 pictures of the court appearance... Asad Kalia denies allegations, says he was in Naini Central Jail Asad Kalia, the second accused in the case, was brought from Kasganj Jail and recorded his statement before the court. He said he was lodged in Naini Central Jail when the alleged incident took place. Kalia said, “I was lodged in Naini Central Jail at the time. I could not speak to anyone from the jail. The allegations against me are false and incorrect.” Altamash appears in court, but statement deferred Accused Altamash was also present in court in the case along with Ali and Asad Kalia. However, his statement could not be recorded as his lawyer did not arrive at the court on time. His lawyer subsequently requested that the statement be recorded on another date. After recording the statements of Ali and Asad Kalia, the court said they could be produced in person again if required. Otherwise, further proceedings would be conducted through video conferencing. Complainant’s brother was murdered in 2002; Atiq gang was accused In 2002, Mohammad Ashraf, a resident of Kasari Masari and not related to Atiq Ahmed, was murdered outside his house. Members of the Atiq gang were accused in the case. At the time, there was enmity between Atiq’s family and Ashraf’s family, although the two sides later reached a compromise. In 2023, Ashraf’s brother Afzal lodged an FIR at Kareli police station in connection with the matter. FIR witness now related to one of the accused Afzal, a resident of Kasari-Masari, named Amir Hamza as a witness in the FIR. Hamza has since become a close relative of one of the accused, as he married the sister of accused Altamash around six months ago. Given the family relationship and the fact that both families belong to the same community, the possibility of a settlement has now emerged. Over 250 policemen escorted Ali, yet associates reached him Ali Ahmed appeared before the ADJ court on Monday with a visibly different demeanour. He was wearing a white cap, shirt and jeans, with his hands tied and a gamcha in one hand. Police took him directly into the courtroom. The arrangements for bringing Ali to Prayagraj had been kept confidential, with no prior information available about his movement. More than 250 policemen escorted him from the district court to the courtroom. Despite the tight security, several of Ali’s relatives and associates ran alongside him and managed to reach him. Ali also spoke to several people despite the police cordon. Policemen repeatedly tried to keep people away, but some of his close associates managed to approach him amid the crowd of lawyers. 35 policemen escort Ali to Jhansi in three vehicles Ali, son of Atiq Ahmed, was produced in a Prayagraj court on Monday (21 Sept) in connection with an extortion case. When he came out of the court, media personnel tried to speak to him, but police prevented them from doing so. Ali was immediately taken to a police van, and the curtains were drawn. He was then taken to Jhansi in a three-vehicle convoy accompanied by 35 police personnel. Police admitted him to Jhansi jail at around 11 pm. Learn about the case in which Ali was produced in court Ali has been in jail for four years Ali has been in jail for four years. He surrendered at the Prayagraj court on 30 July 2022. He was then sent to Naini Central Jail. Cash was recovered from his barrack on 17 June 2025. He was subsequently sent to the security cell. He was transferred to Jhansi Jail on 1 October 2025.

stories.title: Man told teacher, ‘You take my life, I’ll take yours’:Handed pistol before shooting; killed her, then died by suicide in Lakhimpur
stories.summary: A young man who shot dead a teacher before dying by suicide in Lakhimpur had posted a final message on Instagram shortly before the incident. He wrote: “We have come into this world, so we will also have to leave it. Forgive me if I have hurt you knowingly or unknowingly... Allah Hafiz.” His Instagram bio had also reportedly been written in Spanish and read: “The user is dead...!” Man carried two country-made pistols to school The young man reportedly reached the school carrying two country-made pistols in his bag. He handed one of the pistols to the teacher and allegedly told him, “You take my life, and I will take yours.” When the teacher did not fire, the young man allegedly shot him before taking his own life. The teacher’s family has alleged that the killing was linked to one-sided love. The incident took place in the Sadar Kotwali area. Teacher shot inside school, attacker dies by suicide Children’s Academy School is located opposite the district collectorate. On Monday, September 21, Nishat Fatima, 26, was teaching students in a classroom on the second floor. At around 11.30 am, the attacker, Saud Ansari, 28, allegedly arrived at the school carrying a country-made pistol in his bag. He reportedly grabbed Fatima’s hand and dragged her to the veranda, where the two began arguing. Saud then allegedly pulled out the pistol and fired several shots at Fatima. She fell to the floor, while the gunshots triggered panic among students and staff. As schoolchildren screamed, staff rushed to the spot. Saud then shot himself and died at the scene. Saud and Nishat lived around 1 km apart Saud Ansari lived in Mohalla Naurangabad, while Nishat Fatima’s family lived in Hidayat Nagar. Their homes were around 1 km apart. Fatima travelled by auto-rickshaw every day to teach at Children’s Academy School in the Shahpura Kothi area. Local residents said that until a few months ago, Saud would occasionally ride his motorcycle to drop her off and pick her up. Nishat Fatima’s father works in Mumbai Saud Ansari’s father, Qayum Ansari, works at the District Industries Office, while his elder brother, Dawood Ansari, runs a sofa and mattress shop. Saud had completed his BCom and was pursuing a BEd. Nishat Fatima’s father, Iliyas, works in Mumbai. Her elder brother, Shadab Akhtar, is preparing for the PCS examination, while her younger brother, Anas, is also a student. The family originally belongs to Sultanpur. Nishat’s family moved from Sultanpur 12 years ago Around 12 years ago, Iliyas moved his family to Lakhimpur. Initially, the family rented a house owned by Saud’s family. It was during this period that Saud and Nishat began talking to each other. A few days later, Iliyas had a house built for his family and they moved there. However, Saud and Nishat continued to remain in contact. Saud had been posting sad content on social media Saud and Fatima had reportedly stopped speaking to each other over the past few months. During this period, Saud frequently posted content related to sadness and ego on Instagram. His Instagram bio read, “The user is dead.” A few minutes before the incident, Saud also posted a story on Instagram in which he spoke about death and asked people to delete his photographs and messages after his death. ‘Nothing in this world is permanent’ In the post, Saud asked people to pray for him after his death and forgive him if he had hurt anyone knowingly or unknowingly. He also requested people not to post his photographs or write “RIP” after his death, asking them instead to use the Islamic condolence phrase “Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un”. He ended the message by expressing pride in being a member of the Ummah of Prophet Muhammad and wrote, “Allah Hafiz.” Saud allegedly pressured teacher to talk to him and marry him People familiar with the matter, speaking on condition of anonymity, said Saud had allegedly been repeatedly pressuring Fatima to speak to him and marry him. On Monday morning, Saud reached Children’s Academy School carrying a bag containing two country-made pistols and five cartridges. The students were appearing for their examinations at the time. At around 11.30 am, after the exam ended, Fatima was escorting the students towards the school gate. Argument between the two escalated on first floor Meanwhile, Saud approached Fatima and began speaking to her. An argument reportedly broke out shortly afterwards. While arguing, the two reached the first floor and got into a heated confrontation in the corridor outside Room No. 11. Saud allegedly pulled out the pistols and handed one of them to Fatima. Hearing the commotion, a teacher from another classroom rushed to intervene. Saud allegedly pointed the pistol at her and threatened to shoot anyone who tried to interfere. The teacher then locked herself inside the classroom with the students. Saud opened fire when Fatima tried to flee Saud allegedly told Fatima, “You take my life, and I will take yours.” When she tried to flee, he allegedly opened fire at her. He then put the pistol to his temple and shot himself. The sound of gunfire triggered panic across the school, and staff hurriedly moved the children outside. Children flee school in panic, leave behind tiffins and water bottles As the examination was ending, many parents were waiting outside the school gate. The children were so frightened by the incident that several began crying as soon as they saw their family members. After being alerted by the school management, police reached the spot and evacuated the entire building. The children and their families were so terrified that they left behind their lunch boxes and water bottles inside the school. Two pistols and five cartridges recovered from spot Police personnel were deployed around the school and no one was allowed to enter the premises. Police recovered two country-made pistols, four spent cartridges and one live cartridge from the scene. SSP Khyati Garg, ASP Pawan Gautam and CO City Vivek Tiwari also reached the spot. Teacher’s brother alleges Saud pressured her to marry him Teacher Nishat Fatima’s brother, Shadab Akhtar, has lodged a complaint against Saud Ansari, his father Qayum Ansari and his mother. Shadab alleged that Saud frequently harassed his sister and pressured her to marry him. He said the family had confronted Saud several times and had also complained to his parents, but his behaviour did not change. Shadab has demanded strict action in the case. Police register case, post-mortems conducted Kotwal Rajesh Singh said Fatima’s brother had filed the complaint. He added that Saud had also accused Fatima’s father, Qayum Ansari, and mother of pressuring him to marry her. A case has been registered, and post-mortems have been conducted on the bodies of both Fatima and Saud.

In today’s UP Explainer, read why the upper-caste community is protesting in Dalit-dominated Agra. Is this a sign that the UGC agitation could begin again? stories.title: Getting ₹12,000 honorarium won’t be easy for Anganwadi workers:Pay raised with conditions; no incentive for negligence
stories.summary: Major news for Uttar Pradesh Anganwadi workers and helpers. The state government has increased their honorarium, but to receive the full amount, they will now have to ensure that their fieldwork and digital reporting are 100% accurate. Under the new rules, Anganwadi workers will receive the full honorarium of Rs 12,000, while helpers will get Rs 6,000 only if they complete all their assigned work and data entry on the app on time. If there is even a slight lapse in work or reporting, Rs 4,000 of the workers’ amount and Rs 2,000 of the helpers’ amount will be deducted as Performance Linked Incentive (PLI). This means simply attending the centre will no longer be enough to receive the full payment. They will have to provide a complete account of the services provided to children and pregnant women. Understand the calculation of honorarium and PLI Uttar Pradesh has 1,75,335 Anganwadi workers and 1,68,158 helpers. To understand the increase in their honorarium, it is important to look at the ‘fixed salary’ and ‘incentive’ components. This means the worker’s fixed honorarium has now become Rs 8,000 and the PLI Rs 4,000. Similarly, helpers will receive a fixed honorarium of Rs 4,000 and a PLI of Rs 2,000. If a worker opens the centre for 21 days in a month and carries out the basic work of teaching and feeding children, she will receive only Rs 8,000. The remaining Rs 4,000 will be paid only if she completes all the other digital and field-level tasks prescribed by the department. Of this Rs 4,000 incentive, Rs 2,500 will be paid by the state government and Rs 1,500 by the Centre. There is growing discontent among workers over the decision, but officials argue that the system is necessary to improve the health of children and mothers. 50% of workers unable to receive full PLI Officials of the Department of Child Development and Nutrition say around 50% of workers currently do not receive the full PLI. The biggest reason is that several workers are unable to upload their data and reports on time on the ‘Poshan Tracker’ app. Under the rules, the amount of PLI credited to a worker’s account will depend on the proportion of reports uploaded on the portal. Officials expect that the increase in the incentive amount to Rs 4,000 will encourage more workers to upload their reports. They expect around 90% of women to be able to receive the full PLI. Know when and how the full PLI will be paid 1. Anganwadi workers’ salary breakup Total honorarium - Rs 12,000 Fixed - Rs 8,000 PLI (incentive) - Rs 4,000, as follows: 2. Anganwadi helpers’ salary breakup Total honorarium - Rs 6,000 Fixed - Rs 4,000 PLI (incentive) - Rs 2,000, as follows: Anganwadi workers will have to fulfil these 4 responsibilities The government has laid down the responsibilities of Anganwadi workers. Officials claim that if the work is done properly, these tasks can be completed within 5 to 7 days a month. 1. Education and centre operations: Provide Early Childhood Care and Education (ECCE) to children before they start school, teach them basic literacy and develop good habits through play-based learning. Organise creative and cultural activities for the mental and physical development of children. 2. Nutrition and healthcare: Provide nutritious food and rations to children below six years of age, pregnant women and breastfeeding mothers. Measure children’s height and weight and identify severely malnourished (SAM/MAM) children. Work with ANMs and ASHAs to ensure timely vaccination of children and women and refer sick children to Primary Health Centres (PHCs). Actively participate in Pulse Polio and other government health campaigns. 3. Digital reporting: Record real-time data on mobile phones. Use the facial recognition system during the distribution of rations and supplementary nutrition. Measure children’s growth using the new device and immediately enter the data on the mobile phone. 4. Surveys and home visits: Visit mothers at their homes and educate them about hygiene, breastfeeding, and a balanced diet. Maintain records of new births, deaths, pregnant women, and families in the area. Anganwadi helpers will also have to perform these 6 key tasks Helpers play a crucial role in running an Anganwadi centre. Their main duties are: Poshan Tracker app ends middlemen’s role Officials of the Department of Child Development and Nutrition believe that linking the PLI system with the Poshan Tracker app and digital platforms has ended the role of middlemen and corruption in the system. According to officials, as soon as workers upload their work reports on the portal through their mobile phones, the incentive system will automatically calculate their payment. No official will have the power to stop it. This, they say, will ensure that the actual benefits of the schemes reach children and women who need them.

stories.title: Man feeds wife biryani, gives her lassi, then stabs her:Har­doi man pierced her heart; couple had no child for 12 years
stories.summary: In Hardoi, a husband stabbed his wife to death after feeding her biryani and giving her lassi. He stabbed her so many times that her heart also ruptured. They had been married for 12 years. Despite this, they had not had a child. The husband suspected that his wife was having an affair with someone. Police revealed on Thursday evening that the woman had been murdered in the early hours of Wednesday. Based on the husband's information, police recovered the small Rampuri knife used in the murder. After arresting the accused, police sent him to jail. The incident took place in the Islamnagar Tiliya area. He switched on the high-speed fan to prevent his wife's screams from being heard Parvez (34), a resident of Islamnagar Tilia, had a love marriage with his niece by relation, Nagमा (30), 12 years ago. The couple had no children. The husband suspected that his wife was having an affair with Nazim, a motorcycle mechanic. The couple had frequently quarrelled over this issue for eight months. On Tuesday night, Nagमा was lying on a wooden cot in the room when Parvez killed her. The door was locked. As a high-speed fan was running in the room, no one realised that a murder had taken place. At 3:30 a.m. on Wednesday, Parvez called his sister Jubina and informed her about the incident. Now read the accused's confession... During questioning, Parvez told police that before the incident, he had fed his wife Nagma biryani and then given her lassi. The two began arguing after this. Nagma brought a knife to attack him. The husband snatched the knife from Nagma. He then repeatedly stabbed her in the chest and neck with the same knife. After the incident, the accused took a bath and admitted to the murder in front of police. Police arrested him. Husband had told police he feared for his life from his wife The investigation revealed that five days before the murder, the accused had lodged a complaint at the Kotwali police station, saying he faced a threat to his life from his wife and her lover. The police are now investigating the complaint and the lover's role as well. The police have sent the accused husband, Parvez, to jail. According to the post-mortem report, the woman had suffered serious injuries to her chest. The police said the blows to her chest had ruptured her heart. The body was buried at the cemetery near Bilgram Chungi on Wednesday night.

stories.title: No vigilance probe against IAS Abhishek Prakash:Lucknow HC questions why affidavit wasn’t filed; complainant admits mistake
stories.summary: The Lucknow High Court has quashed the vigilance inquiry initiated against IAS officer Abhishek Prakash. Justice Rajiv Singh accepted Abhishek Prakash's petition on Thursday and cancelled the inquiry proceedings initiated through government orders issued on 20 and 28 March 2025. Abhishek Prakash has served as secretary of the Industrial Development Department and CEO of Invest UP. Case began in March 2025 The case was related to a complaint filed by an official of a company on 20 March 2025. It alleged that a senior Invest UP official had given the complainant Nikant Jain's mobile number and asked him to contact Jain. Nikant Jain was alleged to have demanded 5% of the project's value to secure its approval from the empowered committee and the Cabinet. FIR against Nikant Jain had already been quashed An FIR was registered against Nikant Jain on the basis of the complaint. Meanwhile, a letter was sent for a vigilance inquiry along with the initiation of departmental action against Abhishek Prakash. During the hearing, the High Court considered it significant that no affidavit had been filed along with the complaint. A major development later took place in the case. In a counter-affidavit filed in court, company official Biswajit Dutta said the complaint dated 20 March had been made due to a misunderstanding. At the time, he was unaware that reports from YEIDA and UPCL on land availability and other related issues were still awaited. Biswajit Dutta also made it clear that he had not paid any money to Nikant Jain. The company proposed establishing a solar cell and solar module manufacturing unit in Invest UP on 3 December 2024. Meetings of the evaluation committee were held on 24 February, 12 March and 25 March 2025 to consider the proposal. At the 12 March meeting, the company was asked to provide further information, as details related to land and electricity subsidies were not available. Following this, the committee recommended at its 25 March meeting that the company's proposal be placed before the High-Level Empowered Committee. Complaint described as a misunderstanding in an affidavit Senior advocate Gaurav Mehrotra, appearing for Abhishek Prakash, told the court that the project was already under consideration at the evaluation committee level. The meeting held on 25 March had also recommended placing it before the High-Level Empowered Committee. He said the complainant had later submitted an affidavit himself, stating that the complaint was the result of a misunderstanding. The petition also argued that initiating a vigilance inquiry on the basis of a complaint without an affidavit and failing to obtain the prescribed approval of the State Vigilance Committee was not in accordance with government rules. Affidavits are required to prevent fake complaints Advocates Shailendra Kumar Singh and Anirudh Singh, appearing for the state government, opposed the petition. They said the administrative department had decided to order a vigilance inquiry in view of the seriousness of the allegations. The complaint could not be treated as fake outright. During the hearing, it was also accepted that the 1997 government order provides for an affidavit to be submitted along with a complaint to prevent fake complaints against Group A officers. In its judgement, the High Court said that the requirement to submit an affidavit along with complaints against Group-A officers is intended to protect honest officers from harassment based on false or fabricated complaints. Investigation launched without waiting for the outcome of the proceedings The court also found that, despite departmental proceedings having been initiated against Abhishek Prakash, the matter was referred to the Vigilance Department without waiting for their outcome. In addition, approval was not obtained from the State Vigilance Committee in accordance with the prescribed procedure. The court said that when the complainant himself has stated that the complaint was the result of a misunderstanding, the basis for any action taken further on the complaint also ceases to exist. On this basis, the court quashed the vigilance investigation initiated against Abhishek Prakash and the related government orders. What was Abhishek accused of regarding corruption? Read the allegations point by point 1. Defence Corridor Land Scam The role of then District Magistrate Abhishek Prakash was also found to be suspect in the case involving land acquired for the Defence Corridor in Bhatgaon, Lucknow. While serving as chairman of the land acquisition committee, he colluded with the tehsil administration to arbitrarily fix land prices. Land allotted to members of the Scheduled Caste category in 1984 was illegally made eligible for sale. A compensation amount of ₹20 crore was claimed through collusion between brokers and officials in the buying and selling of the land. 2- Allegations of irregularities while serving as LDA vice-chairman Abhishek was accused of favouring several builders and issuing sealing orders and licences arbitrarily while serving as vice-chairman of the Lucknow Development Authority (LDA). According to sources, he had several illegal constructions demolished during his tenure as LDA vice-chairman, but also benefited builders close to him. Licences were issued to favoured builders in several areas, including Ashiyana. He was also accused of keeping builders' files pending in collusion with LDA officials. 3. Corruption allegations in Aligarh, Lakhimpur and Hamirpur Abhishek Prakash has served as the district magistrate of Aligarh, Lakhimpur Kheri and Hamirpur. Complaints had been filed against him in Aligarh over irregularities in the purchase and sale of land. He was accused of manipulating government tenders in Lakhimpur and colluding with the mining mafia in Hamirpur. 4- Accused of buying 700 bighas of land while serving as DM in two districts Abhishek has been accused of buying 700 bighas of land in Lakhimpur Kheri and Bareilly in the names of his family members. He allegedly bought the land in the names of his relatives-his mother, father and brother-and by setting up some fake companies. He has similarly been accused of buying 400 bighas of land in Bareilly. There are also allegations of stamp duty evasion in both places.

stories.title: Resort near Taj Mahal gets bomb threat:Message warns of blast within 8 days; police force, BDS team reach spot
stories.summary: An email threatening to blow up a resort near the Taj Mahal in Agra was received. The threat was sent via email. The email said that a bomb had been placed inside the resort and could explode at any time within eight days. The resort operator was shocked after receiving the email. He immediately informed the police. The police department was thrown into a panic as soon as it received the information. The Tajganj police, circle officers, the BDS and the dog squad teams reached the spot. The police first evacuated the resort and cordoned off the entire area. The BDS team then began an intensive search operation inside. See three pictures... Resort owner informs police A threatening email was received by the Taj Resort near the Jalma Institute in the Tajganj area. Resort owner Ramesh Wadhwa said the email arrived on the resort's ID in the evening. It said that a bomb had been placed at the resort and that it could be detonated at any time within eight days. The resort owner informed the police. Following the information, the ACP Taj Security and police force reached the spot. The bomb disposal squad was called in. The resort was checked. Every inch searched, every room inspected The BDS team thoroughly checked every room, hall, kitchen, storeroom, parking area and basement of the resort. No suspicious object was touched. The team scanned the entire premises using modern equipment. No explosive material has been found so far during the investigation, which continued for around two hours. The police said they were treating it as the handiwork of miscreants while taking all necessary precautions. Email being checked According to the police, the email contains only a threat; no information has been provided about the location or the type of bomb. Taking the matter seriously, the cyber cell has been assigned to investigate it. Efforts are under way to trace the ID from which the email was sent, as well as the IP address and location from which it was sent. DCP City Syed Ali Abbas said, The resort owner informed us about the threatening email. The police team conducted an investigation. No suspicious object was found. Further action will be taken after a written complaint is received from the resort owner.

stories.title: UP PCS Mains result out:2,297 candidates qualify for interview; 814 posts to be filled, selected from 10,284 aspirants
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh Public Service Commission (UPPSC) released the results of the PCS-2025 written examination on Thursday evening. A total of 10,284 candidates appeared for the examination, and 2,297 candidates have been declared successful for the interview. Recruitment is to be conducted for a total of 814 PCS posts. Of these, selection for 812 posts will be based on the written examination and interview. For the remaining two posts, selection will be based solely on the written examination. The result for these two posts will be declared along with the final selection results. Examination held between 29 March and 1 April The PCS-2025 main written examination was held from 29 March to 1 April in 2026 at several examination centres in Prayagraj and Lucknow. Girijesh Kumar Tyagi of the commission said that the recruitment drive has 814 vacancies across 28 types of posts. Of these, selection for 812 posts will be based on the written examination and interview. A total of 2,297 candidates have been declared successful for the next stage – the interview – for these posts. Candidates who have passed the main examination will now have to appear for an interview. The commission will soon separately release complete information on post preferences and the interview. The interview dates and other necessary instructions will be announced thereafter. Result available on commission’s notice board and website Earlier, 10,284 candidates had cleared the preliminary examination. Secretary Girijesh Kumar Tyagi said the main examination result is available on the commission’s notice board and website. Selected candidates can check their roll numbers in the list. All information related to the next stage of the process will also be released on the website. Results Related to Cases Pending in the High Court While releasing the results, the commission also mentioned two important legal conditions. In Writ Petition No. 4253/2026, Arpit Shivam Mishra versus the State of Uttar Pradesh and Others, the petitioner's result will remain subject to the final decision of the Allahabad High Court. Similarly, the results of female candidates from outside Uttar Pradesh will also remain subject to the High Court's final decision in Special Appeal No. 475 (D)/2019. This means that despite the results being declared in these cases, the final status will be determined in accordance with the relevant judicial decision. Cut-off and marks to be released later The commission has also clarified the position regarding candidates' marks and the cut-off. Details of the candidates' marks, cut-off marks and other information will be released only after the final selection results are declared. At this stage, the commission has advised candidates not to file applications under the Right to Information Act seeking this information.

stories.title: Life term for student’s killers who burnt her alive:Wife clings to husband weeping as he goes to jail in Sultanpur; mother gives son ₹500
stories.summary: Two men convicted of killing well-known student Shraddha Singh in Sultanpur were sentenced to life imprisonment and fined ₹50,000 each by Fast Track Court (FTC) II at 4.20 pm on Thursday, with both convicts standing with their heads bowed during the proceedings. As they left the court, Subhash's mother gave him ₹500, prompting him to cry, while his veiled wife clung to him and wept, telling him, "I will not let you go"; she relented after he tried to reassure her. Shraddha's father, Pradeep Singh, said, "In my view, the punishment is inadequate. They should have been hanged. However, I accept the court's verdict." The case falls under the jurisdiction of Baldirai police station. Both Convicts Stood Quietly in the Lockup When the court sentenced both convicts, Subhash and Jaykaran, to life imprisonment, they stood quietly in the lock-up. Their lawyer comforted them by saying that he would appeal in the High Court and assuring them that they would be released soon. After the sentence was pronounced, as the police brought Subhash out, his wife held his hand. She began crying with her head resting on his shoulder and refused to let him go. Her husband comforted her and freed his hand. The police then took Subhash away. His wife sat on the bench and burst into tears. Shailendra Kumar Pandey, the complainant's lawyer, said, "Subhash Singh Chauhan and Jaykaran have been convicted in the Shraddha Singh murder case. Both have been sentenced to life imprisonment and fined ₹50,000 each." Twelve witnesses presented by the victim's side In the fast-track court, the victim's side presented twelve witnesses to prove the incident. ADGC Criminal Sanjay Singh and the complainant's lawyer, Shailendra Pandey, represented the case. On Wednesday, the court convicted Subhash Singh Chauhan and Jaykaran Chauhan. Jaykaran is unmarried. The High Court had rejected his bail pleas three times. Subhash, meanwhile, is married. He has a son and a daughter. His bail plea had also been rejected by the High Court four times. Both were arrested on 24 September 2020. The third accused's case stayed, separate hearing under way for the fourth Further proceedings against another accused in the case, Jagbaran Yadav, have been stayed by the High Court. It has been reported that the student did not name him in the statement she gave before the magistrate. Another accused, Mahant, had remained absconding for a long time. In July 2026, the police arrested him from Dehli Bazaar and sent him to jail. His trial is being conducted separately. Now, a look at the murder case... The incident took place on the morning of 21 September 2020. Shraddha, the 17-year-old daughter of Pradeep Singh, a resident of Tarsa, was studying in the first year of a BSc and was alone at home. At the time, her mother had gone to the jail to meet her husband. Meanwhile, Subhash Singh Chauhan, Jaikaran, Mahant and Jagannath, all from Ainjar village, around 500 metres away, reached her house. They tied up Shraddha's hands, feet and mouth, poured kerosene over her and set her on fire. She named three people in her statement to the magistrate Shraddha suffered severe burns. She was then taken to the Community Health Centre in Dhanpatganj. In her statement to the magistrate there, Shraddha named Subhash Singh Chauhan, Jaikaran and Mahant. As her condition was critical, she was referred to Sultanpur District Hospital and then to Lucknow. She died during treatment in Lucknow. Father had been released on parole to perform his daughter's last rites On the day after Shraddha's death, her father, Pradeep Singh, was released from prison on parole and performed his daughter's last rites. Her father said that the police registered a case only after considerable pressure. Pradeep Singh said he owned three bighas of land, which his daughter's killers wanted to seize. On 8 June 2020, he was ploughing the field when they arrived there. A quarrel broke out during this. Subhash Singh's father, Kunwar Singh, 70, died in the altercation. Case registered against 29 people, including the student's father In the case of Kunwar Singh's death, police had registered a murder case against 14 named people, including Pradeep Singh, and 15 unidentified people. Subsequently, the case of Shraddha's murder came to light. Now, in this same murder case, the court has sentenced Subhash Singh Chauhan and Jaikaran to life imprisonment.

stories.title: Snake hidden in blanket bites brother-sister:Sleeping on same cot in Agra; sister dies at nephew’s naming ceremony
stories.summary: Snake hiding in a blanket bit a brother and sister who were sleeping on the same cot to protect themselves from the cold in Agra. The sister did not even realise that she had been bitten. When the brother's condition deteriorated, his family took him to hospital for treatment. The sister, unaware that she had been bitten by a snake, began feeling unwell shortly afterwards. She was then taken to hospital, where she died during treatment. The incident took place on Wednesday. The brother's son was due to have his naming ceremony today, Thursday. The case is from Murkiya village in the Kagarol area. See two pictures... The son had been born only 10 days earlier Rakesh, Pankaj's father, said that Pankaj's son was born 10 days earlier. The naming ceremony was scheduled for Wednesday, and relatives had come home for it. Kamini and Pankaj were sleeping on a charpoy in the room. They felt cold at night and were given a blanket to cover themselves. A snake was hiding in the same blanket. It bit Kamini first. It then coiled around Pankaj's leg and bit him as well. As soon as Pankaj realised that he had been bitten, he raised the alarm. Sister kept screaming, "Save my brother" Rakesh said Kamini also woke up after hearing the noise. She was the one who saw the black snake on Pankaj's leg. However, Kamini did not realise that the snake had bitten her too. She kept screaming, "Snake, snake," as she tried to save her brother. She repeatedly said, "Take my brother to hospital quickly. Save him." She began vomiting half an hour later Rakesh said Pankaj was brought to the district hospital that night. His treatment began. Just then, a call came from home saying that Kamini's condition had deteriorated. She was vomiting and complaining of a burning sensation in her chest and dizziness. It was later discovered that she too had been bitten by a snake. She was also brought to the hospital, where she died during treatment. Family had faith healers perform rituals to save their daughter's life After Kamini was brought home, the family called snake charmers who performed exorcism rituals. But there was no improvement. The family cremated her at around 8 p.m. on Wednesday. Meanwhile, Pankaj has been admitted to GR Hospital on Shamsabad Road. According to family members, Kamini was the daughter of Rakesh's late brother. The family is in mourning following Kamini's death. While the family is grieving the loss of their daughter, they are also praying to God to save Pankaj's life. Pankaj's father, Rakesh, said that his son had studied up to Class 11. Pankaj had married Khushboo around ten months ago. Pankaj had become a father to a son just ten days ago. Preparations for the baby's naming ceremony were under way at home, but the death of his daughter a day earlier turned the celebrations into mourning.

stories.title: Apple manager murder case:Constable convicted of culpable homicide, second cop acquitted; wife calls verdict ‘shameful’, says will move HC
stories.summary: Constable Prashant Chaudhary has been convicted by a court in the killing of Apple manager Vivek Tiwari in Lucknow eight years ago. In its verdict delivered on Thursday, the court found Prashant Chaudhary guilty of culpable homicide not amounting to murder. The other constable, Sandeep Kumar, has been acquitted. Vivek's wife, Kalpana Tiwari, expressed her displeasure with the court's verdict. Calling the decision "substandard", she said she would appeal against it in a higher court. Kalpana said, "We had been watching the court's decision since this morning. We had hoped that we would get justice, but the verdict that has been delivered is unjust. If the death penalty was not awarded, he should at least have been sentenced to life imprisonment." Wife says, 'He was a trained constable, how could he have made a mistake while firing? Kalpana Tiwari said, “Prashant Chaudhary was a trained constable. So how could he have made a mistake while firing? My husband was shot dead. Both constables were present at the spot.” Sandeep’s acquittal is also wrong, both were equally responsible Kalpana also questioned the acquittal of the second accused, Sandeep Kumar. She said, “Acquitting Sandeep is also the wrong decision. Both constables were equally at fault.” Visibly emotional over the court’s verdict, Kalpana said she did not know what she would tell her children now. The family had been waiting for justice in the case for a long time, but the court’s decision had left them disappointed. Vivek died after being shot by Police in 2018 Late on September 29, 2018, Vivek Tiwari, an area sales manager with Apple, was returning home in a car with his colleague Sana Khan. Near the Makdoompur police outpost in Gomti Nagar Extension, constables Prashant Chaudhary and Sandeep Kumar tried to stop his car. According to police, the car did not stop and a collision appeared imminent. During this, Prashant Chaudhary fired a shot that hit Vivek. He died while undergoing treatment at a hospital. Both constables faced trial After the incident, a case was registered at the Gomti Nagar police station in Lucknow based on a complaint by Vivek Tiwari’s colleague, Sana Khan. Both constables were subsequently arrested and suspended. The case was investigated by an SIT, which filed a chargesheet after completing its probe. The trial was then conducted in the Lucknow district court. After the judicial process, including statements from witnesses and examination of evidence, was completed, the final arguments concluded on August 6. News is being updated...

stories.title: 'Dewar-Bhabhi' die by suicide after jumping into canal:Affair for a year; left home 9 days ago, told elder brother they would die
stories.summary: Bodies of a brother-in-law and his sister-in-law were found in a canal about 13 kilometres from their home in Kasganj. The two had left home nine days earlier after having an affair. The elder brother said his younger brother had called to say that he and his sister-in-law were near the canal and were going to die by suicide. Their mobile phones were switched off after that. Fearing that something untoward had happened, the police were informed. The police and the PAC Flood Unit searched the canal for several days, but the two were not found. The bodies of both were recovered from the canal on Thursday. The man was identified as Krishnakant, 27, a resident of Manauta, while the woman was identified as Priyanka, the wife of his elder brother, Pankaj. Priyanka lived in Panipat with her husband Pankaj, while Krishnakant lived in the village. According to the police, the two had been having an affair for about a year. They had left their respective homes to meet each other. They died by suicide out of fear of society. See three pictures... On Thursday morning, passers-by saw two bodies floating in the canal and informed the police. Read the full story... Krishnakant (27), a resident of Manauta in Kasganj, was the third of four siblings. His elder brother, Pankaj (33), and sister Madhuri (29) are married. Krishnakant and his 15-year-old younger sister Lalita are unmarried. After completing his BSc, Krishnakant was preparing for police recruitment. Priyanka, meanwhile, was pursuing her BSc. Around four years ago, Priyanka eloped with Pankaj and the two had a love marriage. After their marriage, they began living in Panipat. According to the family, Krishnakant often visited his brother's home on the pretext of meeting him. Around a year ago, Priyanka and Krishnakant began having an affair. Krishnakant had left home on 7 September Pankaj said he worked at a textile warehouse in Panipat. At around 1 p.m. on 7 September, he returned to his room for lunch. His four-year-old daughter was lying on the bed, and a cold drink and a packet of crisps were in the room, but his wife Priyanka was not there. Pankaj then called his mother, Ramwati, at around 1.30 p.m. and asked about Priyanka. His mother said Priyanka had not come there. At around 6 p.m., Pankaj called his younger brother, Krishnakant. Krishnakant said Priyanka was with him and that they were in Delhi's Kashmere Gate-Chandni Chowk area. When Pankaj said he would come there, Krishnakant said they would come themselves and that he did not need to come. Told his father, ‘I have come to get medicine...’ Meanwhile, a family member in the village said that Krishnakant had left home at around 11 a.m. on 7 September, saying he was going to get medicine. He did not return until late evening. At around 6 p.m., when his father called him, Krishnakant said there was a queue to get the medicine and that it would take some time. At around 3 a.m. on 8 September, Krishnakant called Pankaj. He told him that he and Priyanka were near the picnic point at Hazara Canal in Nadrai. Swearing on his mother's life, Krishnakant said that the two were going to end their lives. Priyanka also spoke to Pankaj over the phone during the call. Pankaj sent Krishnakant a message urging him not to take such a step and to stay safe. Shortly afterwards, Krishnakant's mobile phone was switched off. Both their belongings were found at the spot On 8 September, police reached the spot after receiving information that some belongings had been found in a bag near the picnic point at Hazara Canal in Nadrai, Kasganj. The investigation revealed that Krishnakant and Priyanka were missing. Police found both their purses, clothes and other belongings at the spot. The items were secured and an investigation was launched. Police and the PAC Flood Unit searched for the two in the canal for several days, but could not trace them. Jewellery, cash and photographs found in the purses Police found gold jewellery, ₹4,510 in cash and a passport-sized photograph of Priyanka in one purse. The other purse contained a bindi and passport-sized photographs. Four ATM cards, a driving licence and ₹510 in cash were found in the men's wallet. Both bodies found in canal after 9 days The bodies of both were found in Etah's Hazara Canal, around 8 kilometres from Kasganj, on the morning of Thursday, 17 September. Villagers who had gone out for their morning walk spotted the bodies and informed the police. The police reached the spot and had both bodies pulled out of the canal. The two bodies appeared to be connected to each other. After news of the bodies being found spread, family members and villagers gathered at the spot. Family suspects murder Station House Officer Videsh Rathi said, The bodies of a brother-in-law and sister-in-law have been found. Both bodies have been taken into custody and sent for post-mortem examination. An investigation is under way. Further action will be taken based on the post-mortem report. Meanwhile, the family members have expressed suspicion that both were murdered. The actual cause of death will become clear only after the post-mortem report and the police investigation.
