stories.title: Akhilesh wears blue scarf again at press meet:Says SP-built roads are No.1; former BJP minister joins SP
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav held a press conference at the party headquarters at 1pm on Thursday. Just before it began, party workers and journalists were shown a special film. It featured a ground report on the poor condition of various expressways in Uttar Pradesh, including damaged sections of the Kanpur-Lucknow and Ganga expressways, as well as alleged corruption in their construction. Meanwhile, former cabinet minister Prof Ram Asare Kushwaha returned to the Samajwadi Party along with his supporters after leaving the BJP. Prof Ramshray Vishwakarma and prominent Mathura businessman Ashok Agrawal also joined the SP. Akhilesh Yadav welcomed them into the party wearing a blue scarf around his neck. Mayawati, the BSP supremo, had earlier launched a sharp attack on Akhilesh over his wearing of a blue scarf. She said wearing blue clothes or a blue scarf does not change the casteist mindset of opposition parties and alleged that they were trying to mislead the Bahujan community. Read 5 major things said by Akhilesh… Roads are built later, but start breaking first Akhilesh Yadav said, “I would tell BJP leaders that if Maa Ganga ever calls you, don’t travel via the Ganga Expressway. After the first rain, it became a ‘water expressway’. Carpets were brought from Bhadohi to cover its potholes.” He also listed shortcomings in three other expressways: Bundelkhand Expressway: The expressway inaugurated by the Prime Minister sank soon after it became operational. Repair work is still underway there. Purvanchal Expressway: “They copied us and even landed a fighter jet there. But today, as soon as you pick up speed, your vehicle could land you in hospital or leave you needing back treatment.” Kanpur-Lucknow Expressway: “Two days ago, an RCC bridge started collapsing and the reinforcement bars became visible. I don’t know whether the cement was poor quality or the sand. I have now heard that the company has been blacklisted.” Race for profits between Lucknow and Delhi Akhilesh Yadav also attacked the government over the economy, unemployment and digital transactions. He said, “At the time of demonetisation, it was said that it was meant for the wealthy, but ordinary people suffered. Now even UPI has become a system for extracting money and collecting tolls. This game by these ‘toll collectors’ must stop.” He said more than 20 recruitment examination papers had been leaked in Uttar Pradesh, asking whether any major accused had been sent to jail. He said that if the Samajwadi Party came to power, young people would get employment and social justice (PDA) would be established. He also said, “I have heard that 2 billion trees have been planted on paper. During the SP government, 134,000 trees were planted on 1,000 acres of land. If 2 billion trees have been planted, the government should explain where that land is.” ‘Quality of roads built by us is still number one’ Akhilesh Yadav said, “No one can question the quality of the infrastructure built by the Samajwadis even today. The Agra-Lucknow Expressway is the best expressway in the country. NHAI tried to copy its design but could not replicate it.” He alleged that BJP leaders had even misappropriated money meant for expressway maintenance and failed to build markets along the expressways. He said, “The laptops distributed during the SP government still switch on today. The nozzles at the Gomti Riverfront have not rusted even now. The RCC roads built for the cycle highway during our tenure remain just as strong.” He further said, “What do those who do politics over cow dung and cow urine have to do with a perfume park? Who built the place where the Chief Minister himself sits? If the truth comes out, they will return by boat.” ‘Law and order has collapsed, LDA has become a deal-making agency’ Akhilesh Yadav alleged that murders were taking place continuously across the state, including in Lucknow and Gorakhpur. He said NCRB data showed that women and girls were not safe. He also alleged that Uttar Pradesh had become number one in cybercrime and harassment of journalists. He said the Lucknow Development Authority (LDA) had now become a “deal-making agency”. Referring to a video that had gone viral in Shahjahanpur, the home district of the Finance Minister, he said people allegedly involved in taking bribes were seen swearing not to expose each other. He questioned the situation in a district belonging to a minister who sits beside the Chief Minister. ‘We will build a temple for Vishwakarmaji and declare a holiday on his jayanti’ On the occasion of Vishwakarma Jayanti, Akhilesh Yadav made a major announcement. He said the public holiday observed during the SP government had been discontinued by the BJP. He said the holiday would be restored if the SP returned to power. He also announced that a grand and beautiful temple dedicated to Lord Vishwakarma would be built along the Gomti Riverfront in Lucknow. Ram Asare Kushwaha says, ‘Akhilesh ji honoured me by seating me beside him’ Former minister Prof Ram Asare Kushwaha, who returned to the Samajwadi Party, presented Akhilesh Yadav with a photograph of ‘Netaji’ (Mulayam Singh Yadav). He also handed over a cheque for ₹1 million, of which ₹500,000 was donated to Netaji’s trust. Kushwaha said, “Akhilesh ji honoured me by giving me a chair beside him, just as Netaji used to. Party workers will not sit quietly until Akhilesh Yadav takes oath as Chief Minister again. Netaji used to call me his ‘Birbal’ because I always spoke the truth.” Kushwaha’s return to the SP is being viewed as significant in the context of Uttar Pradesh politics and the upcoming Assembly elections. After returning to the Samajwadi Party, Ram Asare Kushwaha said, Respect is the most important thing in politics. Wherever I am respected, that is where the relationship will remain.

stories.title: Yogi, Rajnath distribute cake at Kashi Vishwanath:Naidu-Paswan also attended; Naga Sadhu played damru, Malini Awasthi sang sohar
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi is celebrating his birthday today. Modi has turned 76. Grand events are being organised in his parliamentary constituency, Varanasi. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath and Defence Minister Rajnath Singh offered prayers at the Kashi Vishwanath Temple. They then distributed cakes and presented Banarasi sarees to women sanitation workers. Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu and Union Minister Chirag Paswan were also present. 76 litres of milk used for Ganga abhishek in Kashi Meanwhile, Batuk Brahmins performed a 'Dugdabhishek' of Maa Ganga using 76 litres of milk. They blew conch shells and performed Ganga Aarti. At Ahilyabai Ghat, former minister of state and MLA Dr Neelkanth Tiwari performed puja with Vedic chants. Naga sadhus played damrus and extended birthday greetings to the Prime Minister. The Namami Gange team offered a 76-metre chunari to Maa Ganga. Cleanliness drive in Ayodhya; special puja at Prayagraj In Ayodhya, Mayor Mahant Girish Pati Tripathi and District Panchayat Chairperson Roli Singh participated in a cleanliness drive by sweeping at Lata Mangeshkar Chowk. In Prayagraj, a special puja and Aarti were performed at the Sangam. Malini Awasthi also congratulated PM Modi on his birthday by singing a sohar. | PM Modi turns 76: Shah flags off 1,300-km Vadnagar-Varanasi bike rally, says 36 countries have honoured the PM Fruits distributed to patients in Lucknow In Lucknow, Deputy Chief Minister Brajesh Pathak distributed fruits to patients at the Civil Hospital. He also inaugurated a blood donation camp. He said the ‘Seva Sankalp Abhiyan’ was being conducted across the state from 17 September. Under the campaign, activities such as fruit distribution and blood donation camps are being organised at hospitals across the state. The campaign will continue for one month, until 17 October. 1,300-km bike yatras between Vadnagar and Varanasi Two ‘Seva Sankalp Bike Yatras’, covering around 1,300 km between Modi’s birthplace Vadnagar and his Lok Sabha constituency Varanasi, are being organised. One yatra is travelling from Vadnagar to Varanasi, while the other will set out from Varanasi for Vadnagar. In Varanasi, Yogi Adityanath and Rajnath Singh will flag off the yatra shortly. The journey will conclude on 7 October. See 5 photos-

stories.title: CM Yogi to remain key face for UP Assembly election:RSS tells BJP about ground realities, says, 'Set aside differences and focus on preparations'
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh Assembly election will be fought under the leadership of Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, with Yogi as the face of the election. This was made clear at a coordination meeting held in the presence of senior office-bearers of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS). The Sangh told the organisation, including BJP office-bearers, to “forget all differences and problems and now focus on election preparations.” Based on feedback received from organisations at the grassroots level, the Sangh also made several suggestions to the BJP and the government. A meeting of senior office-bearers of the Sangh and BJP was held at Dream World Resort in Lucknow on Wednesday. BJP National General Secretary (Organisation) BL Santosh and the party's Uttar Pradesh in-charge, Vinod Tawde, sought grassroots feedback from Sangh office-bearers about Assembly constituencies in their respective areas. Feedback was sought on the strengths and weaknesses of the constituencies. Uttar Pradesh BJP president Pankaj Chaudhary, general secretary Dharmpal Singh, the Sangh's regional pracharak Anil Kumar and all provincial pracharaks were present at the meeting. According to sources, the Sangh said Yogi's image among the public is good and there is no adverse narrative against him. However, there is an unfavourable atmosphere against MLAs in some places. People are unhappy with their working style, while relations between MLAs and party workers are also not good. The Sangh also gave feedback that the working style of police and administrative officials is not good either, and public-related work is not being carried out properly. Focus on Dalits and backward classes to increase; ways to counter anti-incumbency to be explored The meeting emphasised the need to bring Dalits and backward classes into the fold before the Assembly elections. Concern was expressed that both sections could shift towards the Samajwadi Party. The BJP would benefit electorally by bringing both sections on board. The meeting said the central leadership's position was clear: Yogi would remain the face of the election. The BJP will contest the Uttar Pradesh election with full force. Finding a way to counter growing anti-incumbency and the negative narrative at the grassroots level has emerged as the biggest challenge. The RSS made it clear that being active on social media does not simply mean uploading photographs. Leaders will have to go beyond posting birthday wishes and reposting other leaders' posts and instead build a narrative in their respective areas. Sangh coordinator Kripashankar raised issues related to the government and the BJP. According to sources, Tawde and BL Santosh will speak to BJP national president Nitin Nabin and Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath after receiving the Sangh's feedback. They will try to resolve the issues that have been reported. Modi, Shah and Nitin Nabin to visit Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Home Minister Amit Shah and BJP national president Nitin Nabin will visit Uttar Pradesh in the coming days. Before the election is announced, Modi will hold one rally each in the Awadh, Kashi, Braj, western Uttar Pradesh, Gorakhpur and Kanpur regions. Major projects will be inaugurated and foundation stones laid during these events. Home Minister Amit Shah will also hold organisational meetings and rallies in all six regions, along with inauguration and foundation-laying programmes. Party president Nitin Nabin will hold conferences of booth presidents, Shakti Kendra in-charges and mandal presidents. BL Santosh and Vinod Tawde will also visit all six regions and hold organisational meetings. These meetings will be used to gather feedback on campaigning in Assembly constituencies, caste equations, the position of sitting MLAs and the Opposition's standing. Special focus on social media The meeting also discussed setting the narrative on social media. The government's achievements and the organisation's work will be taken to the public through reels and posts. Allegations levelled by the Opposition will also be countered. In particular, a strategy will be developed to reach Gen Z and Gen Alpha through social media and counter the Opposition among these groups. State Working Committee meeting soon The BJP's state executive committee will be formed soon. The meeting also discussed the appointment of members to the committee. Once the members are appointed, a meeting of the state executive committee will be held. BJP national president Nitin Nabin or Home Minister Amit Shah is likely to address it. The meeting also called for the appointment of the party's district in-charges at the earliest so that they can visit their allotted districts and take charge of the work there. BL Santosh also stressed the need to form the state teams of the Yuva Morcha, Mahila Morcha, SC Morcha, ST Morcha, OBC Morcha, Minority Morcha and Kisan Morcha soon. This will enable the teams of all frontal organisations to become active in election preparations. Close eye on 134 seats in Awadh and Kanpur In the 2024 general election, the BJP suffered significant losses in the Awadh region, which has 82 Assembly seats, and the Kanpur-Bundelkhand region, which has 52 Assembly seats. This is why the central leadership has turned its full attention to these two regions. Central leadership has been continuously camping in UP The BJP's central organisation has been closely monitoring every major and minor development in Uttar Pradesh for the past few months. 4 July visit: Nitin Nabin and BL Santosh held marathon meetings in Lucknow with the Chief Minister and both Deputy Chief Ministers. During the visit, a coordination meeting was also held with NDA allies, Apna Dal (S), the Rashtriya Lok Dal, the Nishad Party and the Suheldev Bharatiya Samaj Party. Review meeting on 5 September: State in-charge Vinod Tawde reached Lucknow for a two-day visit and reviewed the organisation with office-bearers at the regional and state levels. Meeting with the core group on 11 September: BJP Uttar Pradesh in-charge Vinod Tawde and National General Secretary BL Santosh held a meeting with the core group at the party headquarters in Lucknow. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath was also present. The meeting lasted more than two hours and focused on preparing the roadmap for Mission 2027.

stories.title: Storm, rain lash Kanpur-Bareilly; roads flooded in Sambhal:Gomti water enters temples in Lakhimpur; rain alert in 66 districts
stories.summary: The monsoon has begun withdrawing from Uttar Pradesh. Rain fell in 10 cities, including Meerut, Sambhal, Moradabad and Bareilly, on Thursday morning. Winds blew at a speed of 40 km per hour in Kanpur, followed by heavy rain. Trees and poles were uprooted in several places, cutting off power in many areas. Bareilly also experienced strong winds. It rained so heavily in Sambhal that the roads turned into ponds. Water entered people's homes, and motorcycles parked in the lanes were half-submerged. Meanwhile, the weather is clear in more than 40 cities, including Lucknow, Varanasi and Prayagraj. However, clouds continue to move across the sky. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a rain alert for 66 districts today. Rivers are in spate because of the rain in the hills. Flood-like conditions prevail in 26 districts, affecting a population of 4 lakh. The water level of the Gomti river has begun rising in Lakhimpur Kheri. Sugarcane crops spread across hundreds of acres have been submerged. Water has entered the temple at Amri Ghat, and its stairs have been submerged. In Pilibhit, leopards have emerged from the forests. Lucknow meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh said- Over the next 24 hours, cloudy skies and rain are likely in several parts of the state. Light to moderate rain may occur, particularly in eastern Uttar Pradesh. Rainfall activity is likely to decrease in western Uttar Pradesh from 20 September. The weather will turn dry across the state from 22 September. See pictures of the rain and flooding…

stories.title: 2 festival special trains to run via Gorakhpur:Delhi-Gorakhpur-Bihar travel to get easier; check the full list
stories.summary: In view of the growing rush of passengers during the upcoming festivals, the railway has decided to operate two special trains via Gorakhpur. The first train will run between Anand Vihar Terminal and Muzaffarpur, while the second will operate between Delhi and Sitamarhi. Both trains will have reserved seating. The Anand Vihar-Muzaffarpur train will run twice a week, while the Delhi-Sitamarhi train will run once a week. This will provide additional convenience to passengers travelling between Delhi, Gorakhpur, Bihar and adjoining areas. 13 trips from Anand Vihar to Muzaffarpur Train 04028 Anand Vihar Terminal-Muzaffarpur twice-weekly reserved festival special will run from 13 October to 24 November every Tuesday and Friday. The train will make 13 trips during this period. The train will depart from Anand Vihar Terminal at 9:15 am. It will then reach Gorakhpur at 10:25 pm via Amroha, Moradabad, Bareilly, Shahjahanpur, Sitapur, Gonda and Basti. After departing from there, it will reach Muzaffarpur at 4:30 am the next day via Chhapra, Sonpur and Hajipur. Will run on Wednesdays and Saturdays on the return journey On the return journey, train 04027 Muzaffarpur-Anand Vihar Terminal will run every Wednesday and Saturday from 14 October to 25 November. The train will depart from Muzaffarpur at 6:15 a.m. and reach Gorakhpur at 12:55 p.m. via Hajipur, Sonpur and Chhapra. It will then reach Anand Vihar Terminal at 5:30 a.m. the next day via Basti, Gonda, Sitapur, Shahjahanpur, Bareilly, Moradabad and Amroha. Train to have 20 coaches The Anand Vihar-Muzaffarpur festival special train will have a total of 20 coaches. These will include one air-conditioned second-class coach, two air-conditioned third-class coaches, nine sleeper coaches, six general second-class coaches and two SLR coaches. Six trips from Delhi to Sitamarhi The second special train will be train 04010 Delhi-Sitamarhi weekly reserved festival special. It will operate every Thursday from 15 October to 19 November. The train will make six trips. The train will depart from Delhi at 11:05 p.m. It will reach Gorakhpur at 1:40 p.m. the next day via Ghaziabad, Moradabad, Bareilly, Shahjahanpur, Sitapur and Gonda. It will then reach Sitamarhi at 11:30 p.m. via Bagaha, Narkatiaganj, Sikta, Raxaul and Bairgania. Will run on Saturdays on its return journey On its return journey, train 04009 Sitamarhi-Delhi will run every Saturday from 17 October to 21 November. The train will depart from Sitamarhi at 12:45 a.m. and reach Gorakhpur at 7:50 a.m. via Bairgania, Raxaul, Sikta, Narkatiaganj and Bagaha. It will then reach Delhi at 8:30 p.m. via Gonda, Sitapur, Shahjahanpur, Bareilly, Moradabad and Ghaziabad. Sitamarhi Special to run with 21 coaches A total of 21 coaches will be attached to the Delhi-Sitamarhi Special train. These will include one LSLRD, four general second-class coaches, six sleeper coaches, four air-conditioned third-class economy coaches, two air-conditioned third-class coaches, two air-conditioned second-class coaches, one air-conditioned first-class coach and one generator-cum-luggage van. During the festive season, the number of passengers travelling on trains to Delhi and Bihar increases. The operation of these two special trains by the Railways will provide additional options to passengers travelling to Delhi and Bihar via Gorakhpur.

stories.title: Woman said, ‘We’ll break up, I need 2 months’:Old video surfaces of Lucknow woman run over by Shahnawaz
stories.summary: An old video has surfaced in the case involving a man allegedly running over his girlfriend with a car in Lucknow. The 36-second video shows the victim, Anamika Singh, with her boyfriend, Shahnawaz. The two can be seen talking, while Anamika is recording the video herself. However, it is not clear when the video was recorded. In it, she says: He is my boyfriend. He wants to leave me, but I don’t want that. I have told him to give me one or two months. I will leave him myself. If I don’t, then you can leave me yourself. Two separate videos of this conversation have surfaced. During the conversation, Shahnawaz talks about shaving his head, but the woman stops him. She says, “I went to him myself. It is not his fault. I asked for his number. I forcibly got his number from his phone. He was afraid that if he did not talk to me, I would beat him badly.” Police have also included these videos in their investigation. Regarding the ‘love jihad’ angle and the allegation that accused Shahnawaz befriended the woman while claiming to be Hindu, police said the videos suggest that the victim and Shahnawaz were in a relationship. The two knew each other. However, the two later had a dispute. Police are investigating whether the man had befriended the woman by concealing his religion. The woman will also be questioned. Meanwhile, Rachna Gautam, secretary of the Vishwa Hindu Raksha Parishad, said, “This is a case of ‘love jihad’. A high-level investigation should be conducted into accused Shahnawaz.” She said a memorandum would be submitted to the police in this regard. Earlier, Women’s Commission vice-president Aparna Bisht had said, Prima facie, this does not appear to be just a hit-and-run case. According to the victim, accused Shahnawaz was pressuring her to marry him. He had concealed his identity. The case appears to involve ‘love jihad’. Further investigation will be carried out. Attempted to run her over with a car The hit-and-run incident took place at around 6.30am on Wednesday (September 16) near Gate No. 4 of Janeshwar Mishra Park in Lucknow. A video related to the incident had surfaced. It showed Shahnawaz, who was driving the car, hitting the woman, causing her to become stuck on the bonnet. The woman kept screaming, but the accused did not stop the car. After driving another 20–25 metres, he increased the speed, causing her to fall onto the road. The accused then ran over her and fled the spot. Two versions have emerged about how the incident began First — Anamika had caught Shahnawaz with his new girlfriend. The two argued over this. When Shahnawaz tried to drive away in his car, Anamika stood in front of the vehicle to stop him. Shahnawaz then ran her over and fled. Second (as stated by the woman in the FIR) — “At around 6.30am, I had gone to have tea near Gate No. 4 of Janeshwar Mishra Park. During this time, Shahnawaz Ali arrived in a car with his friend Danish. Both of them asked me what I was doing there. They then started abusing me. Shahnawaz and Danish got into the car. Shahnawaz drove the car towards me with the intention of killing me and hit me. I was thrown onto the bonnet of the car. I held on to the windscreen wiper. Even then, I fell from the car. Shahnawaz then tried to run the car wheel over me. I lost consciousness after the incident. My younger sister, aunt and other people present at the spot picked me up. I was then taken to Dr Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital. Shahnawaz had also assaulted me several times in the past.” Eyewitness: She was screaming in pain An eyewitness had said that when the woman tried to stop the car, the accused hit her and fled. The woman suffered serious injuries and was screaming in pain. She was heard saying, “God, save me… I will die.” Family initially alleged he had posed as Yash Thakur Soon after the incident on Wednesday, the woman’s family had alleged that accused Shahnawaz had trapped her by introducing himself as Yash Thakur. They said he lived in the Dubagga area and worked as a contractor in Barabanki. However, police said the written complaint submitted by the victim does not mention this allegation. Shahnawaz tells police station: ‘I am being framed’ Shahnawaz told police, “I am being framed. The woman had been harassing me for the past 6–7 months and was following me. She had also taken money from me.” Police have also recovered the accused’s car. The word “Advocate” is written on its number plate. Police conduct Anamika’s medical examination Anamika, who was injured in the incident, underwent a medical examination on Wednesday evening. She was discharged after treatment at Dr Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital and returned home. After reaching home, she did not speak to anyone. Two videos key to the investigation Meanwhile, a case has been registered against Shahnawaz at the Gomti Nagar Extension police station based on her complaint, under charges including attempt to murder and other relevant sections. At present, the two videos have become key evidence in the investigation.

stories.title: Ganga floods hit livelihoods of thousands:Jobs submerged by rising Ganga in Banaras: Boats halt, priests’ stations lie deserted
stories.summary: These days, Banaras in Uttar Pradesh is in discussions due to the fierce form of Mother Ganga. The stairs of Dashashwamedh Ghat remained lost in Ganga for about a month. The place where thousands of devotees gathered every evening and echoed with the sound of hours and conch shells, there was only water everywhere. Although the water has started receding from the regular stage of the world-famous Ganga Aarti, mud still remains. Boats are lined up and tied with ropes at the bank of the ghats. Nearby, even fewer voices are heard, which are the identity of the ghats of Kashi in normal days. Voices like 'Will you take a boat?', 'Please take flower garlands', ‘Please perform puja’ are now silent. Standing on the banks of Ganga and looking around, another face of the flood is visible. The water has not only submerged the ghats, but it has also stopped the livelihood of thousands of families earning their daily living here. Spread over about six kilometers from Assi ghat in the south to Adi Keshav-Namo Ghat in the north, a large portion of Kashi's historic 84 ghats remained in the grip of water. Pedestrian connectivity between the ghats was broken. The conditions at Manikarnika and Harishchandra Ghat became such that for cremation rites, people had to shift towards elevated places, rooftops, and narrow lanes. Now, for the last two to three days, the water level has started decreasing. However, a large amount of silt has accumulated at many ghats including Assi Ghat and Tulsi Ghat. It is difficult even to set foot on the stairs of the ghat. According to the people of the ghat, it is the month of Bhado; the water level of Mother Ganga can increase again anytime. Boatmen said, 'Earnings have stopped, expenses haven't' At Rajendra Prasad Ghat, boatman Golu Sahani said, "About 7 thousand boats operate in Ganga. One boat provides employment to three to four people. As the boat stopped, the employment of 25 thousand boatmen-fishermen was snatched away. More than 1.25 lakh (125,000) people are dependent on them, who rely on Ganga." Moving a bit further, the wooden platforms (chauki) of the priests (Pandas) at the ghat also look deserted. Ghat priest Satyam Pandey tells that at 25 major ghats, more than 500 Pandas conduct daily worship, vows (sankalp), and religious rituals. Due to rising water, along with the Pandas and their dependent families, the livelihood of 30 thousand people was affected. From the second week of August itself, as the water increased, the connection between the ghats broke. Those who offer massages at the ghat, barbers, tea sellers, food item sellers, flower-garland sellers, and oil lamp sellers also face a two-month crisis every year. 'Came to Kashi after 11 years', ‘Wish for a boat ride remained incomplete’ Sudhanshu Puri, who came to visit after 11 years from Sitapur, says, "Got to have darshan of Baba Vishwanath and perform puja, but the wish to see the ghats of Kashi by boat remained incomplete." Thousands of tourists are coming to visit Kashi like this, but they cannot stay at the ghats. It will take time for life at the ghats to return to normal The administration has built 61 relief camps for flood victims. Among these, 22 are active. 16 wards-neighborhoods and 24 villages of Banaras have been affected by the flood. Several feet of silt and filth have accumulated on the ghats. Cleaning takes time. That is, even if the Ganga water recedes, it takes many days for earnings to return. Flood in Bihar as well, 50 lakh people affected across 15 districts Meanwhile, the threat of flood in Bihar has not passed either. Several rivers including Ganga, Gandak, Kosi, and Punpun are flowing above the danger mark. About 50 lakh population across 15 out of 38 districts of the state is affected by the flood.

stories.title: Mother missing for 9 years found on Lucknow road:Son hugged her and wept, said, ‘God heard my prayers’
stories.summary: Fifty-five-year-old Ratan Ben, who went missing from Gujarat in 2017, was reunited with her family in Lucknow nine years later. When her son Vishal met her, the two embraced and broke down in tears. Ratan Ben held her son’s hand and remained seated beside him for a long time. On Wednesday evening, Vishal left for Gujarat with his mother and thanked the police for helping trace her. One word helped police trace her family A few days ago, police found Ratan Ben walking alone on a road in Lucknow. During questioning, she was unable to provide details about herself or her family. The only word she repeatedly mentioned was “Fulpada”. Police searched for Fulpada on Google Maps and found a location in Gujarat. They then contacted the Gujarat Police and eventually traced Ratan Ben’s family, leading to her reunion with her son after nine years. Woman found distressed on road, unable to reveal identity Hazratganj police station in-charge Vikram Singh said, “A woman was found in a distressed condition on the road near Balu Adda a few days ago. She appeared to be mentally unwell, following which police personnel took her to the station.” He added, “Women police officers spoke to her and tried to establish her identity and address, but she could respond only in broken words. During the conversation, she mentioned the name ‘Phoolpada’.” Google Maps search helped police trace Gujarat link Police searched for ‘Phoolpada’ on Google Maps and found a locality with the same name in Gujarat. The Lucknow Police then contacted their counterparts in Gujarat and learnt that Ratan Ben had been reported missing there in 2017. Son stunned to see missing mother on video call The Gujarat Police contacted Ratan Ben’s family and learnt that her son, Vishal Jayeshbhai, lives at Viraj Palace in Phoolpada, Surat. He works with the Surat Municipal Corporation. On Tuesday (15 Sept), Hazratganj Police arranged a video call between Vishal and his mother. He was stunned when Ratan Ben appeared on the screen and struggled to believe that the mother he had been searching for nine years was in Lucknow. Mother and son break down after nine-year reunion On Wednesday (16 Sept), Vishal reached the Hazratganj police station in Lucknow along with Gujarat Police personnel, his friend Praveen and another person. Ratan Ben was seated in the station officer’s room when she saw her son and immediately began crying. Vishal stood looking at his mother for a few moments before embracing her and breaking down in tears. Ratan Ben held his hand tightly and did not let go for a long time. Police personnel then helped the mother and son regain their composure. Mother’s mental health deteriorated after deaths in family Vishal told police that his mother, Ratan Ben, went into deep shock after the deaths of her husband, Jayesh Bhai Rauthar, her maternal uncle and her maternal grandmother. Her mental condition deteriorated following the deaths. She had also left home once before 2017 but was traced and brought back a few days later. According to Vishal, Ratan Ben left home again after his marriage and the birth of his son. She never returned. The family searched for her at police stations, shelters and other possible locations across Gujarat but could not find any trace of her. Vishal later left for Gujarat with his mother.

stories.title: Neem Karoli Baba’s birthplace to be developed like Kainchi Dham:What will ‘Baba Circuit’ from Firozabad to Vrindavan look like?
stories.summary: The film 'Hanuman Ansh', based on Neem Karoli Baba, has earned around ₹291 crore in India and overseas. Made on a budget of just ₹2 crore, the film has further strengthened people’s faith in Baba after watching it. Until now, most people considered Kainchi Dham in Uttarakhand to be the main centre associated with Baba. However, the fact is that Baba was born, meditated and took Mahasamadhi, all on the sacred land of Uttar Pradesh. The Uttar Pradesh government has decided to improve places associated with Neem Karoli Baba. A grand corridor will be built at his birthplace in Firozabad. The five-acre area where he meditated will be developed for religious tourism. Let’s take a look at everything one by one. Firozabad — Birthplace: Grand corridor to be built According to tourism department official Vishal Srivastava, Neem Karoli Baba’s birthplace in Firozabad will be developed on the lines of Kainchi Dham. Around 87.5 bighas of land has been identified for this. The circle rate of the land has been increased to ₹69 lakh per hectare. Vishal Srivastava says a grand entrance gate will be built at the birthplace. A digital museum, an assembly venue, multi-level parking, a bhandara area, food court, interpretation centre, and meditation and wellness centres will also be developed. Kainchi Dham is located in the hills, so its setting may be different, but in terms of facilities, we also want to develop this site along similar lines. He said compensation four times the value of the land will be paid as per the rules. No one has raised any objection. Local villagers, including Baba’s grandchildren, have signed the NOC. The proposal has been sent for government approval. Once approval is received, the land purchase process will be completed, after which construction will begin. ₹12 crore work carried out at birthplace Neem Karoli Baba was born in 1900 in Akbarpur village of Firozabad. His childhood name was Lakshmi Narayan Sharma. From an early age, Lakshmi Narayan had a deep devotion to Lord Hanuman. He regularly performed prayers and worship. Lakshmi Narayan was a householder saint. He had two sons and a daughter. His sons, Aneka Sharma and Dharma Narayan Sharma, have passed away. His daughter Girija Bhatele is now elderly. All institutions associated with Baba are managed by Shri Thakur Hanuman Ji Trust, headed by Girija. Farrukhabad — Meditation site: Water pond to be built across 5 acres Baba meditated for around 12 years in Neeb Karori village (Sankisa) in Farrukhabad. He came to be known as 'Neem Karoli Baba' after the name of this village. There is also a railway station named Neeb Karori here. Since the release of 'Hanuman Ansh', the number of devotees visiting the site on Tuesdays and Saturdays has increased. Around 60,000–70,000 devotees are now arriving every day. The tourism department will develop a water pond across five acres here. Roads will also be widened after removing encroachments. Organised parking facilities will be created. A special childcare point will also be developed for mothers and children. Vrindavan — Samadhi site and temples to be developed The Uttar Pradesh government will also develop Neem Karoli Baba’s samadhi site in Vrindavan. Roads, better basic infrastructure and modern facilities for tourists will be expanded at the samadhi site and surrounding areas. Neem Karoli Baba took Mahasamadhi on the sacred land of Vrindavan on 11 September 1973, after which the complex was built. Besides Baba Neem Karoli Maharaj’s samadhi, the complex has grand temples dedicated to Lord Ram, Lord Hanuman, Goddess Durga and Lord Shiva. Bhandaras are also organised here for devotees. Lucknow — Hanuman Setu temple to be starting point of circuit The famous Hanuman Setu temple in Lucknow will be the starting point of the 'Neem Karoli Baba Circuit'. Located on the banks of the Gomti River, the temple was built under the inspiration of Baba Neem Karoli Maharaj. Guided tours by the Uttar Pradesh State Tourism Development Corporation Limited (UPSTDC) will start from here. Better seating, modern toilets, clean drinking water and a communication centre are being developed for devotees. The temple currently has two idols of Baba Neem Karoli and a grand idol of Lord Hanuman. Baba Neem Karoli Maharaj had called the Hanuman idol here the 'Governor General of all Hanumans'. It is said that during the construction of the bridge over the Gomti, its pillars kept collapsing repeatedly. Baba advised that a Hanuman temple should be built there. After the temple was constructed, the bridge was completed. Know 'Neem Karoli Baba Circuit' tour package The tourism department has created the 'Neem Karoli Baba Circuit' to connect the different stages of Baba’s spiritual journey. The circuit includes Firozabad (birthplace), Farrukhabad (meditation site), Lucknow (Hanuman Setu temple) and Vrindavan (samadhi site). The government has also prepared tour packages for the journey. UPSTDC has launched two-, three- and five-day tour packages from Delhi and Lucknow. The budget for a three-day/two-night tour ranges from ₹10,000 to ₹18,000, depending on the vehicle and facilities. Cars, Innovas and tempo travellers are available. Tourists can book through the tourism corporation’s official website, upstdc.co.in, or by contacting 9149099890.

stories.title: Will UCC be implemented in UP before elections?:What changes, will live-ins get legal status; BJP benefit or loss?
stories.summary: Following Home Minister Amit Shah's statement, speculation is rife regarding the implementation of the Uniform Civil Code (UCC) in UP. Prior to this, UCC has already been implemented in Uttarakhand. In Madhya Pradesh, Assam, and Gujarat, the bill is awaiting the President's assent after being passed. Currently, there is no law in UP regarding live-in relationships (cohabiting without marriage). Provisions related to this may be included in the UCC. Today in UP Explainer, read about when UCC might be implemented here, what is happening within the government regarding this, and whether live-in relationships will receive legal recognition in UP. Question-1: What will change if UCC comes to UP? Will live-in relationships get legal status? Answer: Rules related to marriage, divorce, property, and child adoption will become uniform for people of all religions. Apart from this, rules such as mandatory registration for live-in relationships may come into force. Its impact on the life of a common person can be understood as follows... (A) Marriage: Currently, men in the Muslim community are permitted to marry more than once. Once UCC comes into effect, a second marriage will not be permitted while the first wife or husband is still alive. Doing so will lead to imprisonment. A second marriage will only take place after a 'legal divorce' has been granted. It will be mandatory for individuals of every religion to register their marriage after getting married. There is no fixed age for marriage in Muslim Personal Law. A boy and girl are considered eligible for marriage upon attaining puberty (usually 15 years). Once UCC is implemented, it will be mandatory for the boy to be 21 years old and the girl to be 18 years old for marriage. (B) Divorce: Divorce rules will be identical for all religions. Under Sharia and Muslim Personal Law, Talaq-e-Ahsan, Talaq-e-Hasan, Khula, Mubarat, and divorce through a Qazi will be illegal. Nikah Halala will also be banned. Maintenance will also have to be paid to the woman after divorce. (C) Property: In all religions except Islam, daughters have an equal right to property under the law. However, according to personal law, a daughter receives half of the son's share in property. In simple terms, if a son gets ₹2, a daughter will receive ₹1. If a daughter is the only child, she receives half of the property. The remaining half is distributed among other relatives (such as paternal uncles). If there are multiple daughters but no son, two-thirds of the property is divided equally among all daughters. The remaining one-fourth goes to relatives. Once UCC comes into effect, daughters will have the exact same right to property as sons. (D) Child Adoption: According to Muslim Personal Law, an adopted child receives no share in property after the parents' death. The property is distributed among biological relatives. If parents wish to leave property to an adopted child, they must write a 'will' before their death. Even in this case, a maximum of only one-third (33%) of the property can be willed to the adopted child. Once UCC is implemented, an adopted child will receive all the rights that a biological child gets. (E) Live-In Relationships: Nothing can be said with certainty regarding this. However, looking at the UCC laws in Uttarakhand and Madhya Pradesh, there could be rules like these... Registration may become mandatory to live in a live-in relationship. If the age of the boy or girl is under 21 years, the government official will be able to send this information to the parents or guardians. If a couple is living together without registration, the police administration can investigate on its own or based on complaints from neighbours, local residents, or landlords. Written information about ending the relationship (breakup) will also have to be submitted to the government office. Under Madhya Pradesh's UCC law, a woman will be able to claim maintenance from her partner in the event of a breakup. A child born during a live-in relationship will be considered legitimate. The child will get full rights to the parents' property. Question-2: Can UCC be implemented before the elections? How will this benefit the BJP? Answer: Yes, the UP government can introduce the UCC Bill in the Assembly or announce it before the Model Code of Conduct comes into force. After being passed by the Assembly and receiving the President's assent, implementation takes a few months. However, its political use right before the elections is certain. The BJP's three largest core ideological promises were—construction of the Ram Temple, abrogation of Article 370, and implementation of UCC in the country. Two have been fulfilled. Moving towards the third promise right before the elections will allow the party to firmly return to its core agenda. This will completely consolidate the votes of its traditional supporters. A BJP MP told the news website 'The Federal'—"In the 2022 UP elections, there was apprehension of losing some seats due to various reasons, but we were confident about forming the government. This time too, we are fully confident of victory, but the SP-Congress alliance will make it a very tough contest." "SP and Congress will certainly react to UCC to appease their Muslim voters. Muslim organisations will also react. This will consolidate our Hindu vote bank, which always benefits the BJP." Senior journalist Siddharth Kalhans says—"The BJP fears losses due to issues like the Ram Temple donation theft, paper leaks, and unemployment. In such a scenario, they are floating the UCC issue to divert attention from these topics and polarise Hindu-Muslim votes." "Before the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, an attempt was made to polarise votes through the Ram Temple consecration, but the BJP did not benefit. People had grown weary of the Ram Temple issue. UCC has also been around for a long time. Therefore, it is difficult to say whether it will definitely benefit the BJP." Question-3: Why is the BJP introducing the UCC state by state instead of making a direct law through Parliament? Answer: It is not just about winning the UP elections. BJP insiders say that implementing the UCC state by state rather than across the whole country at once is a deliberate strategy. It can be understood as follows... According to the Constitution, both the Centre and the states have the power to enact laws on subjects falling under the UCC. Senior journalist Ratan Mani Lal explains—If the BJP were to introduce a central law on this, the entire opposition would unite at the national level and protests would erupt. The BJP does not have an absolute majority of its own in both houses of Parliament. Allied parties such as JDU and TDP have traditionally opposed the UCC. In such a scenario, there is no guarantee that the UCC Bill would pass in the current Lok Sabha. However, passing the law one by one in BJP-ruled states prevents the opposition from uniting. For instance, if the UCC is implemented in Bengal or Odisha, the SP will not protest, as it faces no political gain or loss there. Meanwhile, Congress is so preoccupied with internal friction that it will not be able to run a campaign against the UCC. The examples of Uttarakhand, Gujarat, Assam, and Madhya Pradesh are right before us. Once the UCC is implemented in most of these states, the Centre will formulate a central law to harmonise the various state legislation. This will also help the BJP persuade allies like the JDU and TDP. Question-4: What is the stance of the BJP's allies in UP regarding the UCC? Answer: All ally parties of the BJP in UP are in support of the UCC. Cabinet Minister and SBSP chief Om Prakash Rajbhar says that we believe UCC is necessary and in everyone's interest. During the time of NRC and CAA as well, the opposition raised several apprehensions. Now, no one even discusses them. Nishad Party President and Cabinet Minister Sanjay Nishad states that Muslim women will benefit the most from the UCC. They will receive equal rights and respect. In terms of numerical strength, the largest ally, Apna Dal, supported the UCC after consulting with everyone.

stories.title: Girl leaves home with boyfriend:Leaves note saying ‘Mummy-Papa, don’t look for me’: claims parents oppose their marriage; 5 girls go missing in 1 day
stories.summary: “Mom-Dad, don’t look for me. I am going to the same boy. I know you will never let me marry my boyfriend. If you want to see us happy, never try to find me.” A 15-year-old girl wrote these words in her school notebook before leaving home. The latest case is from the Khajni area of Gorakhpur. The girl’s brother filed a kidnapping case against the accused youth at Khajni police station on September 16. The elder brother said, “A local youth used to threaten to elope with my sister. He would say that he would take her away and marry her.” Meanwhile, on September 13, his sister left home in the afternoon without informing anyone. Despite extensive searches, she could not be found. The family then checked her school bag and found the note in which she had written that she was eloping with her boyfriend. The elder brother alleged that the youth had lured his sister into a relationship and taken her away. He said she could be in danger. This is not the first such case. Similar cases are being reported every day from Gorakhpur district’s 30 police stations. Four to five cases of girls leaving home are being registered at police stations each day. Police teams across the district are struggling to trace them. In most cases, police have to travel outside the city or even outside the state to find the missing girls. At the same time, only a small amount is provided for tracing them. Girls aged 13-14 also showing interest in marriage On August 22, two 13-year-old friends left their homes in the Gorakhnath area. Neither returned home by evening. After extensive searches failed to locate them, their families informed Gorakhnath police. Police registered an FIR and formed a team to trace the girls. The investigation found that both had boyfriends and had left home with them. Similarly, a 14-year-old girl from the AIIMS police station area left home with a local youth on September 16. Her family said they had gone to a relative’s house in Kushinagar. When they returned, they found that their daughter had left home. The girl’s mother told AIIMS police that her daughter was a minor and alleged that a local youth had lured her away on the promise of marriage. Police have registered a case and are searching for the accused. Such cases raise concerns about young teenagers becoming involved in relationships and thinking about marriage at an early age. September 16: Five cases of girls leaving home registered in one day First case: A 16-year-old girl from the Chilualtal police station area left home without telling anyone at 7am on September 14. Her father approached the police to report her disappearance. Second case: A 14-year-old girl from the Campierganj police station area left home on September 15. Her father told police that her mother had scolded her for going to school. She left home after becoming upset. Third case: A 17-year-old girl from the Bansgaon police station area left home on September 15. Her mother said they were travelling somewhere together in the morning when she stopped at Kaudiram bus stand to get some change for money. During this time, a boy from their village allegedly lured the girl away. Fourth case: A 19-year-old girl from the AIIMS police station area left home at 9:30 am on September 15. Her father told police that a boy from the same village had allegedly lured her away by promising to marry her. Fifth case: An 18-year-old girl from the Sikriganj police station area has been missing since September 14. Her mother told police that the girl had left home in the afternoon to go to the market but never returned. She alleged that a boy from the village had taken her away. Psychologist says today’s generation is dating and experiencing romance at a young age Psychologist Shweta Johnson said that during adolescence, the brain systems linked to emotions become more active and sensitive. At the same time, the parts of the brain responsible for planning, controlling impulses and understanding the consequences of decisions are still developing. She said that if a child constantly experiences criticism, comparison with others, excessive control or emotional distance at home, attention, affection and emotional support from outside can seem more attractive and important. Today’s generation is exposed to relationships, attraction, dating, romance and marriage-related content at a very young age. Short videos and other content on social media often show only the attractive and romantic side of relationships true love, ideal couples, sacrifice for love, eloping together and happy endings while failing to show the possible negative consequences. Help children understand how to identify manipulation It is not appropriate to dismiss the feelings of a 12-to-14-year-old girl as “false” or “just childish”. Her emotions can be real and intense for her. However, making a decision about marriage based on those emotions cannot be considered the same as making a mature and well-considered decision. It is not enough to simply tell children not to run away from home with someone. They also need to understand the difference between attraction and love, the characteristics of a healthy relationship, how to recognise manipulation and how to deal with their emotions in a safe and balanced way.

stories.summary: UP Assembly Election 2027: AIMIM के मुखिया असदुद्दीन ओवैसी ने उत्तर प्रदेश विधानसभा चुनाव को लेकर बड़ी बात कही है। न्यूज एजेंसी ANI से बातचीत के दौरान उन्होंने कहा- ‘यूपी असेंबली इलेक्शन नजदीक है। लेकिन यह 2014 का इलेक्शन नहीं होगा, न ही 2017, न 2019 का इलेक्शन, न 2022 का इलेक्शन। यह बिल्कुल अलग इलेक्शन होने वाला है। और बहुत चैलेंजिंग भी होगा क्योंकि BJP ने अपने किए वादे पूरे नहीं किए हैं। जब समाजवादी पार्टी पावर में थी, तो Y नॉर्म था। अब, T यहां नॉर्म है, और उससे आगे, गवर्नेंस गुड गवर्नेंस नहीं है। आपके (BJP) कानून राज में कई गरीब लोगों की जमीन छीन ली गई है। इसलिए, डेवलपमेंट के बहुत सारे इश्यू हैं। बिजली बहुत बड़ा इश्यू है। कोई फर्क नहीं है। पहले जो होता था वह यह था कि समाजवादी पार्टी की सरकार में एक अलग तरह की गुंडागर्दी होती थी। कोई और करता था। अब इनके सरकार में एक अलग तरह की गुंडागर्दी हो रही है। यह किसी के लिए भी आसान इलेक्शन नहीं होगा। यह होने वाला है। उत्तर प्रदेश में एक अलग चुनाव…SIT रिपोर्ट (राम मंदिर गबन मामले की) जनता के सामने क्यों नहीं आती? सरकार इसे क्यों नहीं जारी करती? और उन लोगों को बेल क्यों मिल रही है? उन्हें बेल कैसे मिल रही है? यह अजीब है। यह भी एक बड़ा मुद्दा होगा।’

stories.title: UP transfers 10 IAS officers:Amit Kumar Ghosh appointed additional chief secretary for higher education
stories.summary: The state government transferred 10 senior IAS officers on Sunday night. Following the displeasure expressed by Panchayati Raj Minister and Suheldev Bharatiya Samaj Party (SBSP) president Om Prakash Rajbhar, Anil Kumar was removed as the department's principal secretary and appointed principal secretary of the Food and Civil Supplies and Consumer Affairs Department. Meanwhile, Ashish Goyal, Additional Chief Secretary of the Energy Department and chairman of the Uttar Pradesh Power Corporation, was removed and appointed Additional Chief Secretary of the Labour and Employment Department. Energy Minister Arvind Kumar Sharma had not been getting along with Ashish Goyal over the power crisis that had continued in the state from the summer through the monsoon. At a meeting recently, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath reprimanded Ashish Goyal over the issue of power theft. The Chief Minister was also unhappy with his working style. Amrit Abhijat, a close associate and batchmate of Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath's Additional Chief Secretary Sanjay Prasad, has once again been given greater authority. Along with the charge of Additional Chief Secretary of the Tourism and Culture Department, he has also been given the charge of Additional Chief Secretary of the Transport Department. Meanwhile, relations between Higher Education Department Principal Secretary Mahendra Kumar Agrawal and his minister, Yogendra Upadhyay, had deteriorated over delays in scooter distribution and laxity in departmental functioning. The Chief Minister was also not very pleased. Therefore, Mahendra Kumar Agrawal has been removed from the Higher Education Department and appointed Principal Secretary of the Forest and Environment Department. Medical and Health Department Additional Chief Secretary Amit Ghosh has been transferred again, three and a half months before his retirement. He has been appointed Additional Chief Secretary of the Higher Education Department. See the list 10 IAS Transfers

stories.title: 60-65-year-old men became Class 6 students:Played gilli-danda at school; relived their childhood
stories.summary: Former students aged 60-65 returned to Agra's Government Inter College wearing Class 6 uniforms. Dressed in white shirts, black trousers and water bottles hanging around their necks, the friends relived their childhood days. While some ran through the school gate, others sat in the classroom and played pranks. These friends are retired IPS officers, doctors, accountants and teachers. The college's former students made the video around seven years ago to relive their school days. Rakesh, who shot the video, said, "Some parts of the video were uploaded on Instagram on Friday with a new voice-over. Since then, large numbers of people have been viewing and sharing it." Video made 7 years ago Rakesh, who lives in Raja Mandi Gokulpura, says the friends made this video around seven years ago, in 2019, for their YouTube channel, 'Bhoot Ka Anda'. The video received around 1,500 views at the time. Four days ago, parts of the video were reposted on Instagram with a new voice-over. Since then, large numbers of people have been watching and sharing it. The video shows the elderly friends, aged 60-65, entering the school through the gate wearing white shirts, black trousers, and water bottles hanging around their necks. All the friends played childhood games The video shows some friends running into their classroom, while others arrive dancing with their friends. They then appear playing childhood games on the school grounds. They play pitthu, also known as seven stones, and gilli-danda. The excitement on their faces while playing is the same as it was in their childhood. The video also shows the friends visiting the school corridors and classrooms and sitting on the benches. At times, they are seen having fun while holding each other's hands, and at other times, they form a train and run around the classroom. Some friends are also seen dancing to songs. The voice-over playing in the background talks about a friendship spanning nearly 50 years, childhood memories, and staying connected with friends. Now read how the group of friends was formed and where the idea for the video came from.... The group of friends was formed 10 years ago Rakesh Nagar said that about 10 years ago, his friend Keshav Sharma had created a WhatsApp group of former classmates. Gradually, other school friends also joined the group. It includes doctors, chartered accountants, bank and BSNL employees, businesspeople, and others who have worked in different fields. Rakesh said, "One day, I sent a script to the group for making a video about our old school memories." All the friends liked the idea. After this, preparations began to shoot at the school to relive their Class 6 days. After the teacher explained, they were allowed to shoot Rakesh said, "Initially, we were not allowed to shoot at the school. After that, teacher Dr Janak Singh Sisodia explained the entire matter to the principal. The shoot could take place after permission was granted. Dr Sisodia also appeared in the video with the friends." Rakesh said, "The video was shot at Government Inter College. Around 30 friends reached the school dressed like sixth-grade students. Some entered through the school gate, while others were seen sitting in classrooms and misbehaving as they had in the old days." He said that several of the friends featured in the video are now retired IPS officers, doctors, accountants and teachers. Some friends could not take part in the shoot. They included a DGP, an IPS officer, and Dr Arun, a neurosurgeon. Dr Arun joined his friends via video call. He said their group of friends is not limited to school memories. The friends organise an event every year. They also stand by one another during weddings and on occasions of happiness and grief. Enrolled at this school in 1971 Rakesh said, "I enrolled in Class Six at Government Inter College in 1971. I passed Class Ten in 1976. During my school days, I acted on stage and took part in programmes. After school, I worked in private jobs, at a bank and a private school. Since I had a good voice, people advised me to take up singing. I have been singing for several years now. I have a group called 'Karan Priya Music Event'. I have also written a book."

stories.title: Men posing as police officers kidnap businessman in Lucknow:They beat him while driving him to Agra and Kannauj, extort ₹13 lakh ransom
stories.summary: In Lucknow, six young men posing as police officers kidnapped an antique dealer. They held him hostage in a Scorpio and beat him at gunpoint. They forced him to call his wife and demand 15 lakh rupees, threatening to kill him if the money was not sent. On Sunday, eight days after the incident, the police arrested the six accused. Four of them are residents of Bulandshahr in UP, while two are from Bihar. The plot to kidnap the businessman was hatched in Patna, with one of the businessman's own partners involved. He had conducted reconnaissance around seven times over 20 days. Fake ID cards for an inspector, sub-inspector, and constables were recovered from the accused. They had made the businessman get into the Scorpio under the pretext of questioning him after showing him these fake ID cards. Now Read in Detail… Lucknow South DCP Mohammad Mushtaq stated that Sudarshan Ghosh lives in Saket Apartments in Rajendranagar, Alambagh. On 13 September, he lodged a complaint at the Krishnanagar police station. Sudarshan explained that he runs a large antique shop in Alambagh. On 12 September, while heading to his shop, several individuals posing as police officers forcibly bundled him into a vehicle. They intimidated him with weapons and beat him when he resisted. The hardened criminals kept him hostage in the vehicle for nearly nine hours, driving him along the routes between Lucknow, Agra, and Kannauj. They continuously issued death threats while demanding a ransom. Eventually, the businessman called his wife and asked her to bring the ransom amount to a location specified by the accused. The wife dispatched ₹13 lakh and some jewellery through their driver. The accused collected the ransom in Kannauj before abandoning the businessman on Shaheed Path and fleeing. Upon returning home, Sudarshan Ghosh recounted the entire ordeal to his family and lodged a case at the police station the following day. One Accused Was Close to the Businessman; He Gave the Signal for the Abduction During interrogation, the accused told the police that they committed robberies as a gang. The gang consists of people from different states. They used to target individuals who had a significant amount of money. Following this, they would conduct reconnaissance before executing the crime. According to the police, one of the youths involved in robbing the Lucknow businessman is from Patna. He is close to the businessman. He provided information regarding the businessman's financial status and movements to his accomplices. After this, they all stayed in Lucknow and carried out reconnaissance on the businessman. 3 Key Points— Asserted dominance using police ID cards: 4 police ID cards were recovered from the accused. They used to intimidate people using these very cards. The gang possesses several other vehicles: During questioning, the accused revealed that the Scorpio was not their only vehicle. The gang has several other vehicles. They used fake number plates on the vehicles to prevent the police from identifying them. After the crime, all the accused had scattered to different states. They had already divided the cash and jewellery obtained in Lucknow among themselves. Returned to Lucknow for another crime: The accused had returned to Lucknow to carry out their next crime. It was during this time that the police arrested them. Police action is ongoing regarding the role of other accused in the case and the recovery of the remaining jewellery and cash received as ransom. Scrutinised Over 220 CCTV Footages Eight police teams were formed to solve the case. The Surveillance Cell of the Southern Zone was also deployed for the investigation. Using roughly 220 to 240 CCTV footages, technical evidence, manual inputs, and the local intelligence network, the police teams identified the accused. The police have arrested six accused in the case. These include Anurag (26), Lavi Kumar (30), Deepanshu Kumar (24), and Akash Chaudhary (23), all residents of Shikarpur in Bulandshahr. Anurag Kumar (33), a resident of Muzaffarpur in Bihar, and Manish Kumar (24), a resident of Sonepur in Saran district, have also been arrested.

stories.title: Congress protests reduction in reservation at UP medical colleges:Rajendra Gautam says govt failed to present its case in court; gives 24-hour ultimatum
stories.summary: UP Congress in-charge Rajendra Pal Gautam has held the present government responsible for the stay on the SC-ST reservation implemented in four government medical colleges in the state. He said that due to the government's laxity and weak representation in the High Court, the rights of students from the Dalit community are being infringed upon. He has warned the government to clarify its position on the entire matter within 24 hours. Rajendra Pal Gautam claimed that there were a total of 200 seats in the medical colleges of Ambedkar Nagar, Kannौज, Jalaun, and Saharanpur. The construction and operation of these four colleges were not funded by the general budget, but by funds from the 'Special Component Plan' (SCP) earmarked for Scheduled Castes. Since the money came from the Dalit Welfare Fund, 70% of the seats were reserved for students from the SC-ST category under the rules. Gautam alleged that during the hearing in the High Court, instead of advocating for the 70% reservation, the government's lawyer spoke only of the standard 21% reservation. ‘How Did the Verdict Come Without Hearing the Affected Students?’ The Congress leader raised questions about the High Court’s procedure and the government’s lukewarm attitude. He said that the students whose futures were set to be impacted by this decision were not even given a hearing in court. The matter is currently pending before the Division Bench of the High Court. According to Gautam, the government must immediately take legal steps and demand a stay on the Single Bench’s order. Allegation of Irregularities in Scholarship and Fee Funds Gautam also raised the issue of irregularities in the scholarship and fee money for Dalit students. He said that earlier, the fees of SC students taking admission to professional and higher education were directly sent to the institutions through the government system. Now, students are forced to pay the full fee out of their own pockets first, after which the process for scholarships and fee reimbursement begins. As a result, students from poor families are unable to pay the fees and are forced to drop out midway. The Congress has announced a state-wide agitation regarding this issue. ‘Comments on Rahul Gandhi’s Mother Are Inappropriate’ He expressed displeasure over the statements made by BJP leaders regarding Rahul Gandhi’s mother, Sonia Gandhi. Gautam said that families of leaders, especially mothers, should not be dragged into political battles. Regarding the party’s election strategy, he said that the state president and the in-charge will tour different regions. Six AICC (All India Congress Committee) secretaries have been assigned responsibility for different areas so that the entire state can be covered in a short period.

Following this, SP chief Akhilesh Yadav held a press conference. He announced that in the 2027 elections, the SP will work to increase its tally by 27,000 votes in every assembly constituency and reduce the BJP's votes by the same number. During this, Akhilesh raised questions about the BJP government regarding the desecration of Babasaheb Ambedkar's statues, unemployment, paper leaks, and land scams. Apart from this, there are several undocumented cases as well, which failed to make the news. They want to change the Constitution. That is why they are attacking the very Constitution held in Babasaheb’s hands. The BJP’s intentions have never been in favour of reservations and the Constitution.” Youth left unemployed under the BJP government "The highest number of paper leaks in the country occurred in Uttar Pradesh so that the government would not have to give government jobs to the youth. Under the BJP government, jobs have vanished and reservations have been tampered with. “Land was taken from farmers, but they were not given proper compensation by increasing the circle rate. Ayodhya stood as an example of the large scale on which land scams took place there. Despite attempts to vitiate the atmosphere, the party is grateful to our Muslim brothers for the patience, brotherhood, and goodwill they displayed.” Not Even 10% PDA Representation Among Election Officials Akhilesh Yadav raised questions about the administrative preparations for the elections as well. Akhilesh referred to Deputy CM Keshav Prasad Maurya as 'Dapte CM' (reprimanded CM). He asked who was calling him eccentric. stories.title: SP leaders clash in Akhilesh's presence:Party chief says they have grown arrogant with money, expels them from meeting
stories.summary: Two Samajwadi Party leaders clashed in front of SP chief Akhilesh Yadav. After a heated argument, they began hurling abuses at each other. Akhilesh became angry on seeing this and had both leaders, Manjeet Yadav and Jugendra Yadav, removed from the meeting. Akhilesh said angrily, "They are all senior leaders. Ask these people for advice. Go and do whatever you want to do. When a person keeps refusing to listen to the party and has poor conduct, who are we supposed to take it out on... tell me. It's all right, these things happen. It is all arrogance caused by money. Remember, whoever ends up with more money will leave you and go." After this, Akhilesh Yadav left the meeting. An hour later, the party units in both Etah and Kasganj districts were dissolved. The entire incident took place during a meeting at the SP office in Lucknow on Saturday. However, a video of it emerged today. Manjeet and Jugendra exchanged abuses during Samajwadi Party meeting Akhilesh had called the meeting to discuss the party's position in Etah and Kasganj districts and preparations for the Assembly elections. A total of 250 leaders and office-bearers from both districts were present. Akhilesh was seeking information from the leaders about the election preparations and the organisation. During the meeting, Samajwadi Party leader Manjeet Yadav, nephew of former Legislative Council chairman Ramesh Yadav, began speaking about the party's position in the previous elections and the reasons for its defeat. After this, former Etah district panchayat chairman Jugendra Singh Yadav stood up to speak. Manjeet Yadav objected to some of the words used by Jugendra Singh Yadav. A heated argument then broke out between the two. The leaders present at the meeting tried to defuse the situation, but neither of them calmed down. Before long, the two began hurling abuses at each other. This made the atmosphere at the meeting uncomfortable. Angry, Akhilesh Yadav told both leaders to maintain discipline, but neither of them complied. The SP chief then lost his temper.

stories.title: Father dies after hearing of son's death:He collapsed in Prayagraj, family splashed water on him but he did not get up
stories.summary: In Prayagraj, a 52-year-old father died after hearing that his son had passed away. The 28-year-old man was killed in a car collision at around 10:30 p.m. on Saturday. About an hour later, at 11:30 p.m., his daughter told her father, "My brother is no more." On hearing the news, the father clutched his chest and collapsed to the ground. Seeing this, the daughter screamed. The family splashed water on the father's face to revive him. When he did not regain consciousness, they took him to hospital, where doctors declared him dead. The doctors said he had suffered a heart attack. The incident took place in the area under Soraon police station, around 35 km from the district headquarters. Now read the full story... The son had gone to visit relatives and was returning at night Sister received the news of her brother's death The police reached the spot at around 11.00 pm. With the help of local people, they took Shivam to a private hospital in Prayagraj. Shivam died during treatment. At around 11.30 pm, the police took the mobile phone from Shivam's pocket and called his family. His sister Sunita answered the call. The police told her that Shivam had died in an accident. As soon as she heard the news of her brother's death, she began crying loudly. Weeping, she went to her father, who was sleeping outside the house. She told him that her brother was no more and had died in an accident. As soon as he heard this, Ram Singh also let out a loud cry. He suffered severe chest pain after hearing the news of his son's death Father Ram Singh got up from the charpoy, crying. As he stood up, he suffered severe chest pain and collapsed on the floor. His family tried to revive him. When he failed to regain consciousness, they took him to a private hospital in Shantipuram, where doctors declared him dead. Road blocked and protest staged Police searching for absconding driver Soron Station House Officer Deendayal Singh said the absconding driver was being traced based on the car's registration number. A case has been registered under the relevant sections based on the family's complaint. Police are taking further legal action in the matter.

stories.title: FIR against girls for abusing MP Chandrashekhar:Said, ‘Scared to come to Gonda? Mend your ways; abused you, will do it again… not afraid of cases’
stories.summary: FIR has been registered against two girls from Gonda for allegedly abusing MP Chandrashekhar Azad. They are accused of releasing a video containing abusive remarks after the MP's visit to Gonda was cancelled on 17 September. In the video, one of the girls says, "Why didn't you come to Gonda? Were you scared? Mend your ways. If you have the courage, come to Gonda and show it." They said, "We have hurled abuses and will continue to do so. Brahmins are always superior. They will always be called superior. I am Pallavi, and this is Kajal. She has four cases against her and I have 22 cases. What difference would one more FIR make? We are not afraid of cases." A video of Pallavi Shukla and Kajal Singh emerged on 18 September. Ramkishun Kohli, a former Bhim Army office-bearer, posted the video on social media that day and demanded police action. Following this, Sub-Inspector Yogendra Yadav registered a case at Kauria police station at around 11:30 pm on Saturday night. Kajal (30) and Pallavi (20) are both social media creators and live separately from their families. Five cases have been registered against Kajal. She is married but lived separately from her husband. Pallavi had previously commented on Chandrashekhar, and a case had also been registered against her. Now, understand the full case Chandrashekhar Azad was scheduled to visit Gonda on 17 September to meet the family of businessman Vinod Sahni, who was killed. However, he suddenly cancelled his visit. Earlier, on 13 September, he had also been travelling to Gonda, but the police turned him back from Barabanki. During this, Chandrashekhar's supporters and the police also jostled with each other. After his visit was cancelled on both occasions, Pallavi Shukla posted a video on 18 September. In it, she is seen with Kajal. Kajal says that neither of them is afraid of the case, nor will they ever be. She says, "You already know about our influence. Chandrashekhar Azad Ravana was coming to Gonda district, but he did not come. Did he get scared? Chandrashekhar Ravana, mend your ways. We oppose you.
