stories.title: Suspended Jal Kal EE in Varanasi blames civic body:Minister suspended him over waterlogging; says pumps stopped due to flood
stories.summary: Varanasi Jal Kal's suspended executive engineer (EE) has questioned the action taken by Urban Development Minister AK Sharma. He said the waterlogging was caused by the Municipal Corporation's negligence, but he was made the scapegoat. The pump was shut down on 20 August after correspondence. This is done every year because of flooding. If everyone knew about this, how could it be my fault? Following his claim, Dainik Bhaskar visited the 140 MLD pump house in Chaukaghat to understand how it operates. It also tried to find out where the negligence occurred and whether the Jal Nigam or the Municipal Corporation was more responsible. Read the report... Pictures of the pump house Now read what suspended Executive Engineer (EE) Pawan Kumar Gupta said and what questions he raised... Pawan Kumar Gupta, who was posted at the 140 MLD pumping station in Chaukaghat, has now been attached to Kanpur. An inquiry is under way against the Jal Nigam EE. Speaking over the phone from Kanpur about his suspension, he raised a major question and said, Why is action being taken against a Jal Nigam engineer for the Municipal Corporation's negligence? The grounds for the suspension are not valid EE Pawan Kumar Gupta said, The grounds on which I was suspended are not valid. The reality is something else, but the issue has been diverted elsewhere. Sewers in the city are clogged, which is causing waterlogging. They do not have the resources to prevent waterlogging. Action was taken against us to conceal this fact, even though we operated the pumps. Chaukaghat pumping station built near the Varuna river Pawan Kumar Gupta said, The pumping station at Chaukaghat is near the Varuna river. This time, the Varuna's water level reached 71 metres. The entire area was waterlogged. Several times, Varuna's water has also entered the pump house. In such a situation, when we run the pumps, will we be able to pump out Varuna's water? Why has the water level of the Varuna risen? In such a situation, no matter how much we pump, it will not make any difference. So how will the sewage water be pumped out? They are accusing us to conceal their own shortcomings The suspended executive engineer said, All the sewers of the municipal corporation are choked and full. This is causing waterlogging in the city. To hide their own shortcomings, they have blamed us and said that the pump is not working. But when the Ganga's water level has risen, the pump cannot do anything. A large pumping station and a retaining wall should be built here. This is meant for sewage pumping, but they are making us pump floodwater. Find out what Ajay Kumar Sinha, the site in-charge of the Chowkaghat pumping station, said, Sewage from several parts of the city goes to the STP from here Ajay Kumar Sinha said, This is a 140 MLD sewage pumping station (urban). It mainly handles sewage collected from several places. Sewage lines from Phulwaria, the Cantonment, Lahurabir and several other parts of the city have been connected here. We pump it from here, separate the garbage and pump it to the STP. Primary treatment is carried out here before the sewage is sent for treatment. The garbage is then separated, after which it goes directly to the STP. Pumping stations are shut down during floods Ajay further said, This pumping station is related to river pollution. It was built to prevent the river from being polluted. The water from the city's drains and sewers used to flow into the rivers. It has to be intercepted and sent to the STP from here. This area lies along the Varuna, and when flooding occurs, the water level rises and the river merges with the drains. In such a situation, pumping is stopped so that no problem is caused in the river. We will not be able to treat that water because treating the river water and releasing it back into the river would serve no purpose. Letter issued on 20 August itself Ajay said that all pumping stations along the riverbanks are shut during floods. This station is operational. It is shut during floods, but when there is no flooding, it is not shut. This time, when the Ganga's water level rises above 68 metres, the line to this 140 MLD pump station is closed because of the reverse flow from the Varuna. Water from the Varuna then begins flowing into it. This year too, as in the past, our executive engineer received an order from the Dinapur STP stating that the river and drain had met on 20 August. It should therefore be shut and maintenance work carried out. It should be restarted once the water level falls. Heard of this for the first time in six years According to Ajay, this is the first time in six years that it has come to light that the closure of the SPS has caused waterlogging somewhere in the city. This is a new issue for us as well, so it is impossible to say anything at this stage. According to the documents and records available to us so far, whenever floodwater has arrived, not only this station but all pumping stations along the Ganga in the city have shut down.

stories.summary: The Maharashtra Teacher Eligibility Test (TET) papers were smuggled out of a printing press in Agra, Uttar Pradesh, hidden inside the soles of shoes. This has been revealed in Thane Police's 3,500-page charge sheet. The accused were paid ₹8,000 in return for taking the papers out. They were also promised land plots in Agra. Thane Police filed the charge sheet in the local court in Bhiwandi on Friday. Eighteen people, including mastermind Bijendra Gupta, have been named as accused. Gupta's name had earlier surfaced in a paper leak case in Odisha. Sixteen accused have been arrested, while Ashok Saw and Prakash Misal are absconding. The paper was leaked a day before the TET examination scheduled for 28 June. Following this, the Maharashtra State Examination Council (MSEC) postponed the examination. The papers were leaked from Agra's Mahim Patran Private Limited printing press DCP Pawan Bansod received information that three people were trying to sell the examination papers to a man from Bhiwandi. The police then arrested the accused in the Kongao area. They recovered four sets of the papers from them. Officials of the Maharashtra State Council of Examination (MSCE) confirmed during the investigation that the papers were genuine. According to the charge sheet, the papers were leaked from Agra's Mahim Patran Private Limited printing press. Confidential papers for the TET examination were being printed at this press. Between 15 and 17 June, two press employees and a former employee folded the pages of the papers and hid them in the soles of shoes. At the printing press, security guards searched the suspects' clothes but did not check their shoes. The suspects took advantage of this and smuggled the papers out. Four separate sets of the two TET papers had been prepared to prevent cheating in the examination. One of these sets was to be used on the day of the examination. The suspects had taken all four sets out of the printing press. What is the TET examination? The Teacher Eligibility Test, or TET, is a national-level eligibility examination that determines whether a candidate is qualified to become a teacher for primary and upper-primary classes, from Class 1 to Class 8. The National Council for Teacher Education (NCTE) made the examination mandatory in 2010. The Centre conducts Central TET, while states conduct State TET. The NCTE gave candidates appointed to teaching posts five years to qualify the TET, which was later reduced to four years. Candidates approached the court against the NCTE notice. In June 2025, a Madras High Court bench said that teachers appointed before 29 July 2011 would not be required to pass the TET to remain in service, but passing the TET would remain mandatory for promotion. The matter later reached the Supreme Court from different states. 2 September 2025: Supreme Court orders, ‘Teachers must pass the TET’ The Supreme Court said on 2 September last year that teachers must pass the TET (Teacher Eligibility Test) to remain in service or receive a promotion. A bench of Justice Dipankar Datta and Justice Manmohan said that all teachers with more than five years of service remaining would come under the rule. The court extended the deadline for passing the TET from 31 August 2027 to 31 August 2028. Those who fail to pass the TET will have to either resign or take compulsory retirement. The court issued these directions while exercising its special powers under Article 142.

stories.title: UP MLA Pooja Pal duped of ₹1.55 lakh:Money withdrawn via PhonePe; says personal data also at risk
stories.summary: Around ₹1.55 lakh was fraudulently withdrawn from the bank account of Pooja Pal, MLA from the Chail constituency in Kaushambi and BJP State Vice-President. The amount was deducted in multiple transactions between 22 August and 13 September via PhonePe and UPI. The MLA came to know about this on 14 September. Upon inspecting her bank account statement, several transactions were uncovered that had been executed without her knowledge. Following a complaint lodged by the MLA, an FIR was registered at the Dhoomanganj police station in Prayagraj on Friday at 2 pm. Money withdrawn multiple times over 22 days The MLA, Pooja Pal, holds an account with the Union Bank of India branch in Dhoomanganj, Prayagraj. She informed the police that money was fraudulently withdrawn from her account multiple times between 22 August and 13 September. The MLA suspects that someone hacked her iPhone 17 Air and misused her banking and personal data. The police, with the assistance of the cyber cell, are examining the mobile device, PhonePe, UPI, and bank account details. Demand for investigation into transactions and mobile device The MLA has requested the cyber crime police to conduct an investigation into all PhonePe and UPI transactions made between 22 August and 13 September. She has urged for a technical audit of her mobile phone, along with a review of all transaction IDs and bank account details. Furthermore, the MLA has demanded that future unauthorized withdrawals from her account be prevented and that the stolen sum of approximately ₹1.55 lakh be recovered. Copies of the complaint have also been submitted to the Cyber Crime Police Station in Prayagraj, the Dhoomanganj Police Station, and the manager of the concerned bank branch. The police are currently investigating the matter.

stories.title: SP MP’s car pelted with stones, windows smashed:Chaos during Ganesh Visarjan in Sant Kabir Nagar; people angry over DJ's detention
stories.summary: In Sant Kabir Nagar, a crowd vandalised the vehicle of SP MP Laxmikant alias Pappu Nishad during the visarjan of a Ganesha idol. The mob surrounded the vehicle and smashed its window. Police safely evacuated the MP from the crowd. The incident occurred on Friday night at around 11 pm. The visarjan procession had reached the Amardobha crossing. Meanwhile, the police began taking the DJ to the police station. Outraged by this, people sat on the road in protest. Just then, the MP's vehicle was passing through the area. The angry crowd surrounded his vehicle and vandalised it. Following the incident, a heavy police force was deployed in the area. Additional Superintendent of Police Sushil Kumar Singh and the Additional District Magistrate arrived at the spot and reasoned with the people. The incident took place within the jurisdiction of the Bakhira police station area. The MP stated, “All three of my vehicles were vandalised and stones were pelted. The miscreants are protected by the ruling party. They attacked after seeing the party flag and because I belong to a lower caste. Upper-caste people cannot tolerate how a man from a lower caste became an MP. A life-threatening attack was made on me.” A DJ was accompanying the visarjan procession According to local residents, the Ganesha idol visarjan procession had set off from Bakhira town. The procession was heading towards Dhodhaya Canal via Amardobha. Just then, Mehndawal CO Sarvdaman Singh arrived at the spot. It is alleged that the CO took photographs of the DJ vehicle accompanying the procession and spoke of taking it to the Bakhira police station. Outraged by this, the people participating in the procession sat on the road in protest. It was during this time that the mob attacked the MP's vehicle. Following the attack on the MP's vehicle, the occupants inside it were also enraged. They sat on the road and raised slogans against the police and administration. Officers from the police and administration reached the spot and brought the situation under control. The MP stated: Stones were pelted after seeing the party flag The MP said, "I was returning after meeting flood victims and other people. I was stuck in a traffic jam at the crossing. Just then, slogans of 'Pappu Nishad Murdabad' started being raised. Seeing the party flag, people began hurling bricks and stones at the vehicle. I got out of the car and ran towards the market to save my life. When the police saw the vehicles being vandalised, they resorted to a lathi charge. I somehow reached the police station and went home from there."

stories.title: Lucknow’s Papermill Colony has cleanest air in India:70 parks; residents formed groups, planted trees with own money
stories.summary: An unique initiative by residents of Lucknow's Paper Mill Ward has made the entire city proud. The residents formed groups, raised funds and created gardens in every home. The ward is numbered 70 in the municipal corporation. Working with the municipal corporation, they built 70 parks across the area. The project took around 20 years. But the results have now emerged. Paper Mill secured the number one rank in the Ministry of Environment's Air Survey 2026. This means its air is the cleanest in the country. The residents have created vertical gardens in the parks and planted trees using the Miyawaki method. Waste in the ward is collected only using electric vehicles. As a result, air pollution here is nearly zero. The ward has a population of around 60,000. Residents here say, The title of having the cleanest air in the country was not achieved in a single day. We worked hard for years to achieve it and paid attention to cleanliness. This result has come from caring for the ward together. How is the air in the ward so clean? To find out, a Bhaskar reporter surveyed the neighbourhoods. The survey found that the ward has remarkable greenery. It has beautiful parks, trees along the roads and no piles of rubbish anywhere. Homes of all sizes have gardens. The drains are clean, and the roads are free of dust. Five pictures of the ward with the cleanest air in the country- Extent of Papermill Colony Ward: Residents said: Prabha Chaturvedi also contributed to this recognition Prabha Chaturvedi, a resident of the ward, is no longer alive, but people are now praising her work after the ward received the honour. Residents say Prabha had launched a campaign to increase greenery in the ward. Shekhar Malviya said people here had developed the area using their own money. Prabha Chaturvedi was among them. Her efforts transformed the condition of the parks. People became aware of environmental issues. The ‘Greenery in Every Home’ campaign was launched. Work was undertaken on rainwater harvesting and making compost through kitchen-waste management. She initiated these efforts along with providing training. She also worked with women on cleanliness. She died in 2021 during the coronavirus pandemic, but people are now remembering her work. Her family currently lives abroad. 3 major reasons behind the country's cleanest air title Vertical gardens and Miyawaki gardening reduced air pollution Vertical gardens, plantation along roads and riverbanks, and forests developed using the Miyawaki method are being created in the ward to reduce air pollution. Urmila Van and Shakti Van are among the prominent ones. Encroachments and garbage are being removed along the Kukrail river, after which plants are being planted using the Miyawaki method. These forests have improved the air quality in the ward. They have also enhanced the beauty of the area. The parks have been landscaped properly. Better maintenance has further improved their appearance. This has increased the greenery in the area and cleaned the air. Water is sprayed every day to prevent dust from becoming airborne Water is sprinkled daily in the ward to prevent PM-10 pollution particles generated by road dust. As part of efforts to raise awareness, nets are installed at construction sites to contain construction and demolition waste. These nets are later removed properly. Roads within the ward are cleaned more effectively. All major roads are cleaner. In addition, the drains and smaller open drains are covered. PNG lines have been installed for clean fuel in large parts of the ward, including Nehru Enclave and Vishwas Khand. LPG is also used in homes across the ward. Electric vehicles collect waste, with real-time tracking through GPS Electric vehicles (e-auto tippers) have been introduced in place of the old diesel waste-collection vehicles. GPS has been installed in all the vehicles, and a control command centre has been set up for their real-time monitoring. This has improved waste collection in the ward. Waste is no longer piling up inside homes or on the roads. It is not dumped in the open. Waste is collected at only two compactor stations. These are located at Mithaiwala Chauraha and Metro City police outpost. Dustbins have also been placed at various locations in the neighbourhoods. Sewer and water pipelines have been laid throughout the ward, providing convenience to residents. What residents of the ward with the cleanest air have to say- The councillor heeds the elderly, while residents contributed their own money Shekhar Malviya said that for the past several years, elderly residents have been sitting on chairs by the roadside with the councillor from the morning and informing him about the work that needs to be done. Local councillor Rajesh Singh Gabbar implements it. There is greenery around every house here. The colony is old. Its residents have improved it with their own money, so work has continued to be carried out. This is not a one-day effort. Residents work themselves to keep the ward clean Girish Chandra Tiwari said that our ward ranked number one in the country. The biggest reason for this is the parks in our area. They are all clean and well-maintained. People here keep the areas around them clean and tidy. They work towards this themselves. The parks have facilities ranging from exercise equipment to other amenities, which help people stay close to nature. People are called out when they make mistakes; the change did not happen in a day Swati said that the people in her ward are hardworking. No other ward has as much greenery as this colony. The reason the colony is clean and beautiful is that everyone is working towards this with awareness. If anyone makes a mistake, they are stopped from doing so. Residents are also partners, but sanitation workers deserve praise Hemendra Singh Rawat said, I have been living in the colony for 60 years. Relentless efforts have been under way for 20 years. Work has been carried out for the ward since Rajesh Singh became the councillor. The public also contributes to these efforts. Construction and demolition waste is being stored properly. Besides us, we congratulate the workers who work from morning to keep the city clean. Councillor says - made possible by public awareness Rajesh Singh Gabbar, councillor for the Papermill Colony ward, said, Under the National Clean Air Programme (NCAP), the Papermill Colony ward has been ranked No. 1 in the country among wards with a population of more than 30,000 in the Swachh Vayu Survey 2025-26. This has been made possible by the cooperation and awareness of the people in the area. It was my dream for our ward to become the most beautiful ward in the country, with clean air and cleanliness. That has now become possible. I am grateful to all the people for this. For the past 20 years, the people have been guiding me. We have all continued to work together accordingly. This is why we have received this distinction. Congratulations to everyone. Three more pictures of the ward-

stories.title: Ayush says, ‘I will marry Chandni at any cost’:Court approves marriage; her family says they were framed in Shamli
stories.summary: Ayush Malik, a resident of Shamli, told the Allahabad High Court that he had embraced Islam of his own free will. Ayush also expressed his desire to marry his girlfriend, Chandni Qureshi. The court permitted him to do so and said, An adult cannot be prevented from making decisions regarding their religion, residence and choice of life partner solely on the grounds of family opposition. Ayush's father is a prominent medicine trader in the city. A photograph of Ayush wearing a skullcap and offering namaz had gone viral. Hindu organisations protested after this. Ayush's father accused Chandni Qureshi of forcing him to convert. The police also sent several people, including Chandni and her father, to jail. After the court's ruling, Dainik Bhaskar spoke to Chandni's family. Read the report... Chandni's aunt's sons were also sent to jail Our team reached the home of Chandni Qureshi, who lives in Azad Chowk. We met Chandni's sister there. She said their father had gone to the market and that her elder sister was in Noida. Chandni's aunt's house is 100 metres from their home. Her aunt's son Mohammed Salim, her brother Tausif and some neighbours were sitting there. Tausif was also sent to jail in this case. Mohammad Salim said, Chandni is my maternal uncle's daughter. The Bharat Medical Store is 2 km from her home. Devraj Malik's son, Ayush Malik, used to sit there. There is a hospital next door where Chandni worked as a physiotherapist. Ayush used to bring his mother there. Ayush was the one who tried to trap Chandni. Maternal cousin said: Ayush trapped Chandni Mohammad Salim said that Chandni had made it clear from the outset: ‘We are Muslims. You are Jats. We have nothing to do with you and no relationship with you. Nor do we want any ties with you.’ Despite this, Devraj Malik had us framed as part of a conspiracy. He used Chandni as a pawn. He had us falsely implicated and sent to jail. He dragged not only us into the case, but also the family's elder paternal uncle, younger paternal uncle, maternal aunt's sons and the entire family. What is our fault? If we had even the slightest role or fault in this case, they could have shot us at a crossroads. Salim said - If she had wanted to frame him, she could have had a court marriage Salim said that if Chandni had really wanted to frame Ayush, she could have had a court marriage with him, but she did not do so. The boy had been converting to Islam and growing a beard for 12 years - did his father and family not know about it? Even the brothers and paternal aunt's sons have been framed in the case. How could people who cannot sign arrange a nikah? We have been rendered homeless. The locks on our house were broken and the police and administration were let inside; people entered the house by jumping from the roof. This is outright oppression against poor people like us. If the same oppression had happened to someone else, what would they have gone through? Shamli SP Narendra Pratap Singh said that the matter is before the court. The police are not intervening in the matter at present. Action will be taken if any complaint is received. Now, know the full story Devraj Malik, a resident of Dayanand Nagar, is the president of the Chemists Association in Shamli district. He owns a house in the city's upscale area and two well-known medical stores in the city. His two daughters are married. His son, Ayush Malik, ran a medical store after completing a BPharm. On 6 June, Devraj Malik lodged a report at the Kotwali police station. He alleged that Chandni Qureshi had lured his son into a relationship and had him converted. She had his name changed to Mohammed Ali. Ayush had suddenly started changing his appearance. He first grew a beard and then began going to the mosque. A photograph of Ayush also surfaced, showing him offering prayers at a mosque. He was seen sitting at the medical store wearing a skullcap and a kurta-pyjama. FIR filed after protests by Hindu organisations Swami Yashveer, the mahant of Yog Sadhana Ashram, released a video. He said that Chandni Qureshi had trapped the only son of the owner of Bharat Medical Store. Under pressure, the entire family had converted to another religion. After the matter came to light, Hindu organisations began protesting and threatened to stage a sit-in outside Chandni's house. Police had registered an FIR against eight people in the case, including Chandni Qureshi, her father Islam Qureshi and three maulvis. On 7 June, police arrested three accused, including Chandni Qureshi and her father. After spending one and a half months in judicial custody, the father and daughter were granted bail by the court on 24 July. He became a Hindu again after performing religious rituals just 15 days later About 15 days later, Ayush released a video. He said, Mother, seeing your distress, I have returned of my own accord to my original religion, Hinduism. Please forgive me. On 9 September, Ayush's friend Mohammad Sultan filed a petition in the Allahabad High Court. He alleged that Ayush was being forcibly confined at home. The court ordered Ayush's father to produce him before the court on 16 September. Expressed desire to convert to Islam before the court On 16 September, Ayush Malik was produced before a bench of the Allahabad High Court headed by Justice Sandeep Jain. Ayush said, I am around 31 years old. I have studied up to BPharm. I converted to Islam of my own free will in 2014. I want to marry Chandni Qureshi. My father and family do not approve of this decision. Ayush alleged that he had received threats and had been kept under house arrest since June 2026. His father, Devraj Malik, rejected all his son's allegations outright. He said that some people had ‘brainwashed’ his son. As a father, he is deeply concerned about his son's future. Court says Ayush has the right to make his own decisions The court said Ayush Malik is an adult and fully capable of making decisions about his own life. It said he had converted his religion of his own free will, without any pressure or threats, and had decided to marry Chandni Qureshi. The court acknowledged that it was natural for Devraj Singh Malik to be concerned as a father. However, this concern cannot override the constitutional rights of an adult citizen. Therefore, Ayush has the independent right to live with a person of his choice according to his wishes, practise his religion and make decisions regarding marriage in accordance with the law. Father says-he will remain my son After the High Court's order, father Devraj Malik said that Ayush Malik is and will remain his son. He cannot live without his son. The High Court's decision is acceptable to him. ‘I want Ayush to live with his family.’ However, no statement from Ayush Malik has emerged in the matter so far.

stories.title: Lohia Trust becomes important for Akhilesh before polls:Took control after staying on sidelines since 2016
stories.summary: Akhilesh Yadav was recently elected president of the Lohia Trust, which owns the Samajwadi Party’s headquarters, district offices and several other properties and has a fund of around ₹800-1,000 crore; the trust also played an important role in the formation of the Samajwadi Party. During the 2016-17 feud, when then state president Shivpal was pushing Team Akhilesh out of the party, Akhilesh formed the Janeshwar Mishra Trust, while, as the dispute intensified, Mulayam Singh removed his cousin Ram Gopal Yadav, who was supporting Akhilesh, from the Lohia Trust and made his own brother Shivpal its secretary. Mulayam remained its president until his death. After his death, Shivpal became its head, and now the reins are in Akhilesh's hands. There is also discussion that his elder daughter, Aditi Yadav, could become part of the trust. Today, in the UP Explainer, read what changed in the trust's funds, properties and politics from the 2016 family battle to the present. What message is behind handing over its reins to Akhilesh? Question 1: What is the history of the Lohia Trust? Why is it important for Akhilesh? Answer: Let's understand the entire story of the Lohia Trust, from its formation to the present, in three parts... (A) The situation before its formation (B) Lohia Trust became the vehicle for the formation of the SP (C) Mulayam's Lohia Trust vs Akhilesh's Janeshwar Mishra Trust Question 2: How much property does the Lohia Trust have? Answer: There is no official figure available for the trust's bank accounts. As a non-governmental charitable trust, its balance sheet is not made public. After Akhilesh became the SP chief, the importance of the Janeshwar Mishra Trust increased. Funding has also shifted towards it. Question 3: What is the strategy behind changing the Lohia Trust president before the election? Answer: It is being viewed as an attempt to bring family coordination and Mulayam Singh's legacy under one roof ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections. The strategy can be understood as follows...

stories.title: Will UP Congress president be removed?:‘Chair’ tussle between 2 senior leaders; Rahul Gandhi to take final call
stories.summary: Political activity over the organisational leadership of the Uttar Pradesh Congress has intensified ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections. There are two possibilities being discussed: First: State Congress president Ajay Rai could be removed. Second: He could remain in the post, with three to four working presidents sharing responsibility with him. Discussions are reportedly underway over this formula. State in-charge Rajendra Pal Gautam claims that the party leadership is considering the options and that major decisions could be taken by September 30. On the other hand, Ajay Rai says he has no information about any organisational change at the state level. Read the full report... Why the discussion about changing the president is gaining momentum UP in-charge Rajendra Pal Gautam is reportedly presenting social equations before the high command. The argument being put forward is that Ajay Rai belongs to the Bhumihar community, whose population in the state is very small. To win the 2027 election, it is being argued that the Congress needs a face with a larger and broader vote base. Gautam himself belongs to the Dalit community. His strategy is reportedly to target Uttar Pradesh through a Dalit-Brahmin or Dalit-OBC combination. In this proposed change, the name of Pramod Tiwari's daughter and MLA Aradhana Mishra is gaining momentum. Both want to distribute tickets according to their own preferences Party insiders claim that the entire battle is not about the organisation but about retaining control over ticket distribution in the upcoming election. If an alliance is formed with the Samajwadi Party, Ajay Rai wants his close associates to get as many tickets as possible. Meanwhile, state in-charge Rajendra Pal Gautam is trying to field candidates of his choice. However, both leaders have publicly denied any such factionalism. When did the differences between the two leaders become visible? 1. Different claims over alliance with SP and seat-sharing Discussions about Ajay Rai's future began after the Congress replaced Brahmin leader Avinash Pandey with Dalit leader Rajendra Pal Gautam as its UP in-charge. Ajay Rai has been the state president for around three years. During this period, he visited different districts of the state to strengthen the organisation and focused on building the organisation at the grassroots level. After Gautam's arrival, his involvement in the Congress's strategy for seat-sharing with the Samajwadi Party also increased. Gautam advocated negotiating for an equal number of seats with the SP, while Ajay Rai continued to emphasise preparing the organisation across all 403 Assembly seats in Uttar Pradesh. 2. Rai unhappy over attempt to meet Mayawati In May 2026, Rajendra Pal Gautam suddenly reached BSP chief Mayawati's residence to meet her. Some other Congress leaders and MPs were also with him. However, Mayawati did not meet them. At the time, it was described as an attempt to initiate dialogue among Dalit leaders. Ajay Rai openly expressed his displeasure over this. He said he had no information about whose permission Gautam had taken before going to Mayawati's residence. 3. Differences intensified after district presidents' list emerged Although Rai and Gautam were seen smiling together at the 'Lok Hunkar' programme in Lucknow on September 2, discussions about differences intensified within a week. According to party sources, Gautam objected to the list of district presidents prepared under the 'Sangathan Srijan' campaign. There is discussion that he sought greater representation for Dalit, OBC and minority communities. 4. Separate joining programmes by both leaders on the same day On September 9, three prominent leaders were inducted into the Congress at the party headquarters. State in-charge Rajendra Pal Gautam merged the Jan Sardar Party of Siddharthnagar leader Hemant Chaudhary with the Congress. BJP leader Manoj Kumar Chauhan and Harvansh Singh Chauhan were also inducted into the Congress. On the same day, at 11 am, state president Ajay Rai himself inducted retired IAS officer Dr Rakesh Verma and South Indian film actress Firdaus Bano, also known as Zara Khan, into the Congress. Three options before the high command, which one will be approved? Rajendra Pal Gautam travelled to Delhi on September 10-11 and held a lengthy meeting with Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi and organisational general secretary KC Venugopal. There are now three options before the high command: First: Remove Ajay Rai and hand over the state leadership to a Brahmin, OBC or Dalit face. Second: In view of the party's performance in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, retain Ajay Rai as state president. The strongest argument in Rai's favour is that the party won six Lok Sabha seats under his leadership. He himself gave Prime Minister Narendra Modi a tough contest in Varanasi and led at different stages for a total of seven rounds during counting. Third: Instead of taking the risk of changing the president just four months before the election, retain Ajay Rai but appoint three to four working presidents alongside him to maintain a balance. These could include Brahmin, Dalit, OBC and Muslim faces. Will the 'experiment' in Bihar and Jharkhand weigh on the decision? In March 2025, around seven months before the Bihar Assembly elections, the Congress changed its state president. The party replaced Akhilesh Prasad Singh with Dalit leader Rajesh Kumar as state president. In the election results, the Congress fell from 19 seats to six. Similarly, in August 2024, around three months before the Jharkhand Assembly elections, the Congress replaced Rajesh Thakur with OBC leader Keshav Mahto Kamlesh as state president. In the election, the Congress retained its 16 seats. If Ajay Rai is removed as Uttar Pradesh Congress president, the change would mark the Congress's third major experiment with organisational leadership ahead of an Assembly election.

stories.title: 'Mohammed Shami's brother lives with me as husband':Says he promised marriage after IPL selection; now refuses relationship
stories.summary: A Lucknow woman has accused Indian cricketer Mohammed Shami’s younger brother, Mohammed Kaif, of rape. Kaif is also a cricketer and plays domestic cricket. An FIR for rape has been registered against him at Ashiyana police station. The woman said: “Before filing the FIR, I called Kaif for the last time from outside the police station. I wanted to know if there was still any possibility of us getting married. But now, I will never become part of his family… They should understand what a woman’s dignity means.” The woman spoke to Dainik Bhaskar about how her relationship with Kaif began, her conversations with Shami’s family and the entire dispute. Read the full interview… Question: Where did you first meet Kaif? How did the marriage talks begin? Woman: I met Kaif in 2020 through a common friend. He liked me, so we started talking on social media. Our meetings increased in 2023, and he told me that he wanted to marry me. He often said, “I will marry you once I get selected for the IPL.” When he was not selected, I asked him whether he would still marry me. After that, his behaviour changed and he started avoiding the issue. Question: Were you in touch with Kaif’s family? Did you ever speak directly to Mohammed Shami? Woman: When we were in a relationship, I also spoke to Mohammed Shami and other members of his family. But when his family refused to agree to the marriage, Mohammed Shami spoke to me using his elder brother’s phone number. He clearly said that the marriage could not happen. Question: Did you ever have a dispute with his family over your relationship with Kaif? Woman: I had mentioned my relationship with Kaif on a podcast on a sports channel. After that, I spoke to Kaif’s elder brother, Mohammed Haseeb. In May 2026, Kaif told me that he would marry me if I got the podcast deleted. After this, I met Kaif’s mother and his brother Haseeb at the home of his coach Badruddin in Moradabad. During the meeting, they said many hurtful things to me. It felt as though they had a problem with our relationship. Question: How often did you meet Kaif during your three-year relationship? Woman: I worked in the aviation sector, so I travelled to different states for work. Kaif would also call me to places where he travelled for his matches. We stayed together in several cities, including places in Uttar Pradesh, Kolkata, Hyderabad and Delhi. Our relationship was like that of a husband and wife. He never made me feel that he would betray me like this. Question: Why did you leave your job? Was there any pressure from Kaif? Woman: Kaif did not like me working as cabin crew at all. Later, after a lot of difficulties, I started working in Dubai, but he had problems with that too. I then started living under mental stress and could not focus on my career. Question: What did you speak to Kaif about just before filing the FIR? Woman: I last spoke to him on May 30, 2026. After that, when I went to Ashiyana police station in Lucknow to file the FIR, I called him one last time while standing outside the police station. I asked him if there was still any possibility of us getting married. But he clearly refused. Question: If Kaif or his family now agrees to a settlement and offers to marry you, what would your response be? Woman: I will never go to speak to him myself again. They should understand what a woman’s dignity means. I have neither any forgiveness left for him nor any possibility of living with him in the future.

stories.title: Principal shot dead in broad daylight in Mainpuri:3 attackers fired 2 bullets while he returned from school; brother wept hugging body
stories.summary: A 52-year-old principal was shot dead in broad daylight in Mainpuri. At 2 p.m. on Monday, he was travelling home from school. He had gone only a short distance when three men riding a motorcycle overtook and stopped him. They then began abusing him. When the principal objected and tried to flee, the attackers opened fire on him. One of the bullets hit the right side of his abdomen, causing him to collapse on the road. The attackers fled the scene after the incident. People working in nearby fields saw the principal lying injured on the road and informed the village head. Meanwhile, a fellow teacher who was travelling behind him informed his family and the police about the shooting. With the help of his family, the village head took the principal to hospital on a motorcycle, where doctors declared him dead. The incident took place under the jurisdiction of City Kotwali, about 10 kilometres from the district headquarters. First, see two pictures... Now, read the full story Yashpal was originally a resident of Guda village in the Etmadpur police station area of Agra district. However, he had been living in Mainpuri for a long time. He was living alone beside the District Magistrate's residence. His wife had died around 20 years ago. They had no children. Yashpal had previously served in the Air Force, but later left the job. After this, in 2002, he was appointed as a teacher at the upper primary school in Usmanpur. He was currently the principal. Yashpal was the second of three brothers. His elder brother, Rampal Singh, is also a government teacher. Yashpal was returning home after school. Near Rampura, around 5 kilometres from the school, motorcycle-borne criminals shot him dead. People grazing animals in the fields raised the alarm Village head Sanjeev Kumar said that people grazing animals in the fields had seen Yashpal in an injured condition. When they told me about it, I immediately reached the spot. By then, people from Yashpal's village and his family had also arrived there. People present at the spot said that three men had arrived on a motorcycle. They fired two shots at Yashpal. The school staff also left with them after the holiday. Teachers Suman and Kusum were only a short distance from the principal. They informed the principal's family members about the incident. The family then reached the spot. The principal was taken to the district hospital, where doctors declared her dead. On receiving the information, the station house officer and the City CO reached the spot. An FSL team was called to the scene to collect evidence. Based on a complaint by the family, police registered a case against Amit, Prashant and Ramveer. The body was sent for post-mortem examination. Family alleges principal was murdered over an old enmity Yashpal's brother, Rampal Singh, said the murder was linked to an old feud with some members of the family. However, the exact motive will become clear only after the police investigation. Additional SP Abhishek Tiwari said a land dispute had emerged between Yashpal and a distant relative, who was also his childhood friend. Yashpal was pursuing the case. Yashpal's family has alleged that he was murdered over this dispute. The entire matter is being investigated.

stories.title: Student jumps from third-floor hostel, dies:Ran to roof after row with warden; hostel staff hid body for 17 hours in Varanasi
stories.summary: A Class 12 student died after jumping from a hostel in Varanasi late on Sunday night. She fell headfirst from the third floor. The hostel authorities kept her death under wraps for 17 hours and did not inform the police or her family. The operator and staff of Sneh Deep Girls' Hostel in Dhannipur wanted to quietly hand over the student's body to her family. However, someone informed the police at 5 p.m. on Monday. During the investigation at the hostel, police found that the student had quarrelled with the warden before her death. Police have seized the DVR after examining the CCTV footage. Two female school employees have been detained and are being questioned after the students were interrogated. The body has been placed in the mortuary and the family has been informed of the incident. 3 pictures related to the incident... Now, the full incident in detail... Anamika Singh (17), a resident of the Bishra area of Odisha's Sundargarh district, was a Class 12 student at Saraswati College in Chandpur. She had been living in the hostel and studying for the past three years. On Sunday night, the hostel's female warden asked Anamika to do something, but she refused. An argument then broke out between Anamika and the warden. When the warden shouted angrily, several students gathered. Anamika then went to the hostel terrace in tears. Anamika found covered in blood in the hostel grounds At around 11 p.m., Anamika fell from the hostel terrace, screaming. Hearing her cries, the students ran outside and found her lying in the grounds, covered in blood. She had lost a considerable amount of blood. Hostel staff immediately rushed Anamika to hospital, where doctors declared her dead. The hostel operators informed her family late at night that she had fallen from the terrace. Saraswati College in Chandpur was not informed about the incident. Police and forensic team reach the spot As soon as the information was received, Lohata police and ACP Rohania reached the spot. The police took the body into custody and sent it to the Divisional Hospital, Kabir Chaura, for a post-mortem examination. In view of the seriousness of the case, a forensic team and dog squad also reached the hostel on Monday. The team examined the scene and collected evidence. The Lohata station house officer questioned the hostel management and the people present there. Two women questioned, several questions remain unanswered The police detained two women in the case and began questioning them. The actual cause of the student's death is not yet clear. The police are investigating the case while considering all possible aspects. After the incident, the police took possession of the DVRs of the CCTV cameras installed in the hostel. The police are now examining the footage to find out who had been in contact with the student before the incident and what her activities were. ADCP Varuna Zone Lipi Nagayach said- “The cause of death will become clearer only after the post-mortem report is received. The police have begun collecting all evidence related to the sequence of events. Answers to questions surrounding the death will emerge only from the CCTV footage, forensic evidence and post-mortem report.”

stories.title: UP’s 71-year-old Education Minister dances:Danced with Radha-Krishna performers in Sambhal; people said, ‘Never seen her like this’
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh's 71-year-old Secondary Education Minister Gulab Devi was seen dancing to bhajans dedicated to Radha Rani in Sambhal. She went onto the stage and danced to the bhajan with the Raslila performers. The video emerged at around 3 p.m. on Monday. The Shri Ganesh Chaturthi celebrations are being held in Mandanpur village, around 6 kilometres from the district headquarters. Gulab Devi arrived at the programme at around 10 p.m. on Sunday. After the Shri Ganesh puja, a Raslila depicting Radha and Krishna began on stage. A large number of villagers had also arrived to watch the programme. The event will continue until 24 September. See 3 pictures of the minister dancing... Now read the full story... Minister waved one hand in the air and placed the other on her waist During the Rasleela, the performers were dancing to a bhajan dedicated to Radha Rani. At that point, Gulab Devi reached the stage and began dancing with the performers. She was seen swaying with them to the bhajan "Hamaro Dhan Radha, Shri Radha, Shri Radha". The people attending the programme also encouraged her. The minister was seen enjoying the programme with one hand raised in the air and the other placed on her waist. Gulab Devi dancing with the performers on stage became a topic of discussion among the villagers. According to local people, they had seen their MLA in this manner for the first time. Minister attending religious events at night as well Minister Gulab Devi is preparing to contest the 2027 Assembly election. Several religious programmes, including Shri Ganesh Chaturthi celebrations and Ramlilas, are being organised in rural areas these days. In several places, these events continue until late at night. Along with daytime programmes, Gulab Devi is also attending religious events held at night.

stories.title: Husband kills wife in Meerut, then walks into police station:Says he slit her throat with a knife; two children sob beside body
stories.summary: In Meerut, a young man killed his wife on Monday. He then went to the police station and told the police that he had committed the murder. Meanwhile, when the woman's family from her parents' side reached her home to meet her, they found her blood-soaked body lying inside. Her young children were crying nearby. The family then informed the police as well. The police have taken the husband into custody. The woman's family alleged that the husband had assaulted her the previous day too. They said, "When we informed the police, he fled the scene." "We reached her home on Monday to take our daughter with us, but before that, her husband had slit her throat with a knife and killed her." The incident took place at 4 p.m. in the area under Bhavanpur police station. Killed wife and then reached police station himself Kavita (25), who lived in Jaibhim Nagar, married Manish (26), a resident of Khalsa Mohalla, in 2022. They have two children-Umang, also known as Abhishek (three), and their daughter Sona (two). Manish works as a labourer. The husband and wife had been quarrelling regularly since their marriage. On Monday, Manish slit Kavita's throat with a knife and killed her. He then reached Bhavanpur police station himself at around 4:30 p.m. When he told the police that he had killed his wife, they took him into custody. According to the family, Manish's brother-in-law, Mahendra Singh, is a sub-inspector in the Uttar Pradesh Police. He is posted at Loni Border. His first wife had died. He then married Manish's second sister. The sister is about eight years younger than her husband. Manish had arranged this marriage, while Kavita was opposed to it. This often led to arguments between Manish and Kavita. Kavita would tell family members that Mahendra had poisoned his first wife to death. He then married his second sister. Father said - daughter was brutally beaten on Sunday Kavita's father, Brajpal, said that she had been harassed at her in-laws' home ever since her marriage. The couple had been arguing for the past several days. On Sunday, her brother Bhupendra called Manish to speak to Kavita. He could hear Kavita crying in the background during the call. When asked why she was crying, Manish said that they had had an argument and that he had slapped her once or twice. Bhupendra then went to Kavita's home. When he arrived, he found that Kavita had been severely beaten. Kavita told him that Manish had grabbed her by the hair, assaulted her and thrown her out of the house. Manish had fled the house when police arrived After this, Bhupendra informed Dial-112. The police reached the spot, but by then Manish had fled. Her father, Brajpal, said that they wanted to take Kavita with them. However, the police personnel refused, saying that a case could be registered against him instead. On Monday morning, I asked people in the area about my daughter over the phone. They told me that Kavita had not been seen since Sunday. We then went with the family to her house to check on her. When we entered the house, we found both her children crying and Kavita's blood-soaked body lying there. Kavita had a serious injury to her neck and knife-attack marks on her body. The police were then informed. The police sent the body for a post-mortem examination.

stories.title: CO Zia-ul-Haq’s father says, ‘I won’t get justice now’:Raised son in poverty to make him officer; says daughter-in-law is dragging him to court
stories.summary: "We had hoped for justice for a long time, but that hope has now been shattered. We raised and educated our son in poverty and made him a police officer. He was murdered in broad daylight in Kunda. We lost our son, but we hoped that justice would be delivered. The court's order has caused us great distress. Our relationship with our daughter-in-law is no longer good either. A case over the money from our son's LIC policy is pending in court." This was said by Haji Shamsul Haq, father of Zia-ul Haq, who was the Circle Officer of Pratapgarh. The closure report filed in the case related to the murder of the Circle Officer was accepted by the Special CBI Court in Lucknow on 19 September. Following this, no further legal action will be taken against five people, including Kunda MLA Raghuraj Pratap Singh, also known as Raja Bhaiya. As soon as Zia-ul Haq's family in Deoria learnt of the decision, they were overcome with disappointment. Dainik Bhaskar's team travelled to Juafar village in the Khukhundu police station area, around 20 km from the Deoria district headquarters. The team spoke to Circle Officer Zia-ul Haq's family. Read the full report... First, know the full story This dates back to 2 March 2013. After Kunda village head Nanhe Yadav was murdered in Balipur village, Pratapgarh, Kunda CO Zia-ul-Haq reached the spot. The crowd present there surrounded Zia-ul-Haq and beat him to death. The case was handed over to the CBI. After the investigation, the trial began. In October 2024, a special CBI court convicted 10 people and sentenced them to life imprisonment. Those convicted included Phoolchand Yadav, Pawan Yadav and Manjeet Yadav. After this, the CBI filed a closure report in the case. However, following a complaint by Zia-ul-Haq's wife, Parveen Azad, the case was reinvestigated against five people, including Raja Bhaiya. The CBI later filed a closure report in this matter as well. The court of Special Judicial Magistrate (CBI) Pratibha Singh accepted the closure report on 19 September. No further court proceedings will now take place against these five people in the case. Now read about the family's anguish Father said-When my son became a CO, I thought our lives would change We met Zia-ul Haq's father, Haji Shamsul Haq, in Juafer village. It is his house. The only members of his family now left are his wife, Hajra Khatoon, and younger son, Sohrab Haq. Sohrab also works in another district. Shamsul says, "Despite our family's poor financial condition, we educated Zia-ul at the village school. We sent him to Prayagraj to prepare for competitive examinations." After years of hard work, their son became a police officer. The family then hoped that their lives would change. In 2012, Ziaul was appointed CO of the Kunda Circle. But he was murdered just a year later. The death of their son completely devastated the family. Even in their old age, they continue to hope for justice. Daughter-in-law lives in Lucknow, rarely visits here Shamsul says, "Our daughter-in-law, Dr Parveen Azad, is also posted in the police department as an OSD. She lives in Lucknow. She rarely visits Deoria. Over time, the distance between her and us continued to grow." A lawsuit had been filed over the LIC money. A case is now also pending over the movable and immovable property. The matter is scheduled to be heard on 28 September. The growing distance within the family after the loss of their son has made our difficulties even worse. Mother says: Those responsible for her son's death should be punished Since her son's death, Ziaul Haq's mother, Hajra Khatun, has been hoping for justice. She says, "Those responsible for my son's death must be punished. Even in my old age, I have to make repeated trips in connection with the cases. I do not even speak to my daughter-in-law. I have already said that I will pursue the case up to the Supreme Court. The pain of losing my son will remain for the rest of my life, but we do not want to give up hope of getting justice."

stories.title: 105 cases of offerings theft, not 70, at Ram Mandir:SIT tells Supreme Court; says chargesheet will be filed in 2 days
stories.summary: There has been a major development in the Ayodhya Ram Mandir offerings theft case. The Supreme Court was told on Monday that the temple's CCTV footage had captured not 70 but 105 incidents of offerings being stolen. Solicitor General Tushar Mehta briefed the court on the investigation based on the status report submitted by the Special Investigation Team (SIT). He said the SIT's investigation was almost complete. The SIT identified the accused after examining CCTV footage, witness statements and other evidence. Receipts for offerings and valuables are generated through software, and the items are kept in an SBI locker. The court took the SIT's status report on record. Earlier, on 23 June, the first SIT had submitted its preliminary investigation report to the state government. According to the report, around 70 suspected incidents were captured on CCTV between 27 April and 5 June. The footage showed the eight accused arrested by the police hiding bundles of currency notes in their pockets and shoes. A second SIT was formed on the Supreme Court's directions and is conducting the investigation. Charge sheet to be filed by 25 September The Solicitor General said the SIT would file the charge sheet by 25 September. The Supreme Court directed the magistrate to act on the charge sheet in accordance with the law. The petitioners had sought a copy of the SIT report, but the Supreme Court refused to provide it. The bench headed by the CJI said it did not want to take the case out of the jurisdiction of the Sessions Judge. If necessary, the court may issue orders regarding further investigation into the matter. 90 days to be completed on 22 September-will the accused be released on bail? According to senior advocate Shivam Pandey, in cases where the law requires a chargesheet to be filed within 90 days, the accused may become entitled to statutory, or default, bail if the chargesheet is not filed on time. In this case, the 90-day period is coming to an end. Therefore, the deadline for the police to file the chargesheet has become crucial. Notice was issued in July Four petitions were filed in the Supreme Court in July seeking an investigation into the theft of offerings. The Supreme Court issued notices to the Central government, the Uttar Pradesh government and the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust. The petitioners include RJD MP Sudhakar Singh, lawyer NK Goswami, Ajay Kumar Rai and the Hindu Dharma Parishad. The petition also seeks a complete audit of the Ram Temple Trust's funds. FIR registered against eight people on 25 June; all in jail An FIR was registered against eight people at the Ram Janmabhoomi police station on 25 June. They include Ramshankar Yadav alias Tinnu Yadav, Anukalp Mishra, Lavkush Mishra, Manish Yadav, Subhash Srivastava, Avinash Shukla, Karunesh Pandey and Ramashankar Mishra. Police arrested all the accused and sent them to jail. The accused have been booked under sections relating to theft from the temple, theft of property by an employee, criminal breach of trust, helping conceal or use stolen property, criminal conspiracy and committing an offence with a shared intention. All of them are lodged in Faizabad jail. Police outlined the accused's different roles According to the police, Ramshankar Yadav alias Tinnu had the keys to the donation boxes without any formal order. Anukalp Mishra and Lavkush Mishra were involved in counting the cash. The police claim that around ₹20 lakh was recovered from Anukalp's house and around ₹10 lakh from Lavkush's house. Manish Yadav, Subhash Srivastava, Avinash Shukla, Karunesh Pandey and Ramashankar Mishra have also been named as being involved in counting the cash. According to the police, ₹5 lakh was recovered from Avinash Shukla's bank account. CCTV and electronic evidence also collected The police examined CCTV footage from the temple premises. Registers related to the counting of offerings and statements from employees were also included in the investigation. Forensic and electronic evidence has also been collected. The chargesheet will include details of the alleged modus operandi of the theft, the role of the accused and the recoveries made from them.

stories.title: Meat cooked in pot over burning funeral pyre:Son chased and caught man in Shahjahanpur; accused said he craved food after drinking
stories.summary: Three youths cooked meat in a pot over a burning funeral pyre in Shahjahanpur. Seeing this, the deceased's son and his relatives chased and caught one of the accused. His two associates fled on a motorcycle. Police arrested them both on Monday. According to the police, all three admitted during questioning that they had cooked the meat while intoxicated. All three were sent to jail after being formally charged. The accused have been identified as Ramcharan, Rajendra and Surendra Singh. The case is from the Powayan police station area. Now read the full story... Went to see the funeral pyre one hour after the cremation Chhotelal (60), a resident of Natthapur village, died on Saturday after a prolonged illness. On Sunday afternoon, his family members and relatives reached the cremation ground to perform his last rites. After lighting the funeral pyre, they all returned home. About an hour later, Chhotelal's son Veerpal said he wanted to go and check the funeral pyre. He said that if any wood had fallen from it, he would put it back. When Veerpal reached the cremation ground with some relatives, they found three young men cooking meat on his father's burning funeral pyre. Meat was being cooked in a pot over the funeral pyre's fire According to Veerpal, the meat had been placed in a pot and was being cooked over the fire from the funeral pyre. Veerpal and his relatives tried to catch the three young men. They managed to catch one of them, but the other two fled. However, Veerpal had identified them. After this, Veerpal informed the police via Dial-112. The police reached the spot and took the apprehended youth to the police station. Veerpal filed a complaint at the station at around 6 p.m. on Sunday. In it, he alleged that three youths were cooking meat on his father's burning funeral pyre. All three looked like tantriks. They said they had been drinking and felt like eating meat After receiving the complaint, the police began searching for the two absconding youths. Puwayan police station officers set up a cordon near Natthapur Tirahe on Monday morning based on information from an informer. They arrested both youths there. During police questioning, the three youths said they had been drunk. When they felt like eating meat, they placed a cooking pot over the fire of a funeral pyre. According to the police, after sobering up, the youths admitted their mistake and began apologising. However, the police investigation did not confirm that the youths were tantriks. Puwayan Station House Officer R.K. Rawat said the three accused had been arrested and further action had been taken against them. The police challaned them and sent them to jail.

stories.title: Cop convicted of killing Apple manager sentenced:Court awards 10 years; Vivek Tiwari’s wife and brother-in-law absent
stories.summary: Former constable Prashant Chaudhary has been sentenced to 10 years in prison for the 2018 murder of Apple area sales manager Vivek Tiwari. The Apple manager's wife and brother-in-law did not attend court when the sentence was announced. The Lucknow District and Sessions Court had convicted Prashant of culpable homicide not amounting to murder on 17 September, while acquitting the other accused constable, Sandeep Kumar, for lack of evidence. Wife Kalpana says she is not satisfied with the verdict and will approach the High Court After Vivek's conviction on 17 September, his wife Kalpana Tiwari expressed dissatisfaction with the verdict. She had said she expected to receive justice from the court, but the verdict did not meet her expectations. Describing Prashant as a trained police officer, Kalpana had questioned how firing a shot could be regarded as merely a mistake. She had also said that she would approach a higher court against the verdict. Final arguments in the case were completed on 6 August. In this case, which has been ongoing for nearly eight years, the decision on the convict's sentence will be announced today, 21 September. Read what happened on the night of the incident Late on the night of 29 September 2018, Vivek Tiwari was returning by car with a female colleague. Police personnel riding a motorcycle tried to stop his car in the Makdoompur area of Gomtinagar Extension. According to the police, the car did not stop and a collision appeared imminent, following which Prashant Chaudhary fired a shot. Vivek was taken to hospital after being shot, where he died.

stories.title: ‘Even if Rahul, Akhilesh hang upside down, nothing will happen’:Ravi Kishan in Gorakhpur says, 'SP, Congress will lose in 2027 elections'
stories.summary: BJP MP Ravi Kishan Shukla appeared to launch a fierce attack on the Opposition on Monday. Speaking to the media, he said, ‘Even if Rahul Gandhi and Akhilesh Yadav hang upside down, nothing is going to happen’. He further added, 'This is their move, and it is not going to work. They say the ‘P’ in PDA stands for Pandit, but Brahmins are not going to be misled by them. If they think they can win over Brahmins, they should first look at their history, who Brahmins were and what they are. Brahmins have always sacrificed for the nation. This community will never go with them. The SP and Congress will suffer a crushing defeat in 2027.' Responding to journalists’ questions at his residence in Gorakhpur, Ravi Kishan said the AI videos being released by the Samajwadi Party and Congress showed that the Opposition had realised it was facing a crushing defeat. He claimed that their election deposits were being forfeited. “That is why these statements are being made. That is why AI videos are being created. Opposition leaders have lowered the level of politics and made it petty. They are not allowing the House to function. They are getting nothing out of it. The corruption that used to take place under their governments has been completely stopped. That is why they have now stooped to C-grade politics. They are making statements about wooing Brahmins and forming a Backward Classes front.” They will lose in 2027 and suffer an even worse defeat in 2029 Ravi Kishan said the Opposition would lose in 2027 and suffer an even worse defeat in 2029. He said the BJP alone would remain in the country and stay in power until 2047. Speaking about the jibe aimed at Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s mother from Rahul Gandhi’s stage in Indore, he said the public was responding to it. “They are left with nothing. The Congress was once such a huge party, where is it today? If they indulge in pettiness and clownish behaviour, how will they return to power? Rahul Gandhi is doing exactly that,” he said. Commenting on Hamid Ansari’s statement, Ravi Kishan said Ansari also knew that the party he supported would not come to power. “That is why the high command must have told him to make such statements,” he said. Appealing to Ansari, he said that he should not speak in that manner, as he had held a senior position. The entire country views that position with respect. People have been hurt by his words. Ravi Kishan said such things can happen even at a certain stage of life. In response to a question, he said that the Opposition could claw at each other; they had nothing to do with it. “Our concern is the BJP. Let them tear their hair out. We have to see how we can secure an even bigger victory for the BJP in 2027 than in 2017.”

stories.title: Python coils around youth’s neck:Wrapped around his hand after being freed; held him for 30 minutes before letting go after being beaten with a stick
stories.summary: A python suddenly attacked a young man in Lakhimpur, Uttar Pradesh. It wrapped itself around his neck and, within moments, began constricting his entire body. When the young man tried to break free, the python restrained his hands. Hearing the young man's screams, villagers rushed to his aid. They beat the python with sticks for nearly 30 minutes. Only then did it release the young man. His hand was severely injured. After being informed by the villagers, a Forest Department team arrived, caught the python and released it into the forest. The young man was admitted to a nearby hospital. The spine-chilling incident took place on 16 September in the South Nighasan Range area. A VIDEO of the incident emerged today. See 3 pictures- Here is the full sequence of events- Panic gripped the area after the video surfaced Fear has gripped the area after a video of a python attack emerged. People are not venturing out of their homes at night. Mohammed Mobeen Arif, ranger of the South Nighasan Range, said the Forest Department had inspected the site. Python attacks often increase in the area during the rainy season. People have been advised to remain alert.

stories.title: Akhilesh says, ‘Our rath went for diesel, rivals panicked’:Hits back at Mayawati’s ‘saffron’ remark; says SP will make history in 2027
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav held an organisational meeting at the party office in Lucknow on Monday, 21 September, before addressing a press conference that began with the launch of the SP's new songs. Akhilesh said BJP leaders had a negative mindset and were therefore spreading only negative propaganda, adding that they wanted the SP to get caught up in the same negativity, but SP workers were giving them a fitting response on their own. Akhilesh Yadav said he had already held meetings with senior organisational leaders and grassroots workers from Uttar Pradesh constituencies where the Samajwadi Party had failed to win in the previous election. He claimed that everyone had sat together at the party office and resolved that the SP would win the highest-ever record number of seats in its history in the upcoming election. Based on the ground reports and data submitted by workers and organisational members after visiting the ground, the party is soon going to take major decisions. Akhilesh said, ‘If they make songs and videos, we will not back down either’ Akhilesh questioned the BJP's budget. He said that if someone was making videos using the government budget and government money, their workers were not behind either. He said that the workers of their party were making these songs themselves without taking a single rupee, completely free of cost. This reflected their attachment to the party, their love for the party's decisions, schemes and the work carried out by them, which they were bringing out through songs. They did not want to make negative songs but would not back down on the ground either. 'Corruption in government recruitment, PDA's rights being taken away' On the issue of government jobs and reservations, Akhilesh Yadav referred to his earlier report and book. He directly accused the government of corruption in government recruitment. He said, "You will remember that when we first had government jobs audited, it was found how government jobs were being manipulated and looted. Reservations were stolen in each department. The rights and entitlements of people from backward, Dalit and PDA communities were taken away. We had formally released an audit report and a book, which clearly stated that more than 11,000 government posts had been directly looted." Akhilesh said that the government was deliberately not providing permanent government jobs. "They are promoting outsourcing so that they do not have to provide young people with permanent government jobs. If there are permanent jobs, you will not be able to take commissions from the government budget, but in outsourcing, you receive hefty commissions directly from each company." 'Statues of Babasaheb were deliberately vandalised at 151 locations' Akhilesh Yadav appeared highly emotional and aggressive while referring to the Constitution and Dr B.R. Ambedkar. He made the allegations one by one. Akhilesh said he had complete documented information and a list showing that statues of Babasaheb had been deliberately vandalised at 151 locations across the state. In several places, the police simply registered FIRs against 'unknown persons' and closed the files; no concrete action has been taken against anyone to date. Akhilesh said, "Whenever these people break a statue, the first thing they break is Babasaheb's hand. Why? Because he is holding a book of the country's Constitution. Even today, when they do not have a clear majority on their own at the Centre, they are tearing the Constitution to shreds. They have no regard for the law or the courts." 'The government has no figures on cows', cornered over stray animals When Akhilesh was asked about the condition of stray animals and cows in the state, he said, “If this government has the figures, let it tell the media how many cows there were in the state in total and how many of them died of hunger, illness or accidents.” You will never get these figures! The government has no record of this." Major Announcement for Women: SP to Launch ₹2 Lakh Scheme When a journalist asked, "Will there be any special initiative for women if your party forms the government?", Akhilesh recalled his previous tenure. Akhilesh said, "Take a look at our previous manifesto. We were the first to launch the 'Samajwadi Pension' for daughters, students, young people and women. Following our example, states such as Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra later adopted it as well." Akhilesh said, "The Samajwadi Party had initially decided to provide ₹40,000. The BJP copied us and said it would provide ₹50,000. When its ₹50,000 scheme failed, it began saying that it would provide ₹1 lakh. The Samajwadi Party has now decided that, if our government is formed, a special programme worth ₹2 lakh in full will be created for mothers and sisters. Using the same rules and banks through which they are planning their ₹1 lakh scheme, we will arrange ₹2 lakh." When a journalist interjected with a laugh, asking, "Will you give five kilos of sugar as well, like the ration supplied to people?" Akhilesh laughed and brushed off the question, saying, "Don't make me say everything just yet, sir!" 'Hospitals themselves are sick; they sent a living patient to the mortuary' Akhilesh Yadav made serious allegations about the functioning of the Health Department and the Deputy Chief Minister (Health Minister). He said, "What can I even tell you? All of us are somehow getting through our days. He added, "Take my advice and, even by mistake, do not go to a government hospital for treatment. I have already given several examples – one poor man went for treatment for stomach pain, and they amputated his hand! They put the other man's leg in a plaster cast and then amputated his entire leg! A patient regained consciousness in the operating theatre and fled for his life, leaving the operating theatre! The limit was crossed when a living person was sent to the mortuary!" He claimed that government hospitals had neither medicines nor ambulances. Pregnant women were dying in the ambulances themselves. The government had set a new record for poor conditions. "America gave Modi a 100% tariff gift on his birthday" Akhilesh Yadav directly targeted Prime Minister Narendra Modi over foreign affairs and India's ties with the United States. He said, "You never tire of going on about Trump. Only the prime minister could have access to Trump. But look at what America gave you in return. On your birthday itself, it handed you a 100% tariff as a return gift!" On allegations that a narrative was being created in the media and on social media, he said, "Some people are getting false propaganda spread on social media on the strength of a little 'dana-pani' (money and conveniences). I repeat: there has been neither dictatorship nor 'handout-ocracy' in this country, and there will be neither. This dictatorship and 'handout-ocracy', which are being run on the strength of handouts, will both end very soon." "The police have become inhumane; we will take action if we form the government" Referring to the cases in Gorakhpur and Deoria, Akhilesh said that the police had become inhumane. A poor man's bicycle was stolen, but instead of arresting the thief, the police beat to death at the police station the innocent poor man who had bought the bicycle, knowingly or unknowingly. Later, as always, they made the excuse that "he died of a heart attack". Akhilesh made it clear that the Samajwadi Party's longstanding alliance would remain as it was. Hitting back at BSP supremo Mayawati's statement, he said, "Our chariot had only gone to get its diesel tank filled, and the opponents panicked already!"

stories.title: Comedian’s shows cancelled after Modi mimicry:Says UP shows called off over threats from ‘goon workers’; attended Rahul’s ‘Chhatron Ki Goonj’
stories.summary: Stand-up comedian Pulkit Mani has announced on Instagram the cancellation of his show in Noida, Lucknow and Kanpur following a controversy over his mimicry of Prime Minister Narendra Modi at Lok Sabha Leader of the Opposition and Congress leader Rahul Gandhi’s ‘Chhatron Ki Goonj’ event in Indore, Madhya Pradesh. Mani announced the cancellations through Instagram stories. He initially said the Noida show had been cancelled due to “unforeseen circumstances”. He later said his Lucknow and Kanpur shows were cancelled because of what he described as “repeated threats from goon activists”. There has been no independent confirmation in the available reports of the alleged threats or details of any action against the people responsible. Noida show cancelled due to ‘unforeseen circumstances’ In his first Instagram story, Mani said his Noida show had been cancelled due to “unforeseen circumstances”. He apologised to the audience for the inconvenience and thanked them for their understanding and support. In that post, he did not directly link the cancellation to the Indore event or any alleged threats. Mani cites threats for Lucknow, Kanpur cancellations In a subsequent Instagram story, Mani announced that his shows in Lucknow and Kanpur had also been cancelled. He attributed the decision to what he called “repeated threats from goon activists”. Mani did not provide further details about the alleged threats or identify the individuals or groups behind them. Mimicry performed at Rahul Gandhi’s Indore event On September 19, Mani performed at Rahul Gandhi’s ‘Chhatron Ki Goonj’ event in Indore. A video shared by the Congress showed Mani performing a short skit with Gandhi in which he impersonated Modi’s mannerisms and style of speaking. During the act, Mani also mimicked Modi’s interactions with foreign leaders. Another part referred to an incident involving Modi speaking to an elderly woman and offering her a chair. ‘Maa ko kursi do’ remark sparks controversy During the performance, Mani said, “Maa Ko Kursi Do, Maa”. The video triggered criticism from BJP leaders, who accused Congress and Gandhi of disrespecting Modi through the performance. Congress leaders and supporters, meanwhile, described the act as mimicry and political satire. The controversy has since continued on social media, with BJP leaders publicly criticising the performance and the Congress defending the programme.
