stories.title: 26-year-old woman teacher killed in school:Man drags her out, shoots 3 times, then dies by suicide in Lakhimpur
stories.summary: A female teacher was shot dead inside a school in Lakhimpur. The accused first shot the teacher with a country-made pistol (tamancha) and then committed suicide. The incident took place at Children's Academy School, located right in front of the Collectorate. Children were studying in the school at the time of the incident. Upon receiving information from the school management, the police arrived and evacuated the entire building. Parents were called to take the children home. Currently, a police force is deployed at the school, and no one is being allowed inside. A forensic team arrived at the spot and gathered evidence. SP Khyati Garg, ASP Pawan Gautam, and CO City Vivek Tiwari also reached the spot. They questioned the school staff to gather details about the entire matter. The incident falls under the Sadar Kotwali police station area. The teacher was the only sister of two brothers Nishat Fatima (26), a resident of the Hidayat Nagar area, was the only sister of two brothers. She has two brothers, one of whom is named Anas. Her father, Ilyas, works in Mumbai. Several years ago, Nishat Fatima's family lived as tenants in the house of Saud Ansari (28) in Naurangabad. Later, they shifted to their own house. Saud Ansari was a student. His father, Qayyum Ansari, works in the District Industries Centre. Saud's elder brother, Dawood Ansari, runs a sofa and mattress shop. It is reported that the affair between Nishat and Saud began during the time her family lived there as tenants. Dragged her out of the classroom, fired with a country-made pistol On Monday morning around 11:30 AM, teacher Nishat Fatima was teaching students in a classroom on the second floor of the school. Just then, Saud Ansari arrived there carrying a country-made pistol (tamancha). He grabbed Fatima's hand, dragged her out into the corridor, and began arguing with her. Amidst the altercation, Saud suddenly pulled out the pistol and fired multiple shots at Fatima. She collapsed onto the floor. Hearing the gunshots, panic ensued. The schoolchildren started screaming. The staff rushed to the spot. However, in the meantime, Saud shot himself as well and died on the spot. See 3 pictures of the incident- School operates from Nursery to Class 8 A private school named Children's Academy operates out of a two-story building in the Shahpura Kothi area. Children from Nursery to Class 8 study here. SP Khyati Garg stated—Nishat Fatima, a resident of Hidayat Nagar, had been teaching at this school for the past year. Saud Ansari reached the school to meet her. He went straight upstairs to the corridor via the staircase. Saud called Nishat outside. When Nishat refused, he grabbed her hand and forcibly brought her out. Here, both began talking loudly. Hearing the noise, teachers teaching in nearby classrooms also came outside. Just then, Saud pulled out a country-made pistol (tamancha) from his bag and shot Nishat. He then committed suicide with the same pistol. Both died on the spot. stories.title: Crorepati daughter-in-law says, ‘I want to tell court the truth’:Denies giving key to Vishal; files plea opposing police custody remand
stories.summary: Shalu, accused of being involved in the murder of her father-in-law Vineet Minocha, has filed an application opposing police custody remand, claiming that the grounds cited by the investigating officer are incorrect. In her application, Shalu said she never made the statement attributed to her by the police. She told the court that she wants to record her statement before a magistrate and reveal the truth. Shalu, alleged contract killer Vishal and his associate Raj Kishore were produced before the ACJM court on September 19. Police sought their custody for further questioning. Shalu’s lawyer, Shivakant Dixit, opposed the remand application. The court will hear the remand application on September 22. Shalu is currently lodged in Kanpur district jail. Police want to confront Shalu with husband Subrat DCP West SM Qasim Abidi said the remand hearing would be held on Tuesday. Police said that if custody is granted, Shalu will be confronted with her husband, Subrat. Police have alleged that there were four keys to the flat where Vineet Minocha lived, with two of them kept at the residence. Investigators want to establish which key Shalu allegedly gave Vishal so that he could get a duplicate made. Police also want Shalu to identify the key and the location at Parade Square where the duplicate was allegedly made. Shalu has denied making such a statement. Questions police want to ask Shalu Investigators are expected to question Shalu about the circumstances surrounding Vineet Minocha’s murder and why security guard Madan Singh was allegedly given a wrong name for Vishal. Police also want to know why Vishal named Shalu, when the alleged plan was made, where the duplicate key was prepared, whether Subrat knew about it and why Vishal called a day before the murder. Read which questions the police may ask both accused persons... Police to question Vishal about alleged conspiracy Police also want to question Vishal about who allegedly instructed him to kill Vineet Minocha. Investigators are examining why Vishal visited the businessman’s son three times before the murder, whether Subrat knew about the alleged plan, his calls with Raj Kishore and the plan to escape after the killing. Police said Vishal made five calls to a friend in Mirpur Cantonment. Investigators are also examining when the alleged conspiracy was planned, whether Shalu had offered to reinstate Vishal and why Subrat contacted him after his employment was terminated. 309 calls between Vishal and Subrat examined Police have examined the call detail records of seven mobile numbers belonging to Shalu, Subrat and Vishal. According to the police investigation, Vishal and Subrat spoke 309 times between May 1 and September 5. Vishal allegedly purchased a Jio SIM card two days before the murder and used it to contact Subrat. Investigators are questioning the purpose of these calls. Subrat’s firm had 17 employees and three household staff members. Despite this, he allegedly used Vishal for various jobs, reportedly saying that Vishal was a skilled electrician. Police said Subrat and Vishal were seen together around 20 days before the murder and allegedly went to get a key made. Subrat has not explained why the key was needed, according to investigators. CCTV footage allegedly showed the two at a kiosk. Police also said Subrat took Vishal to a doctor after he complained of feeling unwell. Vishal worked with family for 12 years Vishal had worked at the family’s shop and home for around 12 years. Police said Subrat initially denied identifying the accused in CCTV footage, claiming that the faces were unclear. However, investigators said Subrat remained in contact with Vishal even after Vineet had removed him from the job. Subrat reportedly told police that he contacted Vishal for small jobs. Couple attended party on night of murder On the night of September 5, when Vineet Minocha was murdered, Subrat and Shalu attended a couple’s kitty party at Cosmojin Lounge in Tilak Nagar. The party was allegedly organised by Subrat and attended by around 35 people from the pharmaceutical trade. Restaurant records showed that the couple arrived at around 10:30 pm, the party began at 11:30 pm and they left at around 3 am. The booking cost ₹1,400 per person, while the total bill was around ₹49,000. Subrat reportedly told police that he earned ₹35,000 a month and Shalu received ₹10,000 as household expenses. Investigators questioned how the couple could spend around ₹49,000 on the party against their stated combined monthly income of ₹45,000. Police said they did not receive a satisfactory explanation. Social media activity also under investigation After the murder, Subrat reportedly uploaded a Pharma Traders wallpaper on Facebook. He later deleted the post after people commented on it. Police also said that photos and reels from his Facebook and Instagram accounts were deleted after the incident. Vineet lived in ₹1 crore-plus flat Vineet Minocha lived with his family in flat C-104 on the first floor of Ratan Orbit Apartment. The four-room flat also had a dining area and was valued at more than ₹1 crore. He ran Pharma Traders on Birhana Road with his son, Subrat. The business reportedly had an annual turnover of around ₹50–60 crore. Vineet lived with his wife Punita, son Subrat, daughter-in-law Shalu and five-year-old grandson Shrijay. Shalu and Subrat had married seven years ago in Nainital. Punita, a marriage counsellor, lives in Ghaziabad with her daughter Subhani and son-in-law. Shalu’s father, Naresh Arora, is a textile businessman in Thakurganj, Lucknow. Vineet was stabbed more than 26 times On September 5, Vineet Minocha was allegedly attacked with a knife. He suffered more than 26 stab wounds to his neck and chest and died. Police arrested Vishal Gautam, an employee at the family’s shop, and Raj Kishore after an encounter on the night of September 6. According to police, Vishal allegedly told investigators that he killed Vineet at Shalu’s behest. Security guard Madan Singh reportedly told police that Shalu had called Vishal to the house. Police subsequently arrested Shalu and sent her to jail. Police examining possible motive Police had sought 24-hour custody of Shalu and Vishal, but the hearing was postponed to September 19 because of a lawyers’ strike. Investigators also found a will belonging to Punita Minucha, dated June 2022, at the registration office. Police are examining its contents and beneficiaries as part of their investigation into a possible motive. The investigation into the alleged conspiracy, the role of the accused and the circumstances surrounding Vineet Minocha’s murder is continuing.

stories.title: Police leave for Jhansi jail with Atiq’s son Ali:Statement recorded in Prayagraj court; brother’s car stopped while following convoy
stories.summary: Mafia Atiq Ahmed's son, Ali Ahmed, was produced in a Prayagraj court on Monday in connection with an extortion case. He recorded his statement and remained in court for about two hours. As he stepped out, media personnel tried to speak with him, but the police prevented them from doing so. The police placed Ali directly into a van and pulled down the curtains. Following this, a convoy of 3 vehicles with 35 police personnel departed with him toward Jhansi. Asad Kalia, who is lodged in Kasganj Jail, was also produced in court for the same case and recorded his statement. Given the appearance of both individuals, over 250 police personnel were deployed inside and outside the ADJ court. While Ali was being brought to Prayagraj, his brother Ahjam was following the convoy in a car. Upon realizing this, the police stopped and searched Ahjam's car in Kaushambi. During questioning, Ahjam stated that he had learned about Ali being brought from jail, which is why he was following behind the convoy. The police instructed him not to follow along any further. The extortion case is three years old. A farmer from Prayagraj had registered an FIR against five people, including Ali. It is alleged that, on Ali's instructions, his aides demanded an extortion sum of ₹30 lakh, forcibly made him sign blank stamp papers, and assaulted him. Earlier on August 8, Ali was brought to Prayagraj to attend the funeral (Supurd-e-Khak) of his younger brother Abaan. The High Court had granted parole to Ali and his brother Umar. On August 6, Abaan was on his way to meet Ali. His car collided with a divider on the highway in Jhansi, leading to his death in the accident. 3 photos of Ali's court appearance Wearing a white cap, Ali reached Prayagraj Ali had departed from Jhansi for Prayagraj at 6:00 AM for his court appearance. He reached the court at 12:30 PM amidst heavy security. He was wearing a white cap, a shirt, and jeans. His hands were tied with a rope, and he was carrying a towel (gamcha) in one hand. The police took him straight into the courtroom. The preparations for bringing Ali to Prayagraj were kept so confidential that no one had any prior information about it. Scuffle among supporters to meet Ali When the police brought Ali outside after the court appearance, a large number of supporters were present outside the court. They tried to shake hands and talk with Ali. During this, a scuffle broke out among the supporters. After much effort, the police managed to escort Ali out of the crowd. Know the case in which Ali was produced in court About 3 years ago, Afzal, a resident of Kasari-Masari in Prayagraj, lodged an FIR at the Kareli police station against Ali, Faizan, Altamash, Asad Kalia, and an unidentified person. At that time, Ali was lodged in Naini Jail. Farmer Afzal stated in the FIR that he owns land in Enuddinpur village. On August 7, 2023, he received information that some people had arrived to usurp his land. He reached the spot with his nephew Amir Hamza, but by then the accused had already left. According to Afzal, about half an hour later, while returning from the field near the Enuddinpur mosque, Faizan, Altamash, and an unidentified person intercepted his motorcycle. It is alleged that the three assaulted him. Altamash said that Ali and Asad, who are in jail, sent a message to hand over the land so that plotting could be done on it. If the land is not given, ₹30 lakh will have to be paid, which is to be sent to Ali. They threatened to kill him if he failed to comply. Afzal alleged in the FIR that he pleaded for his life. Following this, Altamash forcibly made him sign blank stamp papers. The accused threatened that he must either pay ₹30 lakh in extortion or give up the land; otherwise, they would create a fake agreement and transfer the land to Ali's name. After this, the accused left the spot after giving him a deadline of one week. The police had registered a case under IPC Sections 307 (attempt to murder), 386 (extortion by putting a person in fear of death or grievous hurt), 341 (wrongful restraint), 323 (voluntarily causing hurt), 504 (intentional insult with intent to provoke breach of the peace), 506 (criminal intimidation), and 120-B (criminal conspiracy). Ali has been in jail for 3 years; shifted from Naini to Jhansi after cash was found Ali has been lodged in jail for 3 years. He surrendered in the Prayagraj court on July 30, 2022. Following this, he was sent to Naini Central Jail. On June 17, 2025, cash was recovered from his cell, after which he was shifted to a security cell. On October 1, 2025, he was transferred to Jhansi Jail.

stories.title: Mayawati targets Akhilesh:‘Lost trust in Muslim voters?’ PDA Rath turns saffron; claims Muslims joining BSP like Brahmins
stories.summary: BSP supremo Mayawati has lashed out at Akhilesh Yadav. She said, "The SP's PDA chariot appears more in the RSS-BJP's saffron colour than in red. Has Akhilesh lost faith in Muslims? Or is he changing colours like a chameleon for the sake of electoral interests." Mayawati wrote on X on Monday: "The Muslim community is now beginning to understand that it voted overwhelmingly for the SP in the previous elections. Despite this, BJP governments were formed in Uttar Pradesh and at the Centre. In such a situation, why should people waste their votes by voting for the SP repeatedly? This is why, like the Brahmin community, the Muslim community's inclination is also rapidly shifting towards the BSP." Mayawati's two major points 1- Had her photograph taken wearing a blue scarf; the public rejected it Mayawati said, "The Samajwadi Party should also tell the public what the real reality of its 'PDA' is. In its electoral interests, the SP has so far described 'PD' at times as 'Backward, Dalit' and at other times as 'Pandit'. At one point, it even had photographs taken wearing blue clothes associated with the BSP to project itself as Ambedkarite, but people immediately rejected it as 'fake Ambedkarite'." It may be noted that Akhilesh has so far held press conferences twice wearing blue scarves-once on 31 August and again on 17 September. Akhilesh had launched a new blue uniform for the student wing, 'SP Chhatra Sabha'. 2- BSP worked to control crime and promote development in Uttar Pradesh The former chief minister said, "The BSP controlled crime in Uttar Pradesh and improved law and order, while also undertaking work for public welfare, social welfare and development. The state needs this kind of governance for the welfare and development of all sections of society. The BSP is an Ambedkarite party that follows the policy of 'Sarvajan Hitay, Sarvajan Sukhay' (welfare and happiness for all). The party believes that everyone has the right to live with employment, dignity and self-respect. This is why the BSP has its own identity and respect among all sections of society." Akhilesh to launch PDA rath from Rae Bareli on 24 September Akhilesh Yadav will launch the PDA rath from Rae Bareli, Rahul's stronghold, on 24 September. This is the first time that the PDA rath will hit the road. The high-tech bus carries the words 'Samajwadi PDA Yatra'. It features pictures of several social reformers, including Dr Bhimrao Ambedkar. The slogans on it read: "Social justice will be championed, PDA will bring change." According to party sources, the rath will travel across the state during the 2027 election.

stories.title: Pakistan linked fake currency network exposed:Sting reveals deliveries across UP Assembly constituencies in ₹80 cr deal
stories.summary: The 2027 UP election is coming. Preparations have to begin now. We circulated ₹65 crore in the last election. This time, the target is ₹80 crore. Set up the leader. We have people in every district. Place the order and the money will be delivered to every Assembly constituency. For ₹1 crore, you will get ₹3 crore in counterfeit notes. The printing will be such that even banks will not detect them. These are claims made by a man identified as Ratul, who allegedly operates a counterfeit currency network from Guwahati. During an undercover investigation, a Dainik Bhaskar reporter posing as a buyer contacted Ratul and negotiated a purported ₹80-crore deal for counterfeit currency intended for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly election. The investigation team said it received information about a plan to move a large consignment of counterfeit currency into Uttar Pradesh before the election, allegedly through Bihar. Read and watch the full plan to circulate a consignment of counterfeit notes in the Uttar Pradesh election.. Investigation traces network from Nepal to Guwahati The investigation began after the team received information about a suspected counterfeit currency network. Its initial lead came from Inarwa in Nepal’s Parsa district, where the team learnt about an alleged female agent, Maya Paudel, involved in deals between Bihar and Uttar Pradesh. According to information obtained during the investigation, increased enforcement by the Nepalese authorities had allegedly forced parts of the counterfeit currency trade to shift from Nepal to Guwahati. The team subsequently identified Ratul as an alleged key figure in the network. An undercover conversation with him resulted in a purported deal worth ₹80 crore for counterfeit currency ahead of the Uttar Pradesh election. Reporter: “There is an election in UP in 2027. We need the material.” Ratul: “It will be available. Preparations for the election are already under way.” Reporter: “How will the material reach us in UP?” Ratul: “The first time, you will have to come to Guwahati, see the material and finalise the deal.” Reporter: “We will come.” Ratul: “How much are you planning to start with?” Reporter: “We are planning ₹3 crore. How much will we have to pay?” Ratul: “You will only have to pay ₹1 crore.” Reporter: “How long will it take to prepare ₹3 crore?” Ratul: “Once you place the order, the material will be ready.” Agent claims managers will be placed in every district During the conversation, Ratul allegedly said he would appoint his own managers in different locations before the counterfeit notes were delivered. According to him, the notes would reach these managers and would then have to be distributed by the buyer’s people. Ratul also claimed that the notes were sourced from China and that their colour would not fade for three years. Reporter: “We need the material in every district of UP for the election.” Ratul: “Do not worry. Everything will be arranged. I will appoint managers there.” Reporter: “Your material went to UP during the previous election, right?” Ratul: “Yes, it did. It will go this time as well.” Reporter: “You deliver my material to UP.” Ratul: “It will be done. My entire network will be put to work.” Reporter: “The material must be of good quality. It has to be distributed by a political leader, so there should be no complaints.” Ratul: “The material is top quality. The colour will not fade for three years.” Reporter: “Where does the material come from?” Ratul: “It is from China and Pakistan. It comes to India through Bangladesh.” Reporter: “Where is the currency chest? Will you deliver directly from there?” Ratul: “There is a chest in Guwahati. The material will go directly from there to UP.” Reporter: “What is the target for this UP election?” Ratul: “₹65 crore went last time. This time it could be around ₹80 crore.” Reporter: “There is a Yogi government in UP. Will that cause problems?” Ratul: “We have agents not only in UP and Bihar but also in Delhi, Rajasthan and Haryana.” Reporter: “Will your manager meet the political leader?” Ratul: “None of our people will appear in front of anyone. The delivery will be made to you.” Ratul claims large counterfeit deal took place during Bengal election Ratul also claimed that a large counterfeit currency deal took place during the West Bengal Assembly election. According to him, consignments had been delivered to different locations before polling. When asked whether the notes had been returned after being distributed, Ratul claimed that no complaints had been received from any election and that demand had already begun for the next election. He allegedly told the reporter to visit Guwahati, collect the notes and test them in the market or deposit them in a bank. He claimed that the deal could be cancelled if there was any problem. Ratul also allegedly said preparations for the UP election had to begin early because enforcement would become stricter closer to polling and the stock would therefore need to be arranged in advance. According to Ratul’s claims, his network had supplied a large quantity of counterfeit currency during the previous UP Assembly election. He claimed that around ₹70 crore had been sent and that there had been no complaints. Reporter reaches alleged counterfeit currency chest in Guwahati After the telephone conversation with Ratul, the Bhaskar reporter travelled to Guwahati posing as an agent to reach the alleged counterfeit currency chest. After the reporter contacted Ratul from Guwahati, Ratul gave the reporter’s number to an alleged associate named Rajiv. Around 90 minutes later, Rajiv called and asked the reporter to meet him near the Lokhra flyover. Following Ratul’s instructions, Rajiv allegedly took the reporter towards the purported counterfeit currency storage facility. Rajiv: “Is your money ready?” Reporter: “Yes. Have you prepared the money?” Rajiv: “We are getting a smaller bundle prepared for you from a large consignment that came from Bangladesh.” Reporter: “You get material from here every day. How much stock do you have today?” Rajiv: “Do not ask all that. Whatever the order, the material goes out.” Reporter: “There will not be any problem here, will we be safe?” Rajiv: “You are completely safe. The boss has everything arranged.” Reporter: “Can you introduce me to Ratul?” Rajiv: “The boss stays elsewhere. The deal will be done over the phone.” Reporter stopped outside alleged facility; video shown after phone call Rajiv first questioned the reporter in detail before speaking to Ratul on the phone. According to the investigation, Ratul knew that the purported buyer had come from Uttar Pradesh and was planning to distribute a large quantity of counterfeit currency during the election. Rajiv then took the reporter from the Lokhra flyover towards a hilly area. After travelling some distance, they reached a small market where most shops were closed. Rajiv took the reporter through a lane to an old two-storey building but stopped him outside, saying that some outsiders were present inside the office. He then made a phone call and obtained a video showing the alleged processing, packing and stock of counterfeit notes. Rajiv reportedly said that after the reporter had completed one or two transactions, he would be taken to the alleged printing unit. Video shows counterfeit notes packed like genuine currency The video shown to the reporter allegedly showed three to four people packing bundles of notes. A large carton appeared to contain counterfeit notes worth around ₹2 crore, according to the investigation team. The people involved were shown demonstrating the packing process and explaining how the counterfeit currency was allegedly being prepared to resemble genuine notes. Bundles of ₹500 notes shown in the video appeared similar to genuine currency. The bundles were carefully packed in plastic wrappers. Rajiv said the consignment was being prepared for delivery in Bihar. He claimed there was significant demand for counterfeit currency in Bihar and areas bordering Nepal, including outside election periods. Two types of counterfeit notes allegedly shown in Guwahati The reporter was allegedly shown two types of counterfeit notes at the purported currency chest in Guwahati. One type was described as black-coated, while another appeared to resemble genuine currency. Rajiv claimed the black-coated notes were coming from China and Pakistan and could evade scanning. He further claimed that the notes could remain usable for up to three years because of improved paper quality and printing. According to him, earlier consignments deteriorated within around six months, whereas the newer notes were allegedly made using thicker paper and better-quality printing. Alleged ₹80-crore deal negotiated from Guwahati After the reporter reached Guwahati, Rajiv provided further information about the alleged counterfeit currency operation and contacted Ratul to discuss the purported deal. Ratul allegedly said the operation was now being run from Guwahati because of the city’s proximity to Bangladesh. He claimed counterfeit currency from Pakistan and China was transported through Bangladesh before reaching India. According to Ratul, the operation had previously been based in Nepal, where networks in Uttar Pradesh and Bihar were active. He claimed increased enforcement after a change of government in Nepal had forced the operation to shift to Guwahati. He further claimed that Guwahati allowed consignments to be transported to different parts of India. Where does the alleged counterfeit currency go? The investigation raised further questions about the alleged network: where does the counterfeit currency from Guwahati go, which routes are allegedly used, and how are consignments transported to Bihar and Uttar Pradesh? The investigation also seeks to establish who allegedly receives the consignments further down the chain, whether the same network operates across multiple states, and whether the claims made during the undercover conversations correspond to an operational network on the ground. The next episode of the Bhaskar investigation will examine the alleged route from the Guwahati currency chest to Bihar and Uttar Pradesh, including the routes and network described by the people contacted during the investigation. Next episode: How is counterfeit currency allegedly being delivered across the country from the Guwahati chest? Read the route map and the next part of the investigation.

stories.title: Cyber fraud with AIIMS Patna founder director:Money deducted from account for 2 months; funds stolen without OTP sharing
stories.summary: A cyber fraud case involving the founder-director of AIIMS Patna has come to light in Lucknow's Mahanagar police station area. He is Dr Girish Kumar Singh, 72, currently an orthopaedics professor at Prasad Institute of Medical Sciences. Cyber fraudsters stole ₹3,22,408 from his bank account. Fraud took place between 3 July and 15 September In his complaint to the police, the victim, Dr Girish Kumar Singh, a resident of Eldico Emperor, Dr Baijnath Road, Nishatganj, said the money was withdrawn from his Indian Bank account through several separate transactions between 3 July and 15 September. The professor said he had not shared any OTP or confidential information with anyone. After learning that money had been debited from his bank account, he lodged a complaint on the NCRP (National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal) on 18 September. Police register case and begin investigation Based on the victim's complaint, a case has been registered under the relevant sections at Mahanagar police station in Lucknow. The police have assigned the investigation to Sub-Inspector Jai Karan Singh Bhadauria. The police are trying to trace the fraudsters through bank statements and the digital trail.

stories.title: Kisan Sangh launches outreach drive:Visits villages to spread word about September 23 programme
stories.summary: Public outreach was conducted in various villages of the Harhua block in Varanasi regarding the Bharatiya Kisan Sangh's proposed programme on 23 September at Shastri Ghat, Kachahari, located at the district headquarters. The workers visited Ramsinghpur, Singapore, Bazhiya, Mohanpur Luchchepur and Bishunpur villages, interacted with residents and informed them about the programme. They appealed to as many people as possible to participate in the programme. District president Sanjay Singh, district minister Vipul Singh, district publicity chief Jaishankar Singh, district executive member Rajesh Srivastava, Harhua block president Jyoti Patel, block executive members Piyush, Ashok Kumar and Kailash Master, along with prominent residents of the area, were present during the outreach campaign.

stories.title: Blood donation camp in Sharatpur:Over 37 people donated blood voluntarily; appeal to healthy people to donate
stories.summary: A blood donation camp was organised by Apna Charitable Blood Bank in Basharatpur, Gorakhpur, to mark Prime Minister Narendra Modi's 76th birthday. More than 37 people voluntarily donated blood at the camp. Blood donors, doctors, social workers, supporters and representatives of various social organisations contributed to the success of the camp. Donors encourage others to donate blood The donors said blood donation can play an important role in saving the lives of patients in need and urged every healthy person to come forward and donate blood from time to time. Apna Charitable Blood Bank thanked all the donors and supporters for their contribution. The organisation said helping people in need through blood donation is an important social responsibility. The blood bank appealed to healthy and eligible people to donate blood regularly and contribute to the cause of helping others.

Akhilesh to relaunch Mulayam's Kanya Vidya Dhan scheme:Says he will give Class 12-pass girls ₹50,000 and laptops if elected
stories.summary: Akhilesh Yadav is claiming that if the SP forms the government in UP, they may relaunch the 'Kanya Vidya Dhan Yojana'. Under this scheme, female students who have passed Class 12 will be awarded ₹50,000. Previously, ₹30,000 was provided under this initiative. Not only this, just ahead of the elections, he is bringing his former schemes back into mainstream discourse. Relying on initiatives such as unemployment allowances, Kanya Vidya Dhan, and the distribution of laptops to meritorious students, he is preparing to deliver another masterstroke. Announcements are being tailored with a special focus on Gen Z alongside UP’s more than 7 crore female voters. Kanya Vidya Dhan started by Mulayam, modernised by Akhilesh The Kanya Vidya Dhan scheme was launched during Mulayam Singh Yadav's tenure. Under this initiative, female students who passed Class 12 were provided financial assistance of ₹20,000 for higher education. After assuming power in March 2012, Akhilesh Yadav not only continued the scheme but also increased the amount to ₹30,000. These funds were transferred directly to the bank accounts of female students who passed Class 12 with good marks from the UP Board, CBSE, and ICSE. Now, once again, Akhilesh Yadav has promised to reactivate it. Should an SP government be formed, the amount will also be raised to ₹50,000. SP spokesperson Manoj Yadav says: In the SP government, poor women were provided a monthly pension of ₹500. Female students were given assistance of ₹30,000 under the Kanya Vidya Dhan scheme. Upon forming the SP government in 2027, new schemes will be introduced for women. Akhilesh is Also Mentioning These 5 Schemes Related to Women Stri Samman Samriddhi Yojana— In March 2026, Akhilesh Yadav stated that to empower economically vulnerable women, a pension of ₹40,000 will be provided every year. It will also include a provision for an annual increase. Analysts consider this a modern iteration of the 'Samajwadi Pension Yojana' implemented during the Akhilesh Yadav government (2012–17). In the previous scheme, eligible families were given ₹6,000 annually, with a rule providing for an increase of ₹50 each year. In the new 'Stri Samman Samriddhi Yojana', this budget and amount have been increased nearly sevenfold, which could prove to be a game-changer for women's empowerment. Distribution of Laptops, Mobiles, and Bicycles— Female students pursuing Class 12 and graduation will be provided laptops and smartphones to keep them technically updated. Free bicycles will be given to young girls commuting to school from far-flung rural areas. Special Leave for Women— He has also promised two days of special leave per month for women and female students in government and private offices as well as educational institutions. This has primarily been designed to provide relief to women during the difficult days of their menstrual cycle. No personal or unnecessary questions will be asked of women or female students when taking this leave. Neither a medical certificate nor lengthy paperwork and formalities will be required for this. Priority in Lohia Awas— Widowed and divorced destitute women will be allocated free Lohia housing on a priority basis. Similar to the Lohia Awas Yojana, beneficiaries will receive a 100% subsidy to construct houses. Women will not need to take out any bank loans or incur debts for this. The title deed for the house allocated under the scheme will mandatorily be registered in the woman's name. Closed Primary Schools Will Reopen— Akhilesh Yadav alleges that the present government has shut down over 26,000 schools serving Classes 1 to 8, citing 'mergers' or other policy changes. Upon the SP coming to power, all these closed schools will be reinstated immediately. All tuition and admission fees will be completely waived for all young girls studying in government primary and junior high schools. The SP claims that the closure of government schools has caused the greatest harm to children from poor, Dalit, Backward, and Minority families, as they cannot afford the fees of expensive private schools. For this purpose, the party has also run ground-level campaigns such as 'When Closed Schools Reopen, the PDA Will Study' and 'The School Calls Out'. How Much Alignment Exists Between Akhilesh’s Promises and the UP Budget During election season, the BJP questions these claims made by Akhilesh, as fulfilling these promises will require a massive budget. Senior political analyst Rajendra Kumar says: When the SP distributed laptops and Kanya Vidya Dhan in 2012, UP’s total budget used to be approximately ₹2.10 lakh crore. Today, the state government's annual budget has grown to over ₹7.36 lakh crore—meaning it is three times larger than during the SP government's tenure. A larger budget expands the government's scope to spend more on public welfare schemes. Why is the 'Female Electorate' the Biggest Factor in the 2027 Elections? Electoral dynamics in Uttar Pradesh are no longer confined merely to caste-based engineering. In the 2022 UP elections, women accounted for 46.38 per cent and men for 53.60 per cent of the cast votes. Meanwhile, in 2024, nearly 46.66 per cent of the voters were women. While the BJP considers its hold on female voters to be strong on the back of schemes like 'Lakhpati Didi', free rations, and the 'Ujjwala Yojana', Akhilesh Yadav is placing women in the foremost rank of his 'PDA' social engineering strategy. If the SP succeeds in conveying its promises to the public—providing a direct sum of ₹50,000 to female students passing Class 12, an annual pension of ₹40,000 to women, and loans of up to ₹2 lakh for women to start businesses—it could prove to be the biggest game-changer in the 2027 elections.

stories.title: Congress vows to bring OBC Act if elected:Says it will be like SC-ST Act; will SP back it in UP elections?
stories.summary: Congress is preparing to play the OBC card in the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly election. As part of this, the party is likely to include a promise to introduce an OBC Act in its election manifesto. If Congress comes to power, the Act could be made effective along the lines of the SC-ST Act. Dr Anil Jaihind, national chairman of the AICC OBC Department, said, “I spoke to Rahul Gandhi ji about this during the Bihar election. For some reason, it could not be included in the Sankalp Patra then. This time, Rahul Gandhi ji wants it to be included in the Sankalp Patra for the Uttar Pradesh Assembly election.” How much could the OBC Act benefit or hurt Congress? Will the Samajwadi Party also support it? How easy would it be to implement the OBC Act on the ground? Read this story... Why is there a demand for an OBC Act? Dr Anil Jaihind said the purpose of introducing the SC-ST Act was to prevent atrocities against Dalits and tribals and provide legal protection to these communities. He said several incidents of alleged harassment of OBCs, particularly Extremely Backward Classes, by upper-caste people had come to light in recent times. Similar incidents had also been reported in the past. In such a situation, there was a perceived need for an OBC Act to provide legal protection to backward and extremely backward communities. Congress explains importance of OBC Act through three incidents August 13: Saurabh Vishwakarma was beaten to death with sticks in Pratapgarh district. Saurabh Vishwakarma was a contractual employee in the Supply Department. He was allegedly killed over an old dispute. The accused belongs to the Brahmin community. Some accused have been arrested, while others are still absconding. August 25: Ramlagn Maurya was shot and killed and explosives were used against him in Ayodhya. His mother, Parvati Devi, was also injured and died a few days later. The incident took place over a road dispute. The accused belong to the Thakur community. Several accused are still absconding in the case. September 9: Vinod Kumar Sahani was killed in Gonda. He was a utensil trader. He was attacked with sticks while returning home and later died during treatment in Lucknow. The killing was allegedly carried out over social media posts. The accused belong to the Thakur community, with some still absconding. The Congress OBC Department is presenting these incidents as examples before the OBC community. It is being claimed that if an OBC Act had been in place, people from upper-caste communities would have thought twice before carrying out such killings. How much could the OBC Act benefit Congress? Senior journalist Anand Rai said the BJP has been electorally benefiting since 2014 by projecting Prime Minister Narendra Modi as an OBC leader. He said the BJP had continuously tried to appeal to every section of the OBC community. OBCs account for more than 50% of Uttar Pradesh's population. Congress is struggling to re-establish its political identity in the state. In such a situation, the party wants to attract this section by including an OBC Act in its election manifesto. Anand Rai said the BJP had gained electoral benefits after 2014 by consolidating OBC voters. At the national level, this could be Congress's agenda and its attempt to appeal to OBC voters. Could the Samajwadi Party also support the OBC Act? Senior journalist Anand Rai said a possible alliance between the two parties is considered likely. Congress has a national identity, while the Samajwadi Party is a regional party. He said the SP's base itself is among OBCs. The SP is promoting the PDA slogan, with 'P' referring to backward classes. However, it is not clear how much the SP would agree with Congress on the OBC Act. The SP may not want to invite the displeasure of upper-caste voters by supporting the Act. Would the OBC Act anger upper castes? Senior journalist Yogesh Mishra said BJP was regretting bringing the UGC Act. He said upper-caste voters had earlier been Congress supporters, while regional parties used to pursue OBC politics. As upper-caste voters moved away from Congress, its political strength declined. He said that, going by government data, more cases of conflict between OBCs and Dalits are currently being reported. “Even thinking about an OBC Act would be like political suicide for Congress. There is no need for it at present. Congress is only now trying to emerge again, and in such a situation, every single vote is important.” Senior journalist Anand Rai has a different argument. He said Congress itself had introduced the SC-ST Act. “Did other communities become angry because of it? No community becomes angry simply because a law is enacted. Every rule or law is brought with good intentions.” He said the real concern arises over the misuse of laws. “The upper-caste community became angry because of the misuse of the SC-ST Act. The outcome will depend on its proper use and misuse. And the community for which this Act is proposed will certainly be happy.” Would implementing an OBC Act be easy? Senior journalist Brijesh Shukla said, “The OBC Act can be included in the Sankalp Patra, but implementing it in reality will not be easy. What would be the basis of this act? At present, Dalits themselves are more troubled by backward and extremely backward communities. What would happen in such cases? If there is a dispute between a Dalit and an OBC, it would have to be made clear which act would apply. “There is no visible discrimination similar to untouchability among OBCs. What provisions would be included in the Act regarding this? Unless a formula is presented to people, they will not benefit from it. Congress has been out of power in the state since 1989. It has also been out of power at the Centre for the past 12 years. Its anxiety is therefore understandable.” The OBC Act being considered on the lines of the SC-ST Act needs to be understood in this context:

stories.title: Woman kills husband with boyfriend's help in Bareilly:Dumps body in gorge 4 km away; he had caught them in objectionable position
stories.summary: In Bareilly, a 38-year-old man was killed by his wife with the help of her boyfriend. The boyfriend used to visit the man's house when he was away. One day, the man saw him with his wife, after which the boyfriend fled. The husband had severely beaten his wife ever since. It was then that the wife decided to get rid of him. She got the opportunity on 10 September. She strangled her husband with a rope and killed him with the help of her boyfriend. The boyfriend then put the body in a sack, carried it 4 kilometres away on a motorcycle and dumped it in a ditch. The man's family learnt about their daughter-in-law's affair. They then filed a complaint with the police against her and her boyfriend. The truth came to light only after the police questioned the woman strictly on 17 September. The police arrested the woman and her boyfriend and recovered Pappu's body on Friday. The incident took place in the Bhuta police station area. Here is the full story in detail... They got married 4 years ago His brother Bundan said, "Pappu worked as a tailor. About four years ago, his family lived in Balia village in Budaun district. During that period, Raja alias Riyaz (35), a resident of Faiznagar, used to visit our home. Around the same time, he became friends with my sister-in-law, Nargis. The two began having an affair. After that, Raja often started visiting the house on one pretext or another." His closeness to his girlfriend increased further after leaving the village Meanwhile, around three years ago, Pappu sold his land in Budaun and had a house built in Faiznagar village in the Bhuta area. He then began living there with his wife, three sons and three daughters. After moving to Bhuta, Raja's meetings with his sister-in-law increased further. One day, the family saw Raja talking to his sister-in-law, Nargis. They told his brother Pappu about it. Pappu had gone out for work. When he returned, he too saw his wife with her boyfriend. A heated argument then broke out between Pappu and his wife. Pappu also beat her. Wife grabbed his feet, boyfriend strangled him with a rope According to the police, Pappu returned home from work on the night of 10 September. At the time, Nargis's boyfriend, Raja, was hiding inside the house. Nargis grabbed Pappu's feet, while Raja tightened a rope around his neck. He died on the spot. Raja then put the body in a sack, took it near the Mirzapur kiln and threw it into a ditch. Inspector Ravindra Kumar said that during police questioning, the accused, Raja, confessed to murdering Pappu over an affair. Pappu's body was recovered based on information provided by Raja. The wife and her boyfriend have been arrested in connection with the murder.

stories.title: Lucknow man dies by suicide on video call with girlfriend:He drank poison mixed in a soft drink, then shot himself in the temple
stories.summary: A young man in Lucknow died by suicide while speaking to his girlfriend on a video call. He rode his motorbike towards a forest, where he mixed poison into a soft drink and consumed it before shooting himself in the temple with a pistol. Blood was found at the scene, and the young man's motorbike was also found parked there. The incident took place in the Bijnor area on Friday afternoon. The deceased was identified as 25-year-old Karan Yadav, a resident of Raisingh Kheda. There was a gunshot wound to his temple, and foam was coming from his mouth. Police took him to hospital, where doctors declared him dead. See three pictures- He was a private car driver and left home at 9 a.m. Karan drove a private car for a person in Vrindavan Colony. At around 9 a.m., he left home on his motorcycle, saying he was going to work. At around 1 p.m., Karan was found unconscious in a forest near Jalim Kheda village. His motorcycle was parked by the roadside, while he was 100 metres inside the forest from the road. Foam was coming from his mouth, and blood was flowing from a gunshot wound to his left temple. A pistol was also found lying nearby. Police recovered an empty cold drink bottle, an empty water bottle, a disposable glass and two small open vials of medicine from the scene. Passersby saw body while travelling along edge of forest Passersby travelling towards the forest saw Karan lying unconscious and informed the police. The police reached the spot and immediately took Karan to Lokbandhu Hospital. However, doctors declared him dead as soon as he reached the hospital. Karan's family comprises his mother, Keshana, and his two elder brothers, Ranjeet and Sonu. According to the police, the pistol found at the scene was illegal. The investigation has revealed that the deceased was in a relationship with a young woman. Karan was speaking to the woman on a video call when the incident took place. He then consumed poison and shot himself in the temple with the pistol, committing suicide.

stories.title: Woman found with throat slit in Lucknow:Vegetable knife found 5 feet from body, another under pillow
stories.summary: A 70-year-old woman was murdered by having her throat slit inside her home in Banthra, Lucknow. She lived alone. A woman who arrived to deliver milk in the morning saw the body covered in blood. Both gates of the house were locked from the inside, while the door leading to the roof was found open. Police suspect that the killer may have escaped via the roof. Two knives were also found at the scene. A vegetable-cutting knife was found lying on the ground around 5 feet from the body. The second knife was found under the pillow on the deceased woman's cot. The forensic team collected evidence from the scene. DCP South Mohammad Mustaq said: All the household items were found in order. It appears that the house was entered through the roof and the crime was committed. A case has been registered against an unidentified person under the murder section. Four police teams have been formed to solve the case. It will be solved soon. See 3 pictures of the crime scene... About the woman Chhedana lived alone in Khurrampur village. Her husband, Shankarlal, died six years ago. She had two daughters, Ram Janki and Archana. Both are married. Ram Janki lives with her in-laws in Balaganj, while Archana lives with her in-laws in Thakurganj. Chhedana had two brothers-in-law. One, Amrit Lal, is retired from the RTO department, where he served as an enforcement constable, and lives with his family in Ashiyana. Her other brother-in-law, Nandkishore Gautam, is a deputy jailer in Jaunpur. His family lives near Sarosa-Bharosa in the Para police station area. Knife wounds inflicted along both cheeks and on the leg The deceased woman's throat had been slit. There were knife marks along the edges of both her cheeks. She had also been stabbed in the right leg below the knee, and there was a knife mark on her right palm. Her clothes were dishevelled as well. This suggests that she may have put up a strong struggle during the incident. Her elder daughter, Ram Janaki, said her mother used to wear a gold chain around her neck, earrings in her ears and anklets on her feet, but none of these were found on her body today. In the case, her brother-in-law Amritlal filed a complaint at Banthra police station, following which a case was registered against an unidentified person. Woman who arrived to deliver milk in the morning saw the body The incident took place in Khurrampur village under Banthra police station limits. At around 9:30 p.m. on Thursday, villagers saw Chedana outside her house. She then went inside. At around 7:30 a.m. on Friday, Asha, a woman from the village, went to deliver milk to her. The door did not open for a long time. Asha called out several times, but received no response. She then peered inside through the gate and saw Chedana's body lying in the veranda, covered in blood. As soon as they learned of this, people from the surrounding area reached the spot. Both main gates found locked from inside The deceased's house has two main gates. One of them always remains closed. The other gate was used to enter and leave the house. This gate, too, was found locked from inside. Meanwhile, the door leading to the staircase to the roof was open. For this reason, the police are also investigating the possibility that the killer escaped via the roof. Daughter says-Mother's jewellery missing The deceased woman's elder daughter, Ram Janki, said her mother wore a gold chain around her neck, earrings and anklets. When she reached home after learning about the incident, she did not see the jewellery on her mother's body. Her cheeks, neck, chest and other parts of her body had been slashed with a knife. Senior police officers also reached the scene after receiving the information. Police examined the crime scene. It is not yet known who killed her or why. Police are investigating the case. They looked over the back wall and found her dead on the cot Amritlal Gautam, the brother-in-law of the deceased, Chhedana, said, "I met my sister-in-law only yesterday evening before leaving. All the women were sitting at the door. This morning, when the door had remained unopened for a long time, people looked over the back wall. She was lying dead on the cot. Her neck and leg had been cut with a knife." Investigation into the murder is under way Deputy Commissioner of Police (South) Mohammad Mustaq said the circumstances surrounding the elderly woman's murder were being investigated. All the belongings in the house were found in order. At first glance, it is suspected that someone entered the house via the roof and committed the crime. The case will be solved soon.

stories.title: Youth protest UGC with 100 tractors:Police reach Agra with 4 hydras, 7 bulldozers; highway sit-in continues after scuffle
stories.summary: Around 1,200 young people took to the streets in Agra on Friday in protest against the UGC. Riding around 100 tractors, they set out from Sanwai village in Etmadpur for the district collectorate. However, around 200 metres from the village, police and the PAC stopped them by putting up barricades. The police arrived at the scene with four Hydra cranes and seven bulldozers. Two companies of the PAC and around 300 police personnel were deployed for security. The young protesters insisted on being allowed to go to the district collectorate. An argument broke out between the protesters and the police, following which pushing and shoving began. The police drove the protesters back towards the village. Both sides remained locked in a standoff until the afternoon. Around 3 p.m., the protesters removed the barricades and ran towards the Agra-Firozabad Highway. The police also chased them. The protesters then staged a sit-in on the highway and began reciting the Hanuman Chalisa. The protest led to long queues of vehicles on the highway. To bring the situation under control, the PAC has detained around 10 young protesters. Three pictures of the protest...

stories.title: Basic Education Minister Sandeep Singh’s wedding fixed:Tilak in Aligarh, wedding in Delhi; brother Saurabh to marry alongside
stories.summary: Sandeep Singh, a minister in the Uttar Pradesh government and the grandson of former Chief Minister Kalyan Singh, is set to get married. Sandeep and his younger brother Saurabh will have their tilak ceremony in Aligarh on 14 November. The two brothers will get married together in Delhi in the final week of November. Details of their future brides have not yet emerged. According to sources, Minister Sandeep's future bride belongs to a business family in Aligarh. The date and hotel for the wedding have not yet been disclosed. According to sources, the wedding may take place on one of 26, 27 or 28 November. There is also talk of a reception after the wedding. A separate feast may be organised in Lucknow. Cleaning begins at the family's Raj Palace residence According to Sandeep's father and former MP Rajveer Singh, a baby shower and tilak ceremony will be held in Aligarh. Preparations are being planned on a 100-bigha field along the Aligarh-Ramghat-Kalyan Marg. Cleaning, painting and whitewashing, as well as the installation of new stone, are also under way at the family's Raj Palace residence. Close relatives, supporters and acquaintances of the family from Aligarh, the Atrauli Assembly constituency and different parts of the state will attend the tilak ceremony. Preparations are under way to send invitations to workers and supporters at the booth level. There is also discussion of booking a wedding planner separately for the wedding. Work is under way on booking catering services and a German hanger. President and chief ministers of several states attended the sister's wedding eight years ago The Kalyan Singh family had previously hosted a major wedding ceremony in 2018. Kalyan Singh's granddaughter Purnima Singh married Praveen Raj Singh. Besides President Ram Nath Kovind, several state chief ministers and governors attended the ceremony. Get to know Saurabh Singh, the minister's younger brother Sandeep's younger brother, Saurabh Singh, remains active in the Atrauli Assembly constituency. When their father and elder brother are not present in the district, he represents the family at social and political events. Saurabh is also the young national president of the Akhil Bharatiya Lodhi Rajput Kalyan Mahasabha. His father, Rajveer Singh, is the organisation's patron.

stories.title: ‘If court sends me to jail, I won’t seek bail':Brij Bhushan says ready to go to jail for national interest; products banned in several countries
stories.summary: “Let the court punish me; let the court imprison me. I will not seek bail; I will go to jail for the sake of the country. At least this will spread awareness about adulterated food products in the country.” Former BJP MP from Kaiserganj in Gonda, Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh, said this while speaking to the media on Friday morning. He said that he had not done anything merely to remain in the news. He said, "In politics, publicity, pamphlets and expenditure are its characteristics." He has always remained in the news for one reason or another. He is now in the news over the issue of adulterated ghee. Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh said that reports of adulterated sweets, mawa, khoya, curd and oil being sold from villages to cities keep emerging. He said people should be made aware of such cases. He also said that if he went to jail, it was possible that awareness would be created among the public against those selling adulterated products. Brij Bhushan also made several claims about Patanjali products. He mentioned several products, including honey, ghee and medicines. Also spoke about his own ghee and Baba Ramdev's ghee Comparing the ghee produced at his facility with the ghee associated with Baba Ramdev, Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh said that ghee is not produced on a large scale at his facility. The ghee produced there previously cost around ₹2,000, and he has said that its price would be increased to more than ₹3,000. Baba Ramdev's company has filed a ₹50 crore defamation case against Brij Bhushan. The Madhya Pradesh High Court heard the case on Tuesday (15 September). Brij Bhushan's lawyer sought more time from the court to file a reply. The court has scheduled the next hearing for 18 September. The case relates to Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh calling Patanjali's products, particularly its desi ghee, counterfeit. In 2022, Brij Bhushan had also called Patanjali's ghee "counterfeit" at a public event and appealed to people to keep a cow or buffalo at home. At the time, his statement had also led to a dispute between Baba Ramdev and Brij Bhushan. Patanjali ghee has already been fined In 2025, the Food Safety Department fined Patanjali in Pithoragarh after its ghee was found not to meet the prescribed standards. In 2020, the department had collected a sample of Patanjali's ghee in Pithoragarh for testing. The sample failed the initial test. The company then sent the sample for retesting. However, the ghee was again found not to meet the prescribed standards in the second test. A case was subsequently filed in court. The court then imposed a fine of ₹1 lakh on Patanjali. The long-running feud between Baba Ramdev and Brij Bhushan The dispute between Baba Ramdev and Brij Bhushan is quite old. On 17 August last year, Brij Bhushan said in Balrampur, "Ramdev is one-eyed. The person whose name he is earning his livelihood in the name of-the history of Maharishi Patanjali also originates here in Gonda." However, he later apologised for the statement. Explaining it, Brij Bhushan said, "I made a statement during the Lok Sabha election. After that, Acharya Balkrishna Bhatt called me on the phone and called me a fool. We also responded in kind, and that is when our dispute began. In Balrampur, I was talking about the history of Gonda, Balrampur and the Devipatan division." “It was during this that Maharishi Patanjali was mentioned. I remembered that when Baba Ramdev had set out on his Swadeshi Yatra, he had mentioned the birthplace of Maharishi Patanjali in Gonda and promised to restore it. He had made this promise to the people. In that context, I was reminded of Baba Ramdev. A few words slipped out of my mouth. I later realised that I should not have said that.” This happened around eight months ago. After seeing the acne on a student's face, Brij Bhushan stopped him by holding his hand. He asked him why he had so many pimples on his face. "This is fake oil that is coming out, understand? This is the ghee from Ramdev," he said. As soon as people heard Brij Bhushan make this statement from the stage, they began laughing. Had earlier made a statement about fake ghee as well On 24 November 2022, while he was an MP, Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh said at a religious discourse tent in Barabanki, “If there is no disease in the body, there is no one richer than that person. A poor person's child is born weak. A healthy person's child is born healthy. To stay healthy, it is essential to maintain cleanliness at home and have milk and ghee. Milk is easily available in villages. I, too, used to go out grazing buffaloes. Only by rearing buffaloes and cows can one get pure milk and ghee. Otherwise, one has to eat Ramdev's fake ghee.”

stories.title: 25 years on, Konaseema Railway Line project yet to get on track
stories.summary: The ambitious 57-km Kotipalli–Narsapur railway line—which includes three bridges across the mighty Godavari River—still hangs fire 25 years after its foundation stone was laid. Locals rue successive governments’ silence on bringing a train to Konaseema, with many blaming lack of political will among the elected representatives from the Godavari region, despite severe losses to trade, commerce, tourism, and connectivity. stories.title: Minister Nishad asks who paid for Phoolan Devi’s killing:Called her an icon, warns against people who betrayed her
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh government minister Dr Sanjay Nishad said on Monday, "Be wary of those who orchestrated Phoolan Devi's murder. Phoolan Devi was an icon. When she became disillusioned with the Samajwadi Party (SP) and formed her own party, she was murdered to silence her voice." The Nishad Party president said: Why did the SP not demand an impartial investigation into her death? Were they afraid that the real faces would be exposed? The fishing community will not forget such political betrayals. It will hold them accountable for every betrayal. Her death should be investigated. It should also be established who paid for the contract killing. The minister appealed to the fishing community to remain alert ahead of the Assembly elections. He said, "The election season has begun. Those traders who did not come to share your joys and sorrows for four-and-a-half years have now started hopping around you like seasonal frogs under the pretext of panchayats, laying out their mats." The minister's reference was to Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav. Recently, Akhilesh had described himself as the true well-wisher of the Nishad community. He had said, "The Nishad community was given respect, recognition and rights under the Samajwadi Party government. It was the SP that secured Phoolan Devi's release and got her elected as an MP twice." Three major points made by Sanjay Nishad 1- Phoolan Devi is a symbol of rebellion and justice Minister Nishad said, "Phoolan Devi is a symbol of rebellion and justice. She is an inspiration for women. Every woman will have to become a Phoolan Devi. The earlier era was one of guns. Now it is the era of the button. She suffered a great deal of injustice." She had spoken to the then prime minister and sought security. She had said, "We are unsafe in Uttar Pradesh; we will live in another state. Give me a guarantee, and only then will I surrender; otherwise, I will deliver justice with my weapon." 2- Phoolan Devi joined the SP, but received death in return Sanjay Nishad said, "The Congress made a promise, but forgot it." Phoolan Devi then joined the SP. The SP made her a leader and an MP, but what did she get in return? Death. When Phoolan Devi became disillusioned with the SP, she formed the 'Eklavya Sena'. She later formed her own party. She was murdered 27 days later. When she became disillusioned, the reason for it should also be explained. An answer should also be given as to why there was a need to form another party. A Chaurasia linked to the SP has occupied Phoolan Devi's property. 3- These are seasonal leaders who only shed crocodile tears The minister said, "The Nishad community is now awake. It will no longer be misled by anyone. The entire fishing community-including Mallahs, Nishads, Kevats, Kashyaps, Binds, Dheewars, Kahars, Bathams, Rayakwars and Majhis-must be wary of such people. They are seasonal leaders. They shed crocodile tears, come to power by taking Nishad votes and then forget the fishing community. They give everything to their own people. The fishing community's independent political identity is now the Nishad Party. The fishing community is not one that rolls out carpets for others; it is a community that fights for the rights of the OBC community."

stories.title: Man shoots girlfriend’s brother, kills himself:Had eloped with girlfriend 4 days ago in Lakhimpur Kheri
stories.summary: In Lakhimpur Kheri, a lover shot his girlfriend's brother at around 7 a.m. on Friday. The bullet struck his abdomen. He then pressed a country-made pistol to his own temple and fired. The lover died on the spot after being shot in the head, while the girlfriend's brother is in critical condition. A doctor at the district hospital referred the injured man to Lucknow. The incident took place in Dulahi village, under the Padhua police station area, 47 km from the district headquarters. The deceased was identified as Idrish of Dulahi village, while the injured man was named Akhilesh. According to neighbours, Idrish and Akhilesh's sister had been having an affair for a long time. Four days earlier, on 14 September, Idrish and his girlfriend had left home and eloped. The girl's family had filed a case against Idrish, accusing him of abducting her with the intention of sexually exploiting her. Police found both of them on Thursday. Know the case chronologically A shooting took place in Dulhi village at around 7 a.m. on Friday. Idrish, 38, a village resident, shot Akhilesh, 33, who lived opposite his house. Idrish then placed a country-made pistol against his temple and shot himself. Idrish died on the spot from the gunshot wound, while Akhilesh was seriously injured after being shot in the abdomen. At around 7 a.m., Akhilesh was sitting outside his house, washing his face. During this time, Idrish also came out of his house. An exchange of abuse and an argument began between the two. They had been quarrelling over the same issue for the past four days. Their family members thought they were fighting with each other as usual, so they did not pay attention initially. After around half an hour of exchanging abuse and arguing, Idrish went inside his house and returned with a country-made pistol. He threatened to shoot Akhilesh. When the argument did not subside, Idrish opened fire at Akhilesh. The bullet hit Akhilesh in the abdomen. Hearing the sound of gunfire, members of both families and villagers reached the spot. People asked Idrish what he had done. During this, Idrish placed the country-made pistol against his temple and shot himself. The bullet passed through his temple, killing Idrish on the spot. He fell on the village road. The villagers informed the police about the incident. The police reached the spot and sent Idrish's body for a post-mortem examination. Akhilesh was taken to the district hospital for treatment. As his condition was serious, doctors referred him to Lucknow. His condition is still reported to be critical. Idrish and Akhilesh's houses face each other and are around 20 metres apart. Idrish accused of eloping with Akhilesh's sister A dispute over taking Akhilesh's younger sister away has emerged as the motive behind the shooting. According to police, Idrish had taken Akhilesh's sister with him around four days earlier. Akhilesh had filed a case against Idrish and his brothers in the matter. Police recovered the young woman. Tension had persisted between the two families since then. Idrish had married a year earlier Idrish (38) was the eldest of four brothers. His brothers Budha (32) and Hafiz (25) work as labourers in Delhi, while Munawwar (27) drives an auto-rickshaw in Delhi. Idrish had married in the Singahi area around a year earlier. His wife is pregnant and is living at her parental home. The family also has two sisters, both of whom are married. Had already served seven years in prison in a shooting case According to villagers, Idrish's name had surfaced in a shooting case around 15 years ago. At the time, he was accused of shooting two people. A case was registered against him under Section 307, and he was sentenced to seven years in prison. Idrish completed his sentence and was released from prison about a year ago. Akhilesh is a sanitation worker at the Nagar Panchayat Akhilesh has two brothers, Rahul and Chhotu. His mother's name is Aarti. The family has four sisters, one of whom is married. Akhilesh and his brother Rahul work as sanitation workers at Nighasan Nagar Panchayat. SP Dr Khyati Garg said: A dispute reportedly broke out between the two sides over taking the young woman with them. One person died in the incident, while another was injured. Evidence has been collected from the scene. The cause of the incident is being investigated.

stories.title: Ram Mandir priests can keep beard, moustache and hair:Stay clean-shaven or purification for rule violation; new guidelines explained
stories.summary: New guidelines have been issued for the priests of the Ram Mandir in Ayodhya. They state that the priests must either keep their hair, beards, moustaches, and ‘shikhas’ or remain completely clean-shaven. Applying a tilak will also be mandatory. They will have to wear yellow clothes every day. They will not be allowed to enter the temple without bathing after using the toilet. If the rules are violated, purification will be carried out with cow's milk, ghee, and curd. Swami Rajkumar Das, a member of the Ram Mandir Religious Committee and head of Shriramvallabhakunj, shared details of the new guidelines with Dainik Bhaskar. He said, The Ram Mandir Trust's Religious Committee held a meeting on 12 September. The guidelines were issued with everyone's consent. The priests have been informed about them. Everyone has been asked to follow the rules. Priests will not be allowed to take mobile phones into the sanctum sanctorum According to the guidelines, priests will not be allowed to take mobile phones into the sanctum sanctorum. They will have to avoid making statements about the temple on social media. They must not post anything on WhatsApp or other social media platforms that could send a wrong message to people about the Ram Mandir. They will have to behave courteously with devotees. Priests will have to avoid joking and casual banter During their duties, priests will have to remain at their designated positions. If they need to leave their position for an important task, they will first have to inform the shift in-charge of the reason. They may leave their duty station only after that. They will have to avoid unnecessary conversation, group discussions and joking. They will have to remain calm and try to handle any incident. If necessary, they will have to seek assistance and guidance from those responsible. They must not engage in unnecessary conversation with devotees, as this could create a wrong impression of the priests or the Ram Mandir in their minds. Inform Acharya Ji if there is any problem Apart from the offerings and prasad provided by the temple, no outside items may be taken into the sanctum sanctorum. Priests must refrain from making unnecessary comments or asserting their authority. In case of any problem or dissatisfaction, they must inform Acharya Ji and seek his guidance. When family members or close friends visit, Acharya Ji will assist them with darshan, prasad and other arrangements, or these will be carried out as per his instructions. If any priest provides such special assistance or treatment to another person, the priest concerned will be held responsible. The utensils (made of gold, silver and other metals) must be counted before being handed over to the attendants and again after cleaning.

stories.title: Long queues for iPhone 18 in Noida, crowds at mall:Buyer from Punjab waited since morning, bought 2 Pro Max phones
stories.summary: Sales of Apple's new iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max began in India today. A crowd of buyers started gathering from 6 am at the only Apple store in Uttar Pradesh, located in Noida. By 7 am, a long queue had formed. People from border states such as Punjab, Haryana and Uttarakhand are reaching Noida to buy the new iPhone. As it was the first day of the launch, the Apple retail store at DLF Mall in Sector 18 was opened ahead of its scheduled time, at 8 am. As soon as the store opened, employees welcomed customers with applause. People were allowed to enter one by one. Those who emerged carrying iPhones were seen dancing and singing. The first young man to come out with an iPhone said, "I have come from Punjab. Sales of the new phone have not started there yet, so I first went to Delhi. There was a very large crowd at the store there, so I took a cab and came straight to Noida. I reached here at 6 am and was the first person in the queue. I bought two iPhone 18 Pro Max phones." India has a total of six official Apple retail stores-two in Mumbai and one each in Delhi, Noida, Bengaluru and Pune. The new iPhone is currently available for sale only at these six stores. In view of the crowds, the company has decided to keep the stores open until 10 p.m. See four pictures... Price starts at ₹1.64 lakh The iPhone 18 Pro is priced from ₹1,64,900, while the iPhone 18 Pro Max starts at ₹1,79,900. Both models are available in different storage variants. The new iPhone 18 Pro series has been launched in four colours: Black, Silver, Glacier and Burgundy. iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max have the largest batteries ever Apple also launched the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max on 9 September, along with its first foldable phone. These are the first premium iPhones to feature three 48-megapixel cameras: a main camera, a telephoto camera and an ultra-wide camera. Apple claimed that the iPhone 18 Pro would last for 24 hours and the Pro Max for 30 hours on a single charge. This is the longest battery life ever offered. The phones can be charged to 50% in just 15 minutes.

stories.title: ‘Where should a judge go if he faces injustice?’:Judge who awarded 23 death sentences in UP speaks out; once said, ‘I’d rather die than fear’
stories.summary: A judge's job is to deliver justice, but where is he to go if he himself is subjected to injustice? Is a judge working under the administrative control of a district judge also obliged to comply with orders that are contrary to the law? Muzaffarnagar judge Ravi Kumar Diwakar made this observation on Thursday (17 September) while delivering his verdict in a 10-year-old case under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act. He acquitted the accused, who had been making rounds of the court for a long time. During the hearing, the judge expressed displeasure over the decision of the then district judge to withdraw 97 cases from his court and transfer them to other courts. In his verdict, Judge Ravi Kumar Diwakar wrote: No one in India is above the law. The country will be governed by the Constitution and the rule of law, not by the arbitrary conduct of any public servant. No public servant can behave like a king. They must provide the legal reason for every administrative order they issue. This raises the question: was the then district judge's decision to recall the cases on 18 August, without stating any reason, just 13 days before his retirement, justified? Ten days earlier, on 7 September, Judge Ravi Kumar Diwakar wrote in his verdict sentencing the accused in the Shahpur Shahjadi murder case to death, "I would prefer to die rather than be called a cowardly judge. As long as I can follow my principles, I will continue in service; otherwise, I will resign." In fact, during his 17-year judicial career, Judge Ravi Kumar Diwakar has sentenced 36 convicts to death. During his five-month tenure in Muzaffarnagar alone, he sentenced 23 convicts to death. Find out which case the verdict concerns Now read what the judge wrote in the verdict: Took charge on 29 November 2025 Judge Ravi Kumar Diwakar took charge at the Additional District and Sessions Court, Fast Track Court-3, in Muzaffarnagar on 29 November 2025. He began his judicial service in 2009 and was posted in Sambhal and Bareilly before Muzaffarnagar. He has also been in the news over the verdict he delivered in the Gyanvapi case. He has written to police and administrative officials several times, saying that he faces a threat.
